Probably one of my favourite games of all time. It was a little rough after launch with performance, ai issues and bugs, but most problems have been handled and the game is pretty smooth except for a few janky moments when interactions like sandbags, repairing, grenades and that get interrupted or happen on jagged terrain.

This game is by far the best ww2 rts game, its realistic but not too realistic that your tanks can't see anything and get shot from 3km away. Infantry health is just right (and if not for you just get one of the many mods) where good infantry feel incredibly useful and direct controlling makes you feel like a hero of the soviet union, but not a superhero.

Tank combat is incredibly well done, the focus on early barb makes for interesting tank fights that are forgotten in other ww2 games where it usually just pz4, panther and tiger vs t34/85 and IS2. You always have a tool up your belt to deal with big threats, whether its a crazy blitz trying to rear pen the KV1, calling in bombs on IS2s, using your arty direct fire or charging hordes of infantry just to get one satchel thrown.

The campaign missions are pretty good, some are better than others, and some needing just a few changes to be great. Only critique I would give is to make a tool that enables building defenses and placing mines on click to speed up the setup phase rather than 30 min of selecting a guy to go pickup mine then set him to place it. The creativity that you come up with when having to deal with large threats when you only have limited AT is very fun. I remember how satisfying it was to verse a column of pz1 and 2s and a bison with only a PTRD and hitting the ammo detonate.

The skirmish modes (ones where you push to take the 7 points and unlock units) can get a little formulaic, but are always good fun, and some of them on hardcore get incredibly hectic like the battle of Berlin.

The faction balance is reasonable, Soviets are pretty strong but have weakpoints that are covered with other units, but Germans have weakpoints but are a little more versatile. For example, German rifle squads with an mg42 beat the early Soviet rifles that only have Mosins and a DP, but once Soviets start getting more SVT and especially PPSh then they dominate the short and mid range, but Germans always do well at long range using the double mg42 squads. In late war the German infantry using Sturmgewehr are incredibly versatile and strong with strong AT, only outmatched by Sturmoviki and Osnaz. Finnish as expected aren't a superpower, but with lots of PzShrecks they can sorta hold out, they use a lot of funky artillery and aa guns that do quite well against weak armour. Strangely though the WW1 Finnish arty has better accuracy and rof than Soviet arty, but i suspect that is intentional to give them something good.

Only some units stand out as a little too good that might need some kind of nerf. All short barrel 150mm weapons IG33, KV2 and that feel a little too good at killing heavy armour, maybe just a little nerf. The Ig15 is ridiculously good with exellent heat, too accurate and fast rof HE and the best possible arc to shoot from behind terrain.

Soviets and Germans have matchups that reflect history; at the start of barb the early KV1 and T34 are incredibly fearsome tanks to try and beat with at best PzIII L and Pz4 F1, it's only when you get the Pak40 do you start to stand a chance. You react and get the Tiger (rushing the tiger or any heavy AT as germans is essential in conquest) and it does well, but still as happened in my game got blown up by KV2, hit with Br-2, katyusha'd and IL2'd. You never feel completely safe, and the strong yet balanced and reasonable accessible artilleries provide an excellent counter to the typical meta in WW2 RTS of just getting the heaviest tank.

Direct controlling is in its best form here, better than all other Men of Wars, on launch it used to be such a big buff that you pretty much had to, to now being just enough to be fun but not necessary to win. It's nice to have total control of a unit and not lose a game to unit ai problems as happens in many rts games. It enables very creative plays and really makes you use all the small stats like turret traverse, turret rotation speed, rear armour, reverse and acceleration, turning circle, even the rear mg on the KV1, no other rts makes those things matter as much.

Most RTS (like Steel Divison) have few maps that get repetitive and kill replayability, the large number of different maps, attack angles and point locations give a lot of variety in attacking distances and defensive style. I hope they keep up the regular addition of maps and even support some of the modders that are adding maps. And please allow some of the great maps in campaign and conquest to be in multiplayer. 

Tavisota should be able to be disabled in conquest, as it was often just kind of annoying fighting finnish, as they aren't much of a threat to a well put together force, just slow to clear out. Tavisota has some fun campaign missions and are an ok addition to conquest, and being only a bit of a meme in multiplayer. Get this if you have already played all the content in the base game.

Scorched earth only adds a few units, but some that should have been in the base game. There needs to be more SPAA to help with anti-infantry, as well as more shredder crew weapons. The flakvierlung dominated MOWAS2 but it should be in the game maybe at a decently high cost or available with doctrine. Only adding the werbelwind leaves soviets with only the T60 as a dedicated anti-infantry light tank. There are some cool things here, just none that change things up and these should have been in the base game.

The devs are doing well, just wish they would handle and improve grenade ai, remove a bit of jank with crewed weapons, make repairing better (I don't want to have to click repair 5 times and have the guy get out and in 5 times before he decides to repair the tread), fix some issues of multiplayer desyncing with some hits not counting and tanks being killed by an ally but still showing as an enemy for you. Improving the offensive ai in conquest is something that is steadily happening, but still the drive the weak tanks down the road to get one shotted each time then charge infantry into 4 mgs is a little unimmersive. Some ui changes that make hotkeys more better (they often get removed if you decided to manually change them) but also able to tell me at a glance ammo level of main gun and who in the squad has which grenade. More bunkers, units, maps, all would be great.

If you want a fun and challenging game that allows you to play in all 3 gaming perspectives (1st, 3rd, eagle eye) then this is the game for you. I love this game, time era for war and the devs attention to detail and historical accuracy with this game. I will play this game continuously and I very much enjoy the Conquest aspect that allows you to play constantly and prove or disprove strategies in both attacking and defense!

[h3]My thoughts:[/h3]
[i]Gates of Hell[/i] is the best iteration of the RTS genre to date. Set during World War 2, the game feels like an authentic combat experience. No other RTS has come close to reproducing the excitement, let downs, and random cinematic moments that occur during battle.

[h3]What I like:[/h3]
[*][u][b]Asymmetrical Warfare.[/b][/u] 
There is no rock-paper-scissors balancing here. Your infantry are going to get shredded by MGs and field guns without proper armor support. GOH gets compared to [i]Company of Heroes[/i] a lot but it plays so differently it feels like it might as well be in a separate genre.[*][u][b]Combined Arms.[/b][/u]
That feeling of pushing an objective with infantry, armor, and indirect fire support in a tandem effort is unmatched. 
[*][u][b]Direct control.[/b][/u] 
Being able to take control of the tanks in real time with WASD and using your mouse to aim the turret never gets old. Every station (Commander, Gunner, MG Gunner, etc) is available to use. So if you want to use the radio operators MG while the turret reloads go ahead! You can even have the commander open the hatch to use the cupola MG.
[*][u][b]Inventory system.[/b][/u] 
All units in the game can share items, ammo, and other things which adds to immersion. I love being able to see the physical differences between the cannon ammo types (AP, HE, WP, etc)
[*][u][b]Logistics are acknowledged.[/b][/u] 
I love that you can use trucks to tow artillery, field guns, and auto-cannons around. There are specific trucks for ammo, fuel, and supply to keep your army functioning. You can repair your own equipment as well as steal enemy equipment and repair them too. It's so nice to see that this "unsexy" side of war is addressed.
[*][u][b]Several game modes.[/b][/u] 
Story missions are my favorite with the dynamic campaign a close second, both of which can be played in COOP with 4-8 people. The two skirmish modes are fun as comp stomps as well.
[*][u][b]Tons of maps.[/b][/u] 
Crazy detailed environment. So much work went into filling the maps with detritus and articles of war strewn about. They really feel lived in. Some of the missions are made using aerial reconnaissance from the war. There are probably 100 different maps with all the DLC included.
[*][u][b]Amazing graphics and effects.[/b][/u] 
I still remember the first time I saw  a tank cook off. Then when I realized it wasn't just a canned effect it just blew my mind. There is a penetration system regarding armor in this game. Know where the ammo storage is on a certain tank? If you pen it there you'll get a devastating ammo rack that obliterates the tank
[*][u][b]Immersive sound design.[/b][/u] 
The sound from units and effects like gunshots morph depending on how far the game camera is to the source. There are even separate sound effects when you are in third/first person view. There are different sounds for shell ricochets and penetration which are very satisfying to hear. I particularly like the sound of the Tiger's main cannon.
[/list]
[h3] What I dislike: [/h3] 
[*][u][b]So much jank.[/b][/u] 
Issues with unit pathing, AI, and bugs. The more you play the less it affects you but this is a real problem that turns new players away.
[*][u][b]Performance issues.[/b][/u] 
Even with a 13th Gen i7 and RTX 4080, at 3440x1440 resolution the frame rates can dip into the 60s and lower under certain circumstances. Mostly it plays smoothly. Crashing doesn't happen that often but can be frustrating when it does.[/list] 
[h3] Wishlist: [/h3] 
[*][u][b]Join in progress.[/b][/u] 
It would be really nice to have a drop in and drop out system for friends. Currently you have to start a mission over if a friend disconnects for connectivity reasons. Sometimes you have to decide whether to end a game early or finish the mission while your buddy waits because of this issue.
[*][u][b]Ability to save progress in COOP mode.[/b][/u] 
This would also more or less solve the previous problem.
[*][u][b]Assign units to the player that bought them.[/b][/u] 
Currently in COOP Story missions the game will randomly assign units to all players regardless of who purchased them. This leads to micro-management of giving the units to the player that wanted them in the first place, which disrupts the flow of the other players.
[*][u][b]More Logistics.[/b][/u] 
I would love to see a system where a recovery vehicle could tow tank hulls off the battlefield for repairs in safer locations. An engineer could build a vehicle field repair structure that would serve as faster means to repairs and additionally to resupply of repair kits for vehicles.
[*][u][b]More air support.[/b][/u] 
Currently there are a couple of off-map air call-ins that you can do. I'd love to see some way to include how the air war impacted the battles. Some ability to drop paratroopers would be awesome.
[*][u][b]More theaters of World War 2.[/b][/u] 
I'd love to see North Africa, Pacific, Italy, etc.

An offer you can't refuse: Get ready for the ultimate WW2 tactical simulation.

Although it's not quite a complete masterpiece, it's the closest thing I've found to one for this genre. The developers are dedicated to updating this game and it's exciting to think of the untapped potential waiting to be unleashed.

The gameplay mechanics are gripping! You really feel like you're commanding your digital army to victory, or being pushed back into defeat. You can switch to directly controlling individual units through third person or first person view which, while remaining a somewhat clumsy feature, can be a very satisfying experience and can be used for a tactical edge. There are many units available to you and they follow closely to historical lines. It's up to you to put them to their best use. 

Graphics-wise, it's a real treat for the eyes. The visuals are so stunning, I sometimes wish I had a better computer to truly savor them. 

The user interface and controls are pretty seamless, though there are moments when I wish there were additional ways of actually being in control. A good addition to this game was how you are able to select a squad of perhaps 12 units and spread them out across cover over a large area just by clicking and dragging. These sorts of features are extremely useful and could use more expansion. Something I'd like to see is a control that tells units to "stay-in-cover" so that it's not a constant micromanagement. It can be be frustrating. The game flow can easily get overwhelming, as if I need to be everywhere and controlling everything all at once with limited capabilities.

I appreciated the story missions since they draw you right into the WW2 atmosphere and get your feet wet. There are many missions that I have yet to try out. However, this game really shines with the multiplayer.

One thing I've noticed is the wide skill gap between players. You'll need practice and determination to master the game and stay fierce on the battlefield. The good news? Victory is very satisfying. The experience will keep you hooked for hours on end. I lost count of my multiplayer matches. You can use each one honing your strategic prowess and unveiling new aspects of your personal warfare style.

If you're looking for an engaging WW2 tactical simulation that'll keep you hooked for hours, press the buy button. Trust me, you won't regret it.

In an age when the WW2 game market is saturated with nonsense games with titles like Hitler's BDSM bunker, making a mockery of the scale and importance of this dramatic human event, then you have games like CTA:GOH that respect their source material, while having enjoyable gameplay. In my opinion this is the best WW2 rts game out right now, and certainly the one most worthy of praise to be released in recent memory. My review will be from the perspective of someone who is casual and does not play competitively. I play strictly against AI opponents, so keep that in mind.

One of my favorite things about this game is the heightened realism when you compare it with other WW2 rts games. This isn't the gimmicky, arcadey gameplay of Company of Heroes or even Steel Division. There is no base-building and are no bullet sponge soldiers here. The combat is more visceral, things feel like they have more 'weight' behind them, and the scenery is nicer to look at. Many parts of the environment can be destroyed and knocked over, such as trees and buildings. The wreckage, death and destruction lend themselves to the feeling that an actual battle took place. I feel like this can still be improved further, though. I would love to see fires lasting longer, and more instances of buildings, debris and soldiers catching on fire, as well as charred remains and so on. This is there to some degree, but I hope they'll build on it further.

The micromanaging aspect of the game may scare some players, but it isn't as bad as you might think. The difficulty parameters can be changed to give you more or less of a challenge, and when you're playing against AI you usually don't need to play optimally anyway. A good idea to get acquainted with the game a bit is to fire up a skirmish match with an AI and yourself against another AI. Your AI ally can keep the enemy busy while you practice, test out equipment, and so on. The AI itself can cheat, as well as do dumb things at times, but it isn't a huge issue, and the developers continue to improve upon them in subsequent updates. As far as mircomanaging, you can control a individual soldier, or group of soldiers at once. You can toggle first person or third person mode while controlling a soldier. Controlling everything at once isn't completely necessary, you can get your guys into strategic positions and start advancing slowly, or you can be more aggressive and micro-heavy. I prefer the more methodical, casual approach. I mention this mainly so people know that you don't have to be super competitive to play the game. Currently the game has the Soviet Union, Germany and (with DLC) Finland as playable nations. The DLCs are recommended, albeit overpriced in my opinion. 

Let me talk about some suggestions for future updates/DLCs that I think would improve the game. Some of this stuff has been implemented to some extent, but could be increased a great deal. A proper dlc focused strictly on Operation Barbarossa. A lot would need to be done to do proper justice to this largest invasion in history. It would need to include Axis soldiers from not only Germany, but their puppets and satellites that took part in the invasion, namely: Finland, Romania, Italy, Croatia, Slovakia, and Hungary. A way of doing this without making all of those countries as separate factions (which obviously would take A LOT of work) would be to give them as auxillary and complementary troops within the greater German roster. The variety of units, the massive amount of troops involved, and the speed and encircling maneuvers could make this very interesting gameplay. The 1939 invasion of Poland is another frontrunner for new content that could be added. These are all just ideas, but I can't wait to see what comes next with this game.

The game already has quite a few mods and there seem to be more noteworthy ones arriving each week. Mods are highly recommended. Not only can they change up aspects of the game that you might find need tweaking, some also change the game completely, such as the Vietnam mod or the Russian Civil War mod. Take a look at the workshop and see what interests you.

And there you go, my jumbled thoughts about Call to Arms - Gates of Hell Ostfront! It's already a great game, one that can be and still does get improved and updated. In an era where most WW2 games are oversaturated, weird, and lackluster I can easily recommend Gates of Hell to those interested in a rts game with a WW2 setting.

This game is yet another (how many do we have now... six?) version of the good old soldiers game, way back from 2004. Instead of making a new and more optimised engine, the devs have decided to make yet another, more polished clone of the same thing. 
The game has its unique way of managing battlefield and way more indepth feel of everything going around (explosions, sound effects, the sheer variety of units and weapons beat any wannabe WW2 game like CoH...). Unfortunately... it's nothing new and while being a lot more enjoyable, the engine always came with its quirks and troubles.

So here's a list of my overall gripes that eventually made me not recommend this game (and probably give up on it until devs decide to fix the underlying issues):

- First up is the abyssmal AI that controls all the units on the battlefield. Units are sometimes endlessly stupid and can't execute the most simple of commands without dying in some stupid way. Direct control is the only redeeming factor (which to dev's credit has been improved)

- Campaigns are okay and they can provide all the enjoyment for a bogstandard single player fans. I wouldn't recommend trying to come close to any of the multiplayer modes though (including any of the co-op modes).

- And this is the main reason why i stopped playing - multiplayer has been totally ruined by making the netcode unstable to the point of being literally unplayable. Units are rubberbanding and teleporting through the ENTIRE MAP. FPS randomly drops every second and is super inconsistent (so you can dream of having any direct control). I feel like i don't have any control over the battlefield because i'm constantly seeing teleporting and glitching units so i don't really see any point in actually trying to play. 

- And for the love of god... The UI in any of the coop modes should be separate for every player... This is something that has been persistent since MoW:AS and is annoying like hell. Having your interface tab change randomly right when you click to call some unit because your ally decided he want to call something else... it is just infuriating.

To sum up, game has great potential but devs prefer to release more and more releases, piling up more errors on top of this huge existing mound of problems, insead of fixing their releases. I'm going to wait until they finally decide to fix their stuff and i recommend that to everyone else.

After 1276 hours in GoH, I feel it's time to leave an honest and unbiased review. (maybe)

Gates of Hell is a RTS game set in World War 2 released in 2021, it has seen 3 DLC's, 5 Content Updates and 3 Community Updates with many smaller updates so far.

GoH for an RTS is pretty demanding specs. wise. The graphics though pretty to the eye are demanding and performance heavy at times.
The games sound design is second to none, in the RTS genre GoH has probably the best sound design I've ever seen.

Together with the great graphics and sound design are: Vehicle and Infantry models, and they look incredible.
The vehicles (especially the newer ones) come in a stunning amount of detail and historical accuracy, some of the older vehicles have sadly fallen behind graphics wise, they are simply outdated compared to the newer ones.


To go with the amazing models the game features an Amazing damage model for Vehicles. Instead of a plain healthbar, the game models multiple componets of vehicles with various stages of damage:
- Guns can be broken
- Tracks destroyed
- Ammuniton cooked off
- And Additional armor such as skirts and track shot right off

This means tank engaments aren't just waiting to see which one will die faster. Smart shot placement and positioning play a huge role in your vehicles success. 
Different ammuniton types are modelled ranging from AP to APCR and HEAT, Smoke rounds and HE. (with many more variants of shells) the performance of rounds is as real as possible.

The games weapon ranges (for vehicles) are scaled down to an X % of their real life counterpart, meaning for example 200 meters in game = 2k irl (not accurate, just an example) 



The game has many ways to control your units, most interestingly the First Person control mode which allows you to control units more akeen to a FPS game. 

Just a few days ago as of writing this (09.05.2024) GoH has released the German Infantry Overhual, the uniforms quality is the best on the market right now together with the huge amount of historical accuracy. Though accurate and beatiful the uniforms have some hiccups texture wise, not many but definetly noticeable by history nerds.
The Devs have said that Overhuals for Infantry will come to the other Factions too, that being: Finland and the USSR.



The Campaigns:
The base game is set in the "Ostfront" in other words the Eastern Front.
Included are 2 nations: Germany and Soviet Russia with their historic equipment and campaigns.

The game has recently received a completely new tutorial which is very informative and fun to play, teaching new players how to do almost everything.

The German campaign nicknamed "Ostfront" features 6 missions out of the box, those being:
- The Big Prize
- Back to Square one
- Among the Heavens
- Legend of Krasny Bor
- Ace of Swords
- In Spite of Everything

These missions are based on real locations which are faithfuly represented. 
The historical accuracy in these missions is to say the least a bit everywhere, though not completely made up, they sometimes simply just feel wrong.

The Soviet campaign nicknamed "Za Rodinu" also has 6 missions out of the box:
- Absolute Zero
- The Cold Supper
- Operation Bustard Hunt
- Unbroken
- Winter Storm
- Closing the Pocket

Same things can be said about these missions as was said in the German ones.

Also featured in the base game is the Conquest single or coop gamemode.
This gamemode offers the player the ability to research units via a progression system, and create their own Army.
Conquest revolves around researching units with points gained after each battle, these battles are divided into Attacking and Defending objectives on different maps, on the bigger "World" map. The goal, is to reach the enemy HQ. 
Many settings can be customized to the players liking including the length and strength of enemies forces.

This gamemode though great in theory, hasn't received much love from the Developers in a few years.
It is still a good choice for new players to learn and enjoy the game.



The Multiplayer:
Some would say, the main part of the game, Some say it's simply a sweat fest.

The gameplay in MP, is fine. The balancing isn't perfect in many departments, but it gets the job done if you want to play casually.
The biggest issue in MP, is sadly the performance, this mode suffers the most from bad performance and desync. 

It features 3 gamemodes: Battle Zones, Domination and the new Last Stand

Unlike previous games in the "series" GoH features a Doctrine system, Doctrines influence your Special Units and the Infantry units during the game.

I'm not the biggest fan of the mode, but if you like medium paced action and micromanaging.


That would be all for the Base game, it features hundreds of vehicles and equipment, lots of maps and many other interesting things.




The First expansion for the game was "Talvisota" this DLC brought the Finnish faction with it's own campaign ad equipment.
This DLC also introduced the Skirmishes, these smaller missions with objectives placed around the map to capture, capturing these unlocks new units for the player to use. These are also playbale in coop with friends.

Tons of problems that they refuse to change because of design intent. Devs are completely closed to feedback and argue in the forums and even result to childish name calling and gaslighting when confronted with legitimate feedback. Basic things are missing like machine guns shooting through fences, AP rounds through walls, all buildings being destructible (including single-story barns that should be destructible).

[h1] Inventory [/h1]
The inventory system is absolutely awful to deal with in an RTS, but putting up with it can give your infantry huge advantages (for example picking up a rocket launcher or replenishing grenades without spending resources). You would think they would implement a "scavenge" button or something, so you don't have to click on each dude and tell him to loot a specific dead guy, wait for him to run over to him, then manually take the grenades. But nope. No scavenge button, no resupply button. It makes dealing with the inventory a single-unit-at-a-time ordeal and not worth it.

[h1] Direct Control [/h1]
Direct control should be a selling point but is an absolute mess. Jiggle peaking and MG suicide bum-rushing are way too effective.

Direct controlling vehicles is really the only fun part. Direct controlling infantry is horribly clunky and way too effective, making it necessary but supremely unfun.

[h1] Multiplayer Skirmish [/h1]
No real spawn protection means it is absurdly easy to spawn camp since resource gain is logarithmic, and all your dudes spawn in the same place. Spawned units have an invulnerability period, but it doesn't help at all with the line of sight mechanics. The ambushers can just hide and wait for the invulnerability to end, and since they aren't moving and you are, they see you and you don't see them. Playing with friends means you need a ton of stupid house-rules to prevent spawn camping and MG suicide runs and the like that make the game silly and arcade-like.

There's no concede option. If you push someone back to spawn and cap all points, you have to wait for the timer to run down or leave (and then deal with remaking the lobby or reinviting the player). There is no option to just end it.

There's no ping map button?????????

Making a lobby is a pain. If you change any game option that is higher on the screen than options below that option, all options below it revert to default. This means if you want to change the war period after you've already set the resource cap or something, you have to go back and retype or select the drop-down option that you already changed. This is only one example of the ridiculous jank.

Unlike Company of Heroes, your resource gain does not change based on the number of units on the field, so you will always be gaining the number of resources determined by where you are on the resource curve (determined by match time and resource cap), even if you're maxed out on units. This is a key balancing mechanic in real RTS games.

[h1] AI [/h1]
AI is a joke. It blatantly cheats because it's too dumb to do anything other than run in a straight line. They get a ton more resources than you do in a match. It might seem cool to blast a million tanks with your one AT gun because the AI has a huge resource advantage over you, but it gets old real fast. Remember how resource gain is logarithmic? It doesn't seem to be that way for the AI. The AI continues gaining resources after you've hit your asymptote (soft cap), meaning you can't spawn units anymore, but they keep pumping them out. Your three tanks and AT gun can't compare to the fifteen they get in a match unless you're playing cheesy and direct control them. Cheese shouldn't be a game mechanic.

[h1] Main gripes [/h1]
[i] (ok, more like all my gripes, haha) [/i]

[b] Building Things [/b]
[list]
[*]Laying mines requires micromanagement since the code isn't robust enough to automatically manage a squad laying mines. If you place multiple mines by shift left clicking, only one person will try to place them all. If you place multiple by right click dragging, Everyone will attempt to place mines, which is better, but they will usually leave half unplaced. Also you can't place multiple strips of mines by shift right click dragging.

[*]You can only make troops go to cover by clicking directly at cover. It's not possible to order your troops to seek cover or will they go to cover under free movement either, again requiring some extra micromanagement. If there was a way to make troops go to cover without having to find a convenient bush to click on would be great.

[*]Heavy Engineer Can't build gun emplacement if constructing building material dependent things first, and building it first doesn't use any building material. Maybe it is supposed to use an item but it is bugged? (it seems to use a special shovel, but sometimes this shovel is missing and the UI still shows one emplacement left. I guess this happens when I forget to resupply the heavy engineer squad in conquest. Confusing.)

[*]Unlike mines, engineer buildings are easy to build with multiple engineers but it is also too easy to accidentally cancel all your build orders by misclick or if your engineer dies. Maybe some kind of building interface would make building easier to manage. Maybe even add placing mines in there too!

[*]There's not enough time to prepare defenses in conquest.  forces have to be moved into defense positions from your side of the map, which after there is limited time to build anything. moving engineers with a truck it is possible to build one row of Tank Barriers that you right click dragged, but no time to place singular buildings in specific places before the opponent starts their attack (at 5 minutes of game time).
[/list]

[b] Ordering Units [/b]
[list]
[*]It's not possible to order multiple squads to move at the same time. It would help managing different attack direction tremendously if it was possible to group multiple squads and units together in different places of the front. Then have every group retain their formation and then you'd make a formation for the formations... yo dawg... I know, it's a lot, but then I could just push 1 for my alpha group and make them all advance, push 2 for bravo and angle them for support fire, press 3 to order mechanized charge, and 4 for support hotline and rain artillery fire! oh and 5 for bomber of course. Okay, artillery fits nicely to current group scheme since there is never too many artillery guns that wouldn't fit into one group.

[*]Can't order units through minimap. 

[*]Ordering tanks to move at the same time makes them move in a sparse column and not in a line or any other combat formation. So formations would be great. I liked those in Arma, but even one combat formation would nice.

[*]It's not possible to cue vehicle orders after ordering soldier to drive a vehicle (including artillery and ammo crates).

[*]Pathfinding isn't fully optimized yet. Everything works seemingly fine if there are no obstacles or the range is short. Even without obstacles on a longer path, the game chugs. If you surround an objective with impenetrable defense, the game can actually stop for a considerable amount of time when something tries to get in.

[*]Ordering a squad to repair a broken vehicle only makes one of the soldiers repair. Rest just watch from the side as one guy does it and even that guy gives up after one or too broken parts.

[*]Units won't fetch repair packs from close by enemy vehicles.

[*]Ordering artillery or ammo creates to move at the same time makes only one of them move initially. Maybe this is the vehicle column formation thing? Also, they end up in tight bunch at the destination no matter how you order them.

[*]Artillery have hard time moving in and out of trenches, requiring direct control and manually moving over the trench.

[*]Anything that isn't on foot gets stuck into everything often. So sometimes you will be wondering "Didn't I order a tank", and notice it stuck to some tree or another unit somewhere.
[/list]

[b] User Interface [/b]
[list]
[*]Many things lack hotkeys. For me, the hotkey bar is pointless since I constantly need to do everything. It actually would cost me more time to use the bar rather than just clicking through the numpad shaped menu (which can't be operated through numpad). Also, if you click between the buttons, your units will deselect like clicking ground.

[*]Inventory doesn't work in direct control. It opens but doesn't activate cursor, requiring to exit direct control and opening inventory again. In direct control, cursor activates only while examining bodies

[*]No hotkey for changing firearms (Grenades can be cycled with hotkey, though).
[/list]

[b] Misc. [/b]
[list]
[*]Sweeping for mines is very micro-intensive, slow and somewhat unreliable. You still have to pick those mines up since your units will still go through them if those mines are in the path.

[*]Crawling into or out of trench cancels direct control as a soldier.

[*]Maps in conquest are random. damage and defensive buildings don't persist between battles.

[*]No option to automate medics.

[*]Flamethrower infantry doesn't appreciate ROE. They just burn down everybody.
[/list]


[h1] Conclusion [/h1]

These things makes me hope for a fix constantly while playing.

Great game anyway. I have definitely gotten enough bang for my buck with this one.

It took me a while to learn the ropes for this game as it can be daunting/difficult when you're first starting (So many mechanics and things to do!)

So to start off, I mainly play the dynamic conquest mode which is my personal favourite. The single player campaign missions are cool as well, but I kind of started off with the dynamic conquest and it's been my favourite since. 

In dynamic conquest you start by choosing which nation you wish to play us (Currently there's 3 nations, Germany, Soviet Union, Finland,  and I think there will be another faction in the future as a DLC)

When starting dynamic conquest, you get given a specific amount of resources/research points (Depending on what difficulty you select) You use these resources to buy the units you wish to take on your offensive/defensive missions and the research points you use to unlock new units when you're progressing your conquest campaign, so basically you start with standard infantry/early war tanks and you progress onto better/more elite infantry, more late-war tanks etc.
The amount of different units each factions has is crazy and that leads to so many different ways to play the game so the amount of replayability is pretty big! 

Obviously there are the cons as well, like issues with unit pathfinding (Sometimes you need to babysit a vehicle so it gets to it's destination as it might get stuck at a certain point)
The A.I could be better in terms of how they act/counter your playstile, although I can understand that making better A.I is no easy task and it depends on what game engine is being used and what limitations it has.
There could be some more additions to conquest, ie more special abilities as airstrikes/recon, etc and maybe even have some special tasks on some of the dynamic conquest missions to make it more varied (Like having to kill a specific high-value target or have a side activity where you need to destroy an enemy convoy).

The graphics are really great (At least for my eyes) Infantry models look nice, tanks are really detailed (They also change camouflage/uniforms depending on what season your battle is in, ie winter/summer) . The FX of explosions/smoke is great and the game has really nice destruction. You can blow up buildings, fences, telephone poles etc. The sounds and their quality is peak as well! Really makes you immersed in the battle! (Plus the devs are currently working on a sound overhaul/skin update which will get released in the future)

I've experienced many great moments whilst playing dynamic conquest.  One of my fave moments was me playing as the Germans on the attacking side, The main problem was me putting too much research points for better infanty/support units and not researching better tanks/at guns. So what happened was I capped the first attack point with my panzer pioneers and my 2 PZ3 tanks which was fairly easy. Had to defeat some standard Soviet infantry and some dudes with AT rifles. The Soviets sent some ZIS trucks with maxims as counters, but they were no match for my tanks and got annihilated pretty quickly!  Fast forward 10 mins from me capturing the point and I can hear the roar of a tank in the distance. Initially I assumed it was something like a T-70 which did not phase me at all, but 2 min later, I see my panzer 3 getting knocked out with 1 shot. I check the map, zoom in on the location and see that it's a f**ng KV-1 and I had no proper counter for it. The first thing I tried was driving around the KV-1's far side to get some shots off with my 2nd PZ3. Got a few shots in trying to break the tracks of the KV, but my attempt turned futile as it just deflected every shot of my PZ3. Seconds later, the enemy sent another reinforcement wave from the same side the KV came. It was a blob of infantry units which included some guys with AT rifles. My PZ3 got shocked by a few shots from the AT rifles, I tried to get away, but in the end my PZ3 got tracked and it was stuck. I had to watch as that KV-1 turned it's turret towards my paper PZ3 menacingly and I just accepted my fate. The PZ3 was knocked out with the first shot and none of the crew members survived. The KV then started to move towards my defensive position slowly. I was thinking of a way to knock it out, but was becoming desperate. I then remembered that my Panzer Pioneers had some guys with AT nades so I attempted to crawl around it's side while it was engaging my other units at the defensive position to try and disable it. It worked out, I got 2 guys with bundle nades to get on the right side of the KV. Threw the nades. First one did absolutely nothing and the 2nd one knocked out one of it's tracks.  The KV then turned to my 2 guys and gunned them down with it's MG. Brutal. At this point I was already thinking that it's GG as I had nothing to put up against it, but at  that point I also had a small moment of clarity. One of my panzer pioneers has a flamethrower! At that moment I knew what I had to do! Took 3 of my guys including the flamethrower to flank the KV1 from it's right side. Thankfully it had some bushes/foliage so the KV-1 did not see my guys crawling around it. I got 2 of my guys with rifles to distract the surrounding infantry and engage in a small firefight while I was directly controlling my flamethrower guy to crawl to the back of the KV-1. Once I got to the back of the KV-1 I started burning the crew man who was repairing the track and the engine compartment of the KV-1. After a long burst of flames I could see that the KV-1 caught on fire. Finally the whole tank went in flames. All the crew members crawled out of the tank burning and at last, the KV-1 was finished. All 3 guys including the flamer got killed afterwards as there was too much infantry surrounding the tank and they overwhelmed my 3 guys, resulting in their death.  All in all it was a difficult task to pull off, but when I did pull it off, it gave me an immeasurable amount of satisfaction and I just realised that even with an outdated army/units you can still find ways to deal with difficult situations in this game such as this one.  Bit of a long read, but just wanted to give a small story from my own gameplay which really made me appreciate the game so much more! 

All in all, just want to say a massive thank you to the developers as for me, this game is amazing with so much content to explore and I can't wait for any future updates/DLC'S!

I do an in-depth review of one of my favorite franchise.
TLDR:
From "Men of War" the game this one replaces, overall there is Some improvement. The Men of War series, is the best WW2 RTS on the market, by far. But. they're moving towards microtransaction, and their DLC behavior is evidence for their lack of respect towards the community. 


"Uniquely. the game is a mix of RTS, Grand RTS, FPS and MOMBA, which if done well, would be incredible."

Soldiers Have Names, Inventories, and Experience  ::
You can move individual infantry units, which I greater prefer over 'CoH' and their squad based movement. In this I can split squads up and specifically move each solider to certain spots, or rearrange them into different squads. I can tell this solider to loot dead enemy soldiers, steal their grenades, switch weapons. There are also land mines, AT mines, trenches, foxholes you can dig. Conscripts don't start aiming great, veterans come loaded with AT, Smoke and AP grenades. Engineers can take petrol from a truck and refuel a tank, or use a detector to search for land mines, plant explosives. You can also control each unit yourself, by pressing 'E' you walk and shoot, either from a 3rd Person view, or from the normal RTS sky view. 

Big Tanks & Big Guns   ::
Tanks have realistic armor. Comparable to 'War Thunder' they have realistic armor on all sides and weak points to take advantage of. I can not speak on Historical accuracy, but I believe they are, at the least, very close. Realism mods on the Steam Workshop only add to its authenticity. Just like a solider, you can manually control tanks, tanks and guns also allow you to aim down a sight, as if you were in the tank. Artillery has its own unique angle as well. There are a huge amount of models for this game as well, every WW2 Tank 'War Thunder' has might also be modeled in this game. 

Campaign, Muliplayer and Conquest ::
The campaigns, unlike previous games, seem to focus a lot more on smaller based squads, more akin to 'Faces of War'. Only one mission out of six are genuine RTS missions. The rest are RTS/MOMBA quality style levels. There are also less factions then previous games in Campaign. Great Britain and Japan have been not made it into the campaign, only the USA, Soviet Union and Germany. The multiplayer is about as dead as any of the franchise games, occasionally there are players online, its not dead, its not busy. When it comes to 'balancing' there isn't much going on at all. They have tried to keep it real to WW2, and only set a few boundaries, like weapon range and supply amount. Unlike previous games, there is a new mode called Conquest, something slightly like a Grand RTS, where you decide where on the map the army will assault next, and a research tree to grow you army. Something like a basic 'War Band'. Multiplayer is really always been the best part of the games, because the computer is terrible.

The AI Nightmare  ::
It's so bad. Going all the way back to "Faces of War" I don't think the AI has changed at all. In Men of War Assault Squad 1 and 2 they didn't even have working AI in the skirmish modes. The enemy AI wouldn't have a single unit on the map. Unlike Skirmish or Conquest, Campaign is a built map, with each solider placed specifically and each reinforcement route planned manually. So there is an illusion that the computer is making decisions, when it's all planned out before hand. Practically, 99% of the time, you will start a conquest and never see a single enemy unit, the computer just doesn't work. It just does NOT work. On the 1% of times I have gotten it to work, the computer would send maybe 2 infantry squads and maybe 3 cheap tanks instantly to their death, or across the map, all bunched together. The computer has zero code written about this. Skirmish and Conquest, what ever they call it, the computer AI does not work. It doesn't understand you have a tank that is stronger and it doesn't understand any tactics or strategies. 
So the computer does Not work, but the AI? Pretty terrible too. Tanks, soliders, will ignore orders sometimes, or run into fire, take the longest way possible and gets stuck on a hill. Tanks AI switching APCR to HE while your in a tank battle. Other times you will be sending a tank or AT gun up to the front line, desperately needed, only to get stuck on nothing or stop randomly half way and by the time you realize it, your squad of infantry you were micro managing has been completely wiped out. You may ask a artillery gun to point in x direction or a a Zis truck to tow a DHSK to the front, again only to later find out the AI just couldn't do it. Sometimes the AI will shoot and kill its own team. 

A$$hole Greed  ::
When I first bought the game, the conquest and skirmish modes were the first thing I tried, I desperately was hoping they finally made a game with working AI, something akin to Starcraft. Boy was I wrong. I spent twenty minutes in an empty map, thinking the enemy was hunkering down, nope, same ♥♥♥♥ AI. Later I found out that Skirmish mode kinda worked, but you could only fight against the Soviet Union, which pissed me off, because that is faction  I  want to play as. To me, a long time Soviet player, maybe stereotypically, think the German faction is buffed up AI, and that the community is obssessed with Nazi's. I digress, I later found out that the Skirmish and Conquest modes were taken out of the game, and made a DLC that you now how to pay for. Not to mention that this game, had much more DLCs then previous, but unlike previous DLCs, the new ones were basic features that should be in the base game, lots of tank models and soliders that were in previous games, aircraft and a new faction and now skirmish. 

So let me reiterate using an analogy, they released a game in 2010 with two hundred models in it, twelve map missions and a broken skirmish mode. Now they release the same game with 50 models in it, 6 missions, and no skirmish, but you can buy all of those things as DLC, oh and the Skirmish is still broken.

This is the best and most fun WW2 strategy game you can play right now.  I got COH2 on sale a few years ago but have barely played it because there was always MOW Assault Squad 2 and now this to play, which for me are far more detailed and fun games with more tactics and much more depth to them. Really nice looking graphics, The atmospheric maps and weather conditions, great damage with vehicle combat and environment destruction, everything looks and sounds great, infantry combat is fun, tank battles are great, artillery is fun to use. This game is a really good improvement in so many ways from previous WW2 RTS games.

Singleplayer is great, loads to do, lots of the campaign missions are really good, and there are 3 campaigns for three different factions now, German, Russian and Finnish. Then there is the fantastic dynamic campaign where you can capture enemy tanks and vehicles and fight with them from battle to battle. Direct control is a great feature and playing co-op with friends who can command the tactical battle while you run around as an infantryman or drive around in a tank is a great development in RTS games. Developers are doing a great job and adding great new features to the game all the time so its going to get even better. Unlike most games the game comes with an editor so you can create new maps and missions yourself if you want. The new dynamic campaign and editor give infinite replayability, like Total War campaigns. Vanilla game is great on its own but on top of that there is a great modding scene and lots of excellent mods on the workshop, adding everything you want from endless new maps and new missions to many factions and units not in the base game.

I came to the game from MOW AS2  so the basic mechanics of control and how the game worked were familiar to me, but there are several new really useful mechanics and you have to learn them. There are issues here and there, like with all games, but many criticisms seem exaggerated, and devs are very responsive with ironing out any bugs. Its like saying the (older) Total War games weren't among the best strategy games ever because putting men on the walls of cities was often a bit ropey. To avoid frustration you do have to shepherd your vehicles a bit, can't always just click the other side of the map and expect them to find their way there safely if there are a lot of obstacles (and don't drive your vehicles too close together!) but jumping into direct control will usually get your vehicle out of any problems (shift and click to set a path is also often a good idea).  Doing the tutorial is maybe not the most fun way to learn the game, watching a youtube tutorial and jumping into playing the game is probably a more fun way.

Multiplayer is great, I've never had any technical problems playing the game, except sometimes on multiplayer, but it usually works fine even then, skirmishes online or co-op campaign with a friend is an especially fun mode. The DLC is also worth getting and adds a lot to the game, so I'd say getting it all in a bundle is the best way. COH1 was the best game back in the day but COH3 will likely have more simplistic gameplay like the others so personally I'm sure I will still prefer this game a lot over any potential competitors, Don't really know why anyone would skip a game this good on sale and wait for COH or MOW2 and rush off to pay full price as soon as they come out, when new games these days are almost certain to be a buggy mess for at least several months after release, if they don't turn out to be a total travesty.

So in summary, don't be put off by any negative reviews, (and the vast majority are overwhelmingly positive) its a 10/10 strategy game. Seems like the first new game I've seen which hasn't turned out to be a disappointment for a long time. If you look at it and think you will like this game, you will.

[b] Overview [/b]

Considering this is not the next fully fledged release of a "Men of War" series I am pleasantly surprised by the quality and content put in this product. I am glad that this game got voice overhaul so if you select a specific unit it will respond appropriately to its type, so no more kübelwagen crew randomly shouting "load HE shell!". Moreover, this game feels more like "Robz realism mod" from the graphical and destruction point of view while still maintaining the mechanics we know from previous games (except Cold War and Arena ofc). 
Some players complain about the lack of nations you can fight against. Instead as of now with 2 DLCs we get to play as Finnish forces and we can access lend-lease equipment as Soviets. You might be familiar with Katyusha, but have you heard about her sister [spoiler]Andryusha[/spoiler]? That's how rich Arsenal in this game is. There is also a possibility in multiplayer to choose the period of war we want to fight in so we can fight with early war equipment without the need to deal with heavy tanks every single battle.

[b] Gamemodes [/b]

The campaign is pretty enjoyable as far as it is not a stealth mission. I don't know if it is just me, but I really can't stand them it is just a save-and-load game fest. Some defending missions on the other hand were truly epic and required a lot of tactical planning and micromanagement. Besides scripted campaign game offers dynamic campaign. It allows the player to choose a side, build a deck of units using the amount of money based on chosen difficulty and fight subsequent battles where you earn money and research points you can spend to unlock new units and even an airstrike. 

[b] New mechanics [/b]

As it is a Call to Arms DLC it naturally shares some similarities in in-game mechanics. There are 2 modes of direct control, It's possible to aim down sights in tanks, guns, and even with a sniper rifle. Interestingly enough those sights look different from each other. One little detail I am thankful for is when a soldier is carrying an AT weapon there will be an icon above his head. A cool addition is the possibility to build foxholes and to be honest you may disagree, but I am happy you cannot build long trenches lines like in Men of War: Arena they were to OP. Lastly, artillery is firing one shell at a time so you do not have to wait 2 minutes to reload and miss your target with quick 5 shots.

[b] Flaws [/b]

I did not encounter any major bugs and AI is not perfect, but much better than before, using cover could be improved as soldiers will always face the other way you want in the trenches. Path-finding is better, but could still use some work.

[b] Final verdict [/b]

All in all the game is great. I like it. 10/9.

If you're a fan of games like Men Of War or the base Call To Arms, I have reason to believe you'll find this pretty enjoyable. My reasoning for why is that, in effect, GoH: Ostfront is a spiritual successor to Men Of War, as it covers the WW2 era that MoW also did, except on what seems to be a newer engine, with newer tech, newer systems, and a myriad of quality of life changes, also including mod compatibility and a workshop function pre-built into the game with a myriad of other improvements.

While I loved MoW, especially Assault Squad 2, it's safe to say those games have begun to show their age, and the jank present in them is both a result of said age and the older hardware and tech that they were made on. Ostfront doesn't have those issues, and the developers seem aware of what players enjoyed and disliked about MoW, as they're including the former and excluding the latter where they can. Things like better and automatic unit resupply, better ballistics and penetration calculations for tanks, better armor values and profiles, and smarter squad compositions are just par for the course. Alongside that, Ostfront not only includes the classic campaign and flag-capturing skirmishes that MoW was so well known for, but it also includes its own spins in the form of easily compatible multiplayer, co-op campaign functionality, and even a 'dynamic campaign' where you and an AI scramble to achieve military domination in a myriad of randomly selected battles where an evolving tech tree becomes available after the end of each turn.

Alongside this, while I do -not- agree with the choice of the devs to lock certain content behind DLC, such as the faction of Finland and all their units being locked behind the Talvisota expansion or certain iconic German and Russian units like the Karl Thor and certain special T-series tank variants being locked behind Scorched Earth, I do understand they're not a fully fledged AAA super development team and they have to pay the bills somehow. However, I also feel like it would've been better to just charge full price for Ostfront and then have all these DLC packs as free included content than stapling them on and asking for a dollar amount for each one, especially as that leads to cases where certain units that can be considered mandatory to the kind of experience MoW was so known for are permanently locked away unless you're willing to cough up the money, and you'll still have to fight these units in multiplayer if someone else owns the DLC. I played a match with a friend while someone on the other team was a Scorched Earth DLC holder and we had to watch one of our defensive positions get instantly nuked by a shot from the Karl Thor...Which we didn't have but they had because they paid money for it.

If you can overlook the faction/expansion-locked DLC content and approach this as what's basically a smaller-scale Men Of War successor that's focusing a lot more on an attempt at mixing quality and quantity to deliver an updated and revised experience that's far more tangible and satisfying? I think both RTS veterans and greenhorns alike are going to love this one, and players of Men Of War are going to feel right at home in this title while they're waiting for MoW2 to come out, and even then, Ostfront might prove to outpace MoW2 due to the sheer level of quality, effort, and dedication the developers have shown to keeping this thing going. We're at a year and a half since release and relatively sizable patches and updates are released on a month-to-several-month basis, they also talk to the community and are notably active on the discussion boards, so...

End verdict? I personally recommend it because it's a blast from the past that doesn't fail to deliver what it promises, and while I find the piecemeal approach to DLC irritating, it's not enough to turn me off of this. It's a classic from my childhood rebuilt and remastered from the ground up in painstaking detail, and I can't get enough of that. I will also personally say that, even despite my gripes, each expansion they launch does feel like it could be a $10 mini-game in and of itself, and I will begrudgingly admit I do still feel the quality and effort they put into each expansion justifies the price tag, as it keeps their lights on, their staff paid, and permits them to continue updating the game.

In an ideal world Ostfront would've had all factions and all campaigns in at launch, but Barbedwire aren't a huge studio, they don't have AAA money, or AAA resources, yet I'd say what they've made has put the new Men Of War to shame and outshines multiple other recent RTS releases.

So...Yeah. Give them your money if you want to, you'll be helping this thing thrive, and maybe if it sells well enough they'll just be able to make and release a sequel to Ostfront that has everything in it from the get-go.

It's very rare that I review a game, much less review it seriously. However, this game has quickly become one of my all-time favorites

[b] My perspective [/b] 
I do not come from a background of playing Men of War, as some players have. I have it in my library, but have yet to open it. However, I have played many other strategy games extensively, such as Company of Heroes 1 and 2, Blitzkrieg 1 thru 3, R.U.S.E., the Wargame Series, and bits of the Command and Conquer series So, this review comes from a completely fresh perspective on the franchise, but from a fairly experienced RTS perspective.

[b] Game Pace [/b] 
This game is, by far, the most enjoyable RTS I've played. It's realistic enough that knowledge of weaponry matters, but not so realistic that your infantry squad can be wiped out by a single soldier because you didn't invest enough in scouting & reconnaissance. It's a perfect balance, in my opinion, even as a vanilla experience.

[b] Control Individuals [/b] 
You can actually feel and hear the power of everything you use. This is only enhanced by the game's 3rd person feature, which is absolutely huge. Want to be the frontline soldier with an MG, holding off an attack? Take control of him while the rest of the battlefield continues to rage on. Want to take control of a tank or AT rifle to land that perfect hit on a weak spot? Press E, load Armor Piercing, and make sure your aim is true! It's a game were BOTH grand strategy and individuals matter, moreso than any other strategy game I've played


[b] Conquest & Co-Op [/b] 
I have very minimal experience playing multiplayer, just because the singleplayer dynamic campaign (called Conquest) is so good! You can set your difficulty, and play persistent battles which determine your resources, as you make choices on what vehicles and equipment to research to best counter the equipment that the AI, too, is fielding. And the best part? It's co-op too! You can play with up to 3 more friends as you allocate resources, and work together with the decisions you make in each and every battle.

[b] Critique [/b] 
My only criticism is that the AI isn't perfecty up to snuff. There are occasional points of gameplay where you do feel as though you have to micromanage. In my experience, this mostly occurs when towing equipment such as artillery. Parts of the game are physics-based, and sometime the AI isn't smart enough to avoid driving full speed over a crater, or not cut corners on a bridge, sending the towed piece to a watery death.

*Infantry do not place themselves in cover very well.  Often must be done one by one which is fiddly and takes too much time.
*Line of sight & fog of war seem completely broken.   If the AI has one unit that can see you then all of their units can with no seemingly no accuracy penalty.  Range seems to be so long as to be basically limitless.  Indirect fire has insane accuracy. AI seems to find a way to one-shot you through the eye of a needle (e.g. through the windows of a building).  
*Conquest – progress is basically irrelevant as crews cannot be moved to new equipment as it becomes obsolete.  Also, infantry vulnerability means there is little point in getting invested in progress.
*Conquest – Defence. Positions given are often poor.  No time given to set up defences.  Why always two points?  Why not one? Why not five? Would be awesome if the player could select the position. Why not? It’s the players territory after all.
*Conquest - Balance of difficulty levels.  Sometimes ‘easy’ is very easy and sometimes offers quite a challenge. ‘Normal’ scales up far too quickly for equipment available.  Enemy seems able to spawn many more units.
*Control scheme is fiddly and annoying.  
*The direct control mode really can’t be used much as this then leaves the rest of your army without oversight and often it’s impossible to see much – when left in AI mode they will shoot at things you can’t see in direct control mode.  Generally I only used it when I couldn’t move a unit into position (see next point).
*Movement of stationary weapons (AT guns, mortars etc) is impossible if an enemy has been spotted nearby as they will automatically drop out of movement mode constantly.  Direct control seems to be the only way.
*Friendly fire.  Your troops will just fire at the enemy regardless of friendly troops in front.  Made worse by the fact that you can’t fix facings of stationary weapons – they will suddenly swing around and shoot at enemies on the other side of friendly troops.
*Placement of sandbags is very difficult (unless you are placing a single one).  Very tricky to join them together.  Would be better to just have a smaller sandbag ‘unit’ that you can then just drag into a line as long as you need.  Can’t join large foxholes together.
*Repairing is a bit painful as you have to keep telling them do each part.  They should just keep repairing until it is finished or they run out of repair equipment.   Impossible to tell how many repair boxes or whatever they are called will be required to complete the repair.
*Impossible to know how far weapons will fire.  No range cones, even if the developer does not want to do this for some kind of realism reason they also give no range information on equipment.  Weapons will not move to get in range to carry out an attack order.  They will do it if they’re in range, they won’t if they’re not.

 The German Campaign

Whats Great:
The feel and power of all the units.  Every gunshot, mortar round, tank shell feels as if it has weight and will potentially kill you.

This game always popped up in my feed given that I've flushed over 6k hours of my life into CoH2. I'd always blown it off because, from what little I knew about it, I assumed it was one of these disjointed RTS/FPS hybrid/milsim sorta joints that was probably for players looking to get the best of both worlds as opposed to actually experiencing a fully fledged and highly rigorous RTS experience. This assumption was founded mainly on my understanding of the original Call to Arms. Well... nothing could be further from the truth. 

Not only is this game perhaps more fully fledged than most other RTSs ever made, the integrated "FPS" elements aren't merely some gimmick aimed at appealing to a broader audience. [b]The direct control mechanic, which is actually not in first-person, introduces an entirely new stratosphere of tactical potential that launches the game into a league of its own.[/b] For instance, in Company of Heroes, micromanagement and spontaneous combat events do require the player to home in on the utility of one unit at a time in order to accomplish specific goals. However, the RNG element of this system still distances the player from being able to fully assert their tactical dominance over engagements. Being able to get down and dirty, and execute plays EXACTLY how you want to, is not only extremely thrilling, but mentally engaging. Nothing is more satisfying than landing a hit on the ammo box of a Konistiger from across the map and watching its turret literally blast off into space while the ravaged crewmen flail around engulfed in flames. The level of detail, being able to manage the precise inventories of each unit, being able to choose the exact window you'd like a unit to fire from, being able to dictate the stance you want a unit to take on (prone, knee, standing), needing to tend to medical supplies, repairs, munitions, and all these aspects of the game's world which make it come alive, one questions how much more they may possibly be immersed into an RTS experience. 

[i]There are an infinite number of potential solutions to every problem. There is no way of predicting what's going to happen next. There is always more you could be doing to get an edge. The difference between victory and defeat is often a mere well placed smoke grenade or an extra med pack. That bush in the corner may prove the perfect vantage point for your AT rifleman to bring down an enemy heavy tank. And no Company of Heroes moment compares to being able to directly control a flamethrower infantryman as he torches a a tank's engine, forcing the crew inside to flee their vehicle and throw themselves on the ground, begging for mercy. We need more eyes on this game. We need to push it to the forefront so that the multiplying number of RTS developers seeking to make their mark on this new age for the genre can gain true respect for what Barbed Wire Games has accomplished here. They must recognize that to deliver on a product that's anything short of what Gates of Hell represents would be to only take another step back into those failures which are to blame for the decades long death of our genre out of which we are on the cusp of emerging from.[/i]

The game is pretty solid, but it does have it's problems. The problems are mostly minor, like pathfinding issues on some maps, but I've found that after more than 1,000 hours playing, the majority of people's complaints are based on "realism". This game does look beautiful, and while many aspects of it are "realistic" it doesn't feel like it was actually meant to be a simulator. GoH sits somewhere between an RTS like Company of Heroes and a more serious and realistic battle simulator.  It has some really nice features that are absent from other RTS games, like the ability to take over any individual soldier or vehicle in FPS mode, the ability to play the dynamic campaign in co-op mode, and other features which set it apart. The point of a game is to be fun and entertaining, and this game is definitely that. It does have it's flaws which are not deal breakers for the majority of people, but I've been on the Dev's Discord for months and seen firsthand that they do in fact patch bugs and gameplay issues while also releasing additional content. So, this game is much like most games in the sense that it's still under development while having been released, but it's also extremely easy to mod this game so if there's a particular way you'd prefer to play it, you can learn to mod it in under an hour and start changing whatever you want, even adding whole new vehicles to the game. Personally I give GoH a 7/10 which is pretty high praise from me.

EDIT: Next month I'll hit 5,000 hours in-game, I've been an official beta tester, and I've created multiple huge mods for the game. The content that's still being released, the new game features, the care and maintenance fixes still being released, and the continuing expansion of a game originally called "Ostfront" that now includes the West front too... well it's safe to say that even with the minor wonkiness of the game, it's still very satisfying to play, even after thousands of hours.

It's really hard for me to have quite as much fun playing other RTS games now knowing I can't just jump into a soldier and deliver a battle defining anti-tank grenade into the ass end of something someones been saving up all game for.

While the campaign cut-scenes are a bit janky and there's bugs here and there, overall it's an extremely impressive title.

I bought this game in the sale because Steel Division 2 lacks sufficient maps or a random map option (but is otherwise a great game).  Sadly this game promises much but fails to deliver.  It tries to combine 1st person shooter with RTS but ends up lost in its overly complicated micro-management that creates a very steep learning curve and far too many clicks to enable a simple task.  The tutorial is awful and of little help; i.e. click on the button in the (whatever) corner without highlighting that button or saying which mouse button to click.  The faults are too many to list but here are a few examples: It claims to be realistic but it takes longer to load a squad into a truck than it does to dig a fox hole.  Tanks fail to present frontal armour to the enemy.   The cry “achtung panzer” can be heard when no enemy tanks are present.  The tiny cursor is white and easily lost against a (typically) monochrome background even on my large 4K screen, resulting in more time trying to locate the cursor than ordering the indistinct units around.  Use of the mini-map is a must if you are to locate the enemy (or indeed your own forces) and navigation around the battle is tricky if I am polite.  OK so I have only played the game for 21 hours . The only saving grace is being able to look through a gun sight and de-pixilate the enemy but even that requires tricky adjustment when moving from 3rd to 1st person perspective.

This game is everything I loved about Men of War Assault Squad 2 and everything I disliked about it with some new additions to the list. This game really feels like a sequel to the Men of War games than an addition to CTA, which I like, but in keeping with the franchise it is definitely a micromanagement simulator. If that is what you are looking for then look no further. If you prefer a higher level strategy then steer clear. This review only covers the single player skirmishes and campaign since I don't have multiplayer experience with this one.

Pros:
This game retains the same familiar feel of MOWAS2, but with better graphics and larger maps (benefit of coming from CTA). If you know how to MOW then you generally feel comfortable with this one. There are some large battles that are amazing that really need tactical level strategy to achieve the objectives or survive. The explosions are satisfying and using combined arms to achieve the goals feels satisfying.

Cons:
The pathfinding for the AI seems to have gotten worse over the years. It is worse than MOWAS2. There should be improvement over time, not digression. Telling a soldier to look in a crate 2 feet away suddenly becomes a headache because there is a fence post in the way and he gets stuck. It happens constantly. Telling a squad to traverse a section of battle field while you issue some other orders? Better not do that since you will have to babysit the squad cause some will get stuck somewhere. Next, the objectives have never been more unclear. Defend the village you say? I didn't know I had to take my only 6 soldiers and have them search the far reaches of the map to kill every last soldier in an enemy battalion to trigger the next phase of the mission. Also, the voice overs have random glitches where they don't match the messages or repeat when they shouldn't. Lastly, and this is just a personal issue, why are we still throwing these random sneak missions into a tactical combat strategy game? I hate sneak missions.

Aside from these issues it is a solid tactical strategy game that I will continue to play (skipping past the sneak missions) If you like micromanagement in your strategy, this is for you. If you want a higher level of strategy where the sub-units can make some decisions, then there are plenty other titles in this genre that offer that experience.
