There's a lot to enjoy in this game, I'd go far as to say that it really is a blast sometimes. But other times it just really makes you question why you're still playing this game.

Starting out with Pros:
+ Sandbox is a huge playground
Possibly the largest open-world game I've played, and it's filled with a lot of fun side-activities and outposts to raid.

+ Fun stealth/infiltration style gameplay
It really feels like a puzzle game, where the pieces are your bullets, and the way to solve them is where you put those bullets. You have tons of toys to play around with and my personal favorite is the exploding drone. I just feel smart for successfully and quietly raiding a base. Or alternatively, blow everything up with C4, mines, and the drone.

The 'tactical' side of this game is mostly just interactions with your friends and marking out targets. It's still highly rewarding and enjoyable. Taking out generators and drone jammers to lower a base's defense is always fun. Removing strategic targets make you feel like a true commando in action. Plus if you play on singleplayer, you have a maximum of three free instant kills on selected enemies.

The support powers are also cool, it reminded me of Battlefield 2, the one from 2005 I mean, so they're not exactly new or groundbreaking but fun to play with nonetheless. And like BF2, the vehicles are also great fun, but most of the time you're going to want a helicopter more than anything else.

It's also just a huge laughter generator, especially with friends. So much ridiculous shenanigans and endless possibilities for unrestrained explosive fun.

+ Extensive character customization
If you want to look like your average The Division character, you can do that. Wanna look like a soldier that's all geared up? Yup. What about a dude on vacation with a polo shirt? That's all game. It's a shame this aspect is held back by one of the major cons, see below.

+ There's lots to do
People complain it's repetitive, then don't play the same game several days in a row. You get your money's worth activities-wise, just play in short-bursts with friends. Otherwise it will feel like a slog having to commute and doing the same types of missions.

+ Game just looks great
My PC has had its glorious days but even with modest settings, game looks really good. Most of everything is highly detailed, especially the outfits and guns.

+ Interesting lore and story
A super-powered drug cartel that bought out the government armed forces is genuinely a dangerous threat. Plus there are some colorful characters in there that intrigue.

As for the frustrations with Cons:
- There's no jump button or jumping of any sort
That means you're prone to getting stuck on the rough terrain or at the cliffside while you make your escape from the Bolivian armed forces. You have two options, you can one: kill yourself, or two: fast travel to a teammate. But that second option isn't always available when you're in combat.

- Direct confrontation is surprisingly not fun
Even with maxed out bullet resistance you still die in as little as 4 - 5 hits to your left pinky toe from a mile away. Enemies have extreme laser precision and have a better wall-hacking system that your supposed state of the art technology of tagging enemies. I get it, it's not the point, but there are times you can't avoid direct confrontation.

- Instant failure stealth missions
There's one particular mission I'm talking about, it's not the one with the mansion. You have to sneak into a heavily guarded base and meet with an agent. Simple right? Problem is, you're not allowed to kill any enemies, and you can't be spotted. It's instant game over. Fine, get lucky with RNG AI pathfinding, you get in and meet with agent. But then the next segment is guns-blazing, and as we've established, your armor is made of butter, and there are no checkpoints.

- Game is prone to crashing
Now I've tested this on three capable machines and all three of them have experienced at least 2 or 3 crashes. If you've played long enough, you're sure to crash more than 5 times.

- Frustrating bugs
There's a specific province with a specific mission where you need to rely on AI units to get into a van then guide you to the next part of the mission. My friend and I have restarted this several times on the beginning alone because the AI kept failing or getting stuck with pathfinding. There was even one time the AI got inside the van only to sit on the roof, THE ROOF OF THE VAN! (WHILE GETTING HIS ARMS STRETCHED ABNORMALLY).

There's another bug with the drone wherein if you get spotted and simultaneously use the detonate button, the drone won't explode, and you won't get your drone back until you reconnect to the game host. Sometimes you can get stuck using the drone until an enemy shoots you once. After activating Tier One, this bug happens a ton more frequently than you would expect, I heard it's a bug from 2017 and it still hasn't been patched out.

There's a separate bug wherein your drone payload flat out does not work but it will trigger the cooldown of that payload. This happens quite frequently and is equally frustrating. They won't patch this out, because a sequel for this game is coming.

There's a relatively uncommon chance for the coop session to become out of sync, causing players to not perform actions reflected on the client-side screen. There were two instances I got separated from my game host but at his screen he was flying the helicopter I was riding. So the one I was on appeared to be floating in mid-air with no sound, no animation, and no other player inside. Sometimes the player will reappear outside the helicopter and smash into the blades causing the heli to explode.

Do you like using grenade launchers? What about your game working consistently? You can promptly say goodbye to both if you do. Your grenade launchers have an extremely large chance of not working, you'll instead shoot a regular bullet, only after a three to five seconds later will they explode. You cannot use this attachment with intentionality. Again, old bug, not fixed.

Fairly often when joining a session, you will spawn in the middle of a firefight. And what have we established about health in this game? You're made of molten marshmallow. A single stray bullet can end the 4-man Bolivian tour group. I cannot for the life of me understand why it doesn't spawn you in a safer location.

- Uplay
Two clients running in the background for a video game and cloud saves. One of them is useless. It constantly stops working during updates, and conflicts with Hamachi. There's also a chance it won't sync your achievement rewards. Not to mention it's slower than a sloth. Yeah I think you've guessed what it is, it rhymes with pooplay.

- Microtransactions
I've got nothing else to add here. They are what they are.

- Super long loading times
Need to respawn right next your teammates in the same area? Wait 1 - 2 minutes. That's an eternity right there.

Conclusion:
I can't say this is something I can easily recommend, especially at full price and with its sequel coming out. This is my first shot at a Ghost Recon title, and I'm frankly disappointed.

This does not mean I hate the game. There are genuinely fun moments to be had when playing with a friend or a group of friends. But its problems are too large to ignore and they very quickly get in the way of everything. No amount of cool cameos from other titles and 80s references can save this game. Because for all the 'care' Ubisoft seems to show for this title seems to be the amount of loot types you'll get on random crates. Terrible unlock system, we don't deserve this, period.

If you really feel like getting it, wait for a big discount. Not that lame 20% off thing, I mean 60 - 75% off. Even then it's tough to kind of level the odds.

Tom Clancy's แรกๆ ที่ดังมากและมีภาคต่อภาคแยกเยอะมาก สำหรับในตระกูล Tom Clancy's และการกลับมาของภาคนี้บอกได้เลยว่าในงาน E3 นี่แฟนเกมต้องร้องแหกปากทำไมว่ะ เพราะว่าภาคนี้จะมีระบบ Co Op 4 Players แบบภาค Future Soldier แต่ที่ทำให้แฟนเกมนี้ ดีใจจริงๆคือ ภาคนี้เป็นแบบ Open World แบบเต็มที่มีแผนที่ ขนาดใหญ่มาก และภาคนี้สามารถขับรถยนต์ ขับคอบเตอร์ ขี่มอไซต์ ขับเรือดำน้ำ เครื่องบินได้ตามใจชอบ ซึ่งเป็นอะไรที่แหวกแนวและใหม่มากสำหรับเกมตระกูลนี้ เพราะเป็นภาคแรกที่ทำแบบนี้ได้ และเกมนี้อาวุธก็มีให้เลือกใช้ เยอะมากๆ แน่นอนว่าเกมตระกูล Tom Clancy's จะเกี่ยวกับทหาร อยู่แล้วดังนั้นถ้าพูดถึงทหารก็ต้องมี ประยุทธ์ ถุยมี เรือดำน้ำ ถุย ก็ต้องมี ปืน อุปกรณ์ครบและภาคนี้ก็มีมากกว่าทุกๆภาค อุปกรณ์ Weapon Mods ครบมือ แต่เกมส์นี้เนื้อเรื่องไม่ค่อยจะดีเท่าไหร่ เพราะว่าเกมนี้ดูเหมือนจะไม่ได้เน้นเนื้อเรื่องเท่าที่ควร เนื้อเรื่องเกมนี้ไม่ค่อยมีน้ำหนัก ด้วยการที่ว่า ภารกิจเกมส์นี้ จะมี บอสใหญ่อยู่ตัวหนึ่ง และการที่จะไปหาบอสใหญ่ได้ต้องจัดการ บอสรองก่อน และบอสกรองจะกระจายตัวอยู่ทั่วแผนที่โดยจะปกครองแต่ละเขตอยู่ และการจะไปหาบอสรอง ได้ต้องทำภารกิจหรือหาข้อมูล ของบอสแต่ละตัวนั้นๆ ก่อน ถึงเนื้อเรื่อง มันจะประติดปรับกันจนพามาเจอกับบอสใหญ่แล้วมันก็ดูธรรมดา ไม่มีอะไรมาก เนื้อเรื่องจืดและเชยมาก ำม่เคยเห็นเกมไหนทำเนื้อเรื่องแปลกๆแบบนี้มาก่อน เพราะแบบนี้ใงเนื้อเรื่องถึงไม่ค่อยมีน้ำหนัก ก็แค่ทหาร 4 คน เข้ามาจับโจรย์ พ่อค่ายา แค่นั้น ส่วนภารกิจ ก็ซ้ำๆ ซากๆ Recommended, but with major caveat — it is filled with extremely frustrating moments that only exist because of game mechanics. Probably the most enduring frustration of the game is the third-person perspective; it's impossible to smoothly sweep through a building interior because the first person aiming narrows the FOV too much and 3rd person over-the-shoulder has you seeing something different from what the player avatar and enemies see. This means that if you see an enemy and shoot, you might hit a wall or box or something that's in the way of the shot, but which you can see clearly. Conversely, sometimes you'll not be able to see an enemy, but the PC is in line of sight of the enemy despite a wall or object obscuring your view. Out in the open, it's rare and has little impact. Inside a building, it's almost as clunky as Arma.

The ballistics system is extremely dumb. As far as I can tell, the trajectory of all guns are the same, but the "range" statistic governs how fast bullets travel and how much damage is reduced. For short guns like pistols and SMGs, you can see the bullet go about as fast as a paintball would so you need to lead a moving enemy by about a foot to make a hit. Sniping is a chore because at 300 or so meters, the bullet will drop about 6 ft from point of aim. Just as well though, as the highest magnification in the game is 6X, which is a very modest magnification in the real world. It's a damn shame though, because the game has some excellent opportunities to play sniper. 

Another major recurring annoyance is the enemy shot spread. It's very narrow, even for enemies holding an SMG in each hand blasting in full auto. At lower difficulties, this isn't a problem because the PC can absorb hits, but at higher difficulties (which is required to get some of the collectibles) an enemy who sees you from 50 ft, alerted by a helicopter that inexplicably can see directly below itself, who blasts away with a full auto MAC-11, can quickly send you to the bleed-out stage. 

On missions that are setup to cause confrontation like that, it gets really old, really fast. 

Friendly AI is both overpowered and next to useless. They can be used to setup impossible shots which is helpful but cheesy, but they won't get your back in any way except to revive you after watching some gangster run up behind you and blast you in the back. It's really jarring to see 3 heavily armed teammates behind you, turn around, and then get shot by someone who ran right past those 3 heavily armed teammates. They have a magic stealth ability where they can walk right past enemies without being seen, but occasionally, during stealth-required missions, they'll somehow get detected and ruin the mission. These of course usually take the most time. 

Furthermore, there's an ending for if you get less than 100% completion, that's incredibly unsatisfying. If you get 100% mission completion, you can another ending, that's just as unsatisfying. Basically, it makes all the events feel like it doesn't matter, which is kind of a big deal for people who like the storytelling. And the end-game mission is completely stupid and makes no sense. I'll just say they really need to take Tom Clancy's name off of these games. 

In all, it was a fun game. Some really satisfying moments when you can pull off the plan in your head, but just as many really annoying and frustrating moments. For the most part I guess I liked the game, but for the annoyance and the hollow ending, I wish I hadn't taken the time to play it.

You will love this game if you enjoyed Phantom Pain as gameplay is similar, with better movement and gunplay. Speaking of which, it was a missed opportunity for Ubisoft to not allow some kind of option to build something with all these resources you collect. Sure, you level up your character and rebel assist options - but you never get an option to establish so much as a crummy looking FOB. You collect guns of all kinds along with their attachments, but you never have that hub to build on. I do understand that the concept is 'Ghosts', your character is aptly named 'Nomad', and this is not another sandbag laying simulator. Having the option to build in this world still would have been great.

You will also love this game if you enjoyed R6: Siege. They've incorporated some Siege characters into the game and their missions really mesh well.

The only other missed opportunity they had with this game was the PvP. 

Competitive modes are fun with their quickplay events and options, though you are limited to 4v4 GHOST matches. They would have been smarter instead to have built modes with bigger maps and higher player counts. The storyline of all out war breaking out in Bolivia could have easily passed and players would have had a blast duking it out over large areas in 50vs50 battles. I'd even settle for 20vs20, because that would at least allow all the PvP kits to truly shine with their utility options.

These are my criticisms and the game is still a blast worth placing many hours of time into.

In short - Wildlands doesn't feel any different from Far Cry, Watchdogs, The Division or Assassin's Creed. It's a "You've seen one, you've seen them all" type of situation. We all know the genre of this game, from the tags and description and also trailer and picture available right above here. So I'll just get to the point.
It's a Ubisoft game, so obviously, it still follows the Ubisoft formula. A bit parkour here, some broken scripts there and alike. Although is so much fun with your friends, it lacks the same experience alone [aka solo]. The AI are worse than ever and commanding them is also not useful and sometimes is even dangerous. The only useful command is sync shot that is not even balanced. If the selected target is in open area, no matter how difficult to reach, They can shoot from kilometers away; They don't even face the enemy or shoot straight at him when you look at them. however the AI teammates are cool and memorable characters, their dialogues are sometimes dark and hilarious.
The graphics....well, although the graphics are heavily un-optimized, the view of Bolivia is outstanding, I play on the lowest resolution [800x600 specifically] and graphics, the view still amazes me and I usually stop by to just watch the sundown or sunrise. The characters are very detailed and the field of view is also breathtaking.
Customization on the other hand, has its ups and downs. You are very limited in case of facial details, but the outfits options are massive, yet not enough. We can say it's better than Division in this case, but still it lack certain style of outfits or most importantly, haircuts. The outfits are great because they have no stats to limit you from how you want to look, unless some certain update accessories that will add new animations or stats. I can looks like a cowboy roaming around Bolivia, or I can be a USA infantry, and none of them change my health, stamina or damage.
There are lots of weapons available for you to use. Although the sounds or stats are not satisfying me [and many other], they are enough for you to choose how you play/improvise. you can be sniper, have a G28 with an HTI, or you can be a loud one, grabbing LMGs and Shotguns, or you can be silent, maybe even all of them in the same time. There's no restriction about what set of weapons you can grab. The game also has a very good and big set of weapon customization system; Dozens of skins with lots of different tools like Laser sights or muzzles.
The story has different aspects and stories but it's not a good linear, full of surprises story. It's really due to the fact of "Full Autonomy" promise they gave us. you can take down whoever you like in any order you like and in any way you like. This leads to freedom of play but a very meh story, since there's no connection between your actions except for head takedowns which will lead to El Sueno's reaction. Though you see every boss has its own story and origins, you won't find a very amazing story in it.
The gameplay which for some of you might be the most important aspect is like every Ubisoft games you [might] have played. Lots of bugs and broken scripts, and some annoying micro transactions. If you are looking for a real challenge, this game can put you to your limits. If you are just looking to slack off and have an easy gameplay, you are also in the right place. Turn of the tier and face the ultimate challenge in the game. although Tier mode doesn't look fair, it's a nice and rewarding challenge. Even turn off the HUD and get the full immersion out of it; Or you can just set it to arcade difficulty, and kill everyone like cutting the butter. The gunplay feels satisfying and fun and the variety of options really helps it, you have full freedom of engagement, jump over a fence, or go guns and blazing in the front door or even go far up a hill and takedown everyone with whatever sniper you like. Even though solo might get boring, it's a good way to get ready to play with your friends. No one will curse you if you screw a mission and you can patiently take your time and learn. Although the game offers Public Matchmaking, I don't recommend it to people who prefer stealth. Sadly there is no way you can customize what type of player you want to play with and most of the people [sadly] prefer direct assault over stealthy approaches.
and YES, the game offers PvP experience, however from where I am [which is middle-east and/or basically Asia], it's nearly dead and takes alot of time to join a match and you probably end up joining an existing match that has been going on before you join.

I have mixed feelings about Ghost Recon Wildlands. There are some parts that I really like and others that could be greatly improved. I'm going to start off with a general list of my pros and cons and go into more detail below.

Pros:
[list]
[*] Huge open world with a variety of different regions ranging from snowy mountains to jungles, swamps and deserts.
[*] Variety of weapon attachments to choose from (on most guns}.
[*] Different ways to approach missions.
[*] Character customization is okay. There is lots of clothing, vest, and headgear variety, but not many helmets.
[*] You don't need any DLC to enjoy the game.
[*] Co-op is fun with friends. I've only had bad experiences with randoms, but that's just me.
[/list]

Cons:
[list]
[*] The map feels empty of enemies, but there's civilians.
[*] Not much mission variety.
[*] Story is meh and you can see the ending coming from a mile away. There was only one twist that caught me off guard.
[*] The friendly and enemy AI isn't the smartest.
[*] Bullet velocity is pitiful, and the drop is atrocious. You can't shoot 200 meters away without aiming incredibly high.
[*] Most of the weapons and cosmetics are locked behind lootcrates / surprise mechanics.
[*] Vehicle handling is awful.
[*] There are still quite a few bugs.
[*] No new game plus.
[*] Daily challenges provides and endgame, but it's extremely repetitive and has you doing the same things over and over again.
[/list]

[b] World and Missions: [/b]

     The Map is absolutely stunning. There is lots of variation between the different regions and each offer their unique scenery. You have urban environments, jungles, forests, deserts, and snowy mountains. The game's version of Bolivia is so big that it takes a long time to drive from one end of the map to the other, which would be great if there was more to do. 

Don't get me wrong, the missions are fun to play, but that's it. Once those are done, there's rebel ops, special operations, collectibles and that's it. Post-game, all you can do is clear bases for fun. There's no enemies in the wilderness other than vehicle patrols and convoys on the roads, making the map devoid of enemy life anywhere but in bases.

The lack of a new game plus mode makes it harder to play the whole game again with what you've earned (outside of lootcrates). Missions (not rebel ops) aren't that much different. There's vehicle stealing missions, assassination/killing missions, capture missions, blow something up missions, gather intel missions and framing missions. The only variety is the enemies you fight and the location that the missions take place in. Often times, it feels like I'm doing the same thing, but in a different place. There are some different ways to approach missions like loud or stealth (for some of them), but there's also a choice on what direction you want to go to get to the objective, each offering their own pros and cons. That's about it. It's nothing like the level of choice they advertised during E3 a few years ago.

[b] Weapons: [/b]

      Weapons are unlocked by finding weapon crates scattered around the world, or by buying them with premium currency (you can get this for free if you work for it though). I think the weapons are alright, but it feels like you're shooting a paintball gun or something. The bullet drop is atrocious and travel time is insane and totally unrealistic. It's like weapons are zeroed to 50 meters, and you have to aim incredible high above the heads of enemies to hit them at 100-150+ meters. Long range sniping is really difficult without a friend to spot for you since enemies disappear after about 500-600 meters (unless you scope them in and walk backwards). Weapon customization extremely limited. I have no idea why it gets so much praise. Most of the attachments might as well be cosmetic, and there's no reason to run several combos.

[b] Customization and Lootcrates: [/b]

     You unlock a lot of the customization when you first play the game, but there are still quite a few things that are locked behind paywalls or grindwalls (crates and store bundles) I think what you start off with is great unless you want helmet mounted night vision or slightly better looking vests. The helmets are sad though. All you have is an Ops-Core FAST helmet and a High Cut helmet. The Ops-Core helmet can't even be brown because the colors on certain pieces of gear are so screwed up. Many of the camos are also off and extremely inaccurate to their real life counterparts. Some of them like AOR1 are so bright and look ugly on anything you put them on. No cosmetics provide any benefit or concealment. Camo doesn't even anything, and armor provides no benefit.

[b] Friendly and Enemy AI [/b]

     The AI in this game isn't absolutely horrible, it's just slightly above that. Your team AI takes out enemies and revives you most of the time, but Unidad (the game's heat system) can kill them so easily. You can upgrade them with skill points to kill enemies better and tank more bullets, but that's it. Their primary use is to do sync-shot kills for you, but even that is limited. They can't drive vehicles, and can't sync-shot enemies inside buildings or structures.

Rebel AI likes to run you over, but they can be good in a firefight if you fully upgrade them. Civilian AI also likes to run you over and jump in your stream of bullets. 

In terms of enemy AI, these guys all depend on the difficulty. When you're not being stealthy, Santa Blanca charges at you and sprays at you, and all of them have the same spotting distance (so snipers don't have more than a grunt). Tier 1 mode is a joke, making enemies become terminators. Essentially, they now have superhuman reflexes and pinpoint accuracy with two uzis from 300 meters away while you're in a fast moving vehicle going at an angle away from them. As for Unidad AI, these guys act somewhat more tactically, carefully advancing on your position, staying put and waiting for you to get out of cover, or spamming you with endless vehicles. These guys never stop coming and tier mode makes them Terminators too. Other than that, they aren't that smart.

[b] Bugs: [/b]

     Where do I begin?

[b] Final Notes: [/b]

     At the end of the day, I'm still going to have to give this game a positive rating. The world is nice, the missions are okay and this game is a blast with friends. Playing with minimal HUD on the maximum difficulty is also a great experience. This is certainly a good time waster but I would only recommend getting this when its on sale. Just remember that this game isn't for everybody.

    In all honesty, if you have a choice between this and Ghost Recon Breakpoint, go with Breakpoint. Most of the negative reviews are extremely out of date, and a lot of the issues are fixed. Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands is a tactical shooter game set in an open world environment and played from a third-person perspective with an optional first person view for gun aiming.

In this game, players play as "Ghosts", a fictional elite special operations unit of the United States Army under the Joint Special Operations Command. It does not feature the futuristic setting used in Advanced Warfighter and Future Soldier, but instead adopts a modern-day setting, similar to the original Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon. As a result, the equipment featured in the game is based on weapons and gear commonly used by military forces around the world. However, it features some original equipment, such as drones that can be used to tag enemies and show objectives. These drones have limited abilities until upgraded.

The game is the first entry to feature an open world environment, which consists of nine different types of terrain, such as: mountains, forests, desert, salt flats, and also introduces a dynamic weather system as well as a day-night cycle. Completing missions during day-time allows players to spot enemies easily, while completing missions at night grants players a tactical advantage, as the night offers players better concealment and easier infiltration due to some guardsmen being asleep. Players are tasked with making observations before carrying out missions. A variety of vehicles, such as dirt bikes, helicopters and dune buggies are featured in the game. Unlike its predecessors, Wildlands features several side-missions.

After playing Ghost Recon Wildlands for over 500 hours I have come to the conclusion that it is probably one of my favourite games. The bullet drop mechanics make sniping more fun than in any other game I have played. Every Base is different and in 90% of cases you can freely decide on how to aproach the situation. No matter what tactic you choose, your AI Teammates will be there to assist you with sync shots. Speaking about the AI, apart from a few weird glitches the Enemies will react realisticly. Snipe one of them and the rest will take cover from the direction of the shot. Local Coop Review

Looking down at the great contrast between multiple reviews--people seem to love it or hate it--I often wonder if these impressions are due to how you actually play the game and with whom. I play this game with my long term gaming partner, and it is a blast. In other words, we never have the AI as partners since we have each other. 

Get into the Mood:

When we really get into a game, we geek out with it. In the case of Wildlands, which is fondly known to us as the "Sicario" game, we take our characters seriously, and they reflect our personas--a sort of second life on screen. I am a Latina, and I crafted my character that way as If I were vicariously living through her--cigar and all. I can understand the Spanish being spoken in the background of the game, so when I am playing, it is extraordinarily immersive. Since I am a teacher in real life, it is really cathartic to sit down at my desk and become my character and snipe some bad guys from afar. She can shoot well, is tough, exchanges slurs with the foul-mouthed AI, and gets down to business with that cartel. It is her job to clean up the dirty world of El Sueno. Someone's got to do it...

Story Come to Life

The game itself is inundated with video clips, some embedded with real people, most CG, but they are released to the player as the story unfolds and as you break into intel. I watched them all, read all of the written evidence and intelligence, and followed the story closely. I felt as if the game did a good job of making some of the NPC three dimensional--at one point at actually felt empathy for some of these villains, and caught myself saying, "Dude...why?" If you jump in to Wildlands, my suggestion is that you do it with both combat boots and read and follow all of the story elements available in Single Player/ Coop. Otherwise, the game might be perceived as being somewhat redundant, which in my mind, explains some of the poor reviews. The game is very visual; take some time to enjoy it.

"Whelp, let's try again I guess."

The difficulty of the game really depends upon how you want to play it. I played through the early game at regular difficulty until we unlocked the elite levels. Together we pursued these, and in the higher levels (without any visual cues on your radar), this can be really, really tough. Sometimes, we found ourselves forgetting about the mission and in all out wars. I was up to it. Bring it on! I should point out that you do not need to move into the elite levels once they unlock and can complete the game at normal difficulty. Sometimes we were not up to the super high intensity and returned to normal mode. Either way, we had fun, and many moments were pretty darn comical, more particularly when my partner would take to the wheel...(he is dyslexic, so what can I say). Still, we took it lightly, had a hard laugh, and would try again and again when needed. There is a real feeling of accomplishment when you complete a mission.

Bugging Out

Because the game is so much fun due to its customization, story elements, and non-linear story, it can be really, and I mean really, disappointing when you run into a mission-breaking bug. There have been times when in the middle of a car chase, we would suddenly find ourselves outside of our vehicle, running along the side. I have also experienced overlaps in quest dialogue and missions not functioning properly in terms of starting and stopping missions. Sadly, these types of problems required restarts. What I perceive is that many of the bugs present find their way into the game via updates and free content. They most definitely can use work on quality control before releasing these patches, but eventually they end up addressing them. That being said, I should mention that if you have an Nvidia 2070, do some Googling on Wildlands and compatibility before you buy. I have heard they have fixed the game-breaking issues with that GPU, but who knows.

Famous Last Words

My advice to you, especially if you plan on enjoying this with a friend, is dive in, especially if you can get it on sale. For now, I am about to jump back into my "Sicario" role since I have not played for a while. I guess the fact that I am still into this game after 150 hours says something in itself. The school semester is over, so it's time to become a badass again.

I'll preface this review by saying I've played this by myself, and as a result, does not directly correlate to co-op play.

I've played this game a fair bit, and it was great fun at first. endless amounts of map to explore, a lot of different weapons to find, rare vehicles that were difficult to obtain, etc. 
But after delving into the mechanics of the game, it's fundamentally broken and buggy. 

To pose a few examples; 
-At one point in the game I had to finish a mission using explosives only to complete a challenge, and I had covertly been using drones to detonate caches from a distance, without a chance of getting spotted, but lo and behold, several enemies are circulating the bush I'd been laying in, without spotting me. That proves to me that the enemy, when aggravated, KNOW where you are at all times, without spotting you, which breaks immersion ruins viability of many strategies.

-Another challenge asked me to complete the most gung-ho mission in the game using nothing but snipers on the hardest difficulty. This mission includes endlessly spawning enemies in armoured cars and gunship helicopters. Needless to say, the enemies homed in on me, despite using everything at my disposal to track, distract, and kill them before that happened. 

For me, that was the straw that broke the camel's back, as it displays so many poor design decisions and outright stupidity in this game's design.

[b] Vehicles [/b]
For a game that consists of hundreds of square kilometres, you'd expect vehicle handling to be fun and intuitive, no? 
Tough ♥♥♥♥♥, because it ain't. 
-Motorcycles and the likes all control horribly and you fly off the bike inconsistently. 
-Vehicles such as the APC oversteer A LOT and are a ball-ache to try to manouvre.
-There are 2 airplanes in the game, and they're both extremely slow and have no utility whatsoever. Add to that no rudder control while in the air.
-2 out of the three helicopters come in three variants, un-armed, minigun or rockets. The miniguns are pinpoint and are horrible to aim as a result of that, rockets are very underwhelming, suffering from poor damage, speed, audio and effects design. The third helicopter has more potential, but is also lackluster. And my final gripe with helicopters are their handeling. Their mevement doesn't have any skill or finesse to it, it's just WASD for directions and shift/control for elevation. Supremely boring, irritating and frustratingly simple. 

Due to all of this, my favourite means of transportation was fast-travel, I.e loading screens. That's not ideal.

[b] Weapons. [/b]
The weapons in this game were thrilling at first, but after a while I noticed they were all mostly the same, and there were no unique customization for any gun, just the same grips, suppressors and scopes. Attachments also don't make a lick of sense at times, reducing stats that shouldn't be affected for the sake of "balance", in a PvE game where the enemy knows where you are at all times.
There were no truly fun and/or unique weapons in the game, making the decent-good shooting mechanics feel pointless.
[b] Challenges and lootboxes. [/b]
This game rewards you lootboxes for completing 5,10 and 15 challenges a week, through 3 daily challenges. Now that may sound generous, but you risk losing your sanity for the sake of satisfying your gambling addiction. Some of these challenges can be so excruciatingly difficult or annoying that you end up doing ONE of them for hours or bust. That is what I was referring to before with the gung-ho mission. 

Unassorted gripes;
-Every single mounted weapon, whether it's tripod or vehicle mounted, is a minigun. With the exception of the APC and the helicopters with rocket pods. It just doesn't feel right or fitting. They're also not satisfying to use, can't tell you why.
-Civilians [b] do not budge [/b] when you want them to move. You can't communicate with them, and pushing them has very limited effectiveness. Shooting to scare them only makes them cower in place. Leaving and making a ruckus elsewhere has no effect either, they don't take the oppurtunity to RUN. This is notable because killing three civilians resets you, whether you're in a mission or not, and some challenges will not allow civilian casualties, despite having to use explosives in places [b] filled with civilians. [/b]
-While the game is beautiful at points, there's no incentive to just take a quiet walk in a jungle. There is little in terms of unique beauty in the world, and it is reinforced by the lacking audio design when out in the middle of nowhere. I feel like Counter-Strike: Condition Zero did a better job with jungle aesthetics than this game, but that might just be my rose-tinted glasses.
-Annoying A.I teammate banter that's very unfitting and embarrassing to listen to.
-A.I teammates sometimes refuses to pick you up, for absolutely no reason other than them being broken to ♥♥♥♥♥.
-An enemy spots you a thousandth of a second before you blow his brains out, and the enemy who previously didn't see you kills you in an instant.

I'll probably add to this when my brain decides to remember what I've so desperately tried to repressed.

I really don't have issues playing the game at times. I also enjoy how you can customize your character and your team with an array of outfits, although I'd personally like to see more variants of hair/facial hair etc. 
Unfortunately I ended up choosing NOT to recommend it is because I am very disappointed in four things:
1. How the AI are able to lock down your precise location even when you're trying to shoot from a huge distance or even trying to move away from your original spot after making a blunder. I swear it's like playing with heat-seeking enemies. Not particularly fun in that department and totally defeats the purpose of utilizing stealth.
2. Enemy spawns are ridiculous at times during gunfights, mostly appearing in locations where you're not looking (usually directly behind you, then they unload bullets happily, either incapacitating or killing you) therefore costing the mission.
3. Whilst I do like the additional content being added, (Sam Fisher, Rainbow Six Siege, Predator etc) I certainly had some form of expectation that these missions would have some depth. However it was nothing short of being frustrating. For instance, meeting Sam Fisher at the Unidad base, the arduous requirement of entering the base undetected, and not killing any enemy becomes an absolute chore, because that's all thrown out the window right afterwards when you have to defend him.  
I do understand the necessity to have difficult missions from time to time, however I believe there's a certain way of designing a mission to be tough without being sloppy or having redundant approaches. 

4. Driving mechanics....I definitely abhor how the vehicles move in such a way that it's so unreal. You try and adjust your lane a bit, your car still goes straight, do a little more, you end up doing a humongous sharp turn, so your car does barrel rolls off the track (or even the cliff). The most outrageous thing of all is that even the slowest collisions results in awfully high damage. So during missions where you have to drive a vehicle, what's the point? 

Would I play this game again? Probably every now and then if there's new content out. As for the 4 Cons I mentioned, I'm not so bothered by the first two since I've adapted to how it run and found a way to get by it. 
But again, it's really unfortunate I have to put the thumbs down mainly due to the last two Cons really ruining the potential enjoyment I could've had.

1. Content:

They add couple challenges weekly, which is the reason I keep playing this game even after far long it's release. As well they add a couple new "Operations" that are basically 2-3 missions, those are really fun and very well design that also give very nice rewards.

Also there is a reward for completing all the 25 waves, but it is not a cool reward so it is not worth it. PVP content, altough Im not a huge PVP player (atleast on GRW) I find it very fun to play, atleast the 5 matches I just played.

If youre going loud, a "Juggernaut" - basically a dude in armour - will usually take a lot of bullets to kill, well not in stealth no, In stealth EVERY enemy takes ONE SINGLE BULLET to wherever you want to shot them and they are gone. Ghost Recon Wildlands is one of those very few heavily detail-oriented military games.  At face value, it seems to be just your typical shooter with elements of Stealth.  There is MUCH more to this game than that.  I'll cover a few points briefly as to why i enjoy this game:

Geography :  The geography of Bolivia,  as far as i can tell, in this game is very similar to the topography you would see in real life.

Stealth / Detection : Wildlands I think has one of the best detection mechanisms in the military gaming industry today.  When an enemy sees you, they have to either fire back, radio in or other people near your target in order to be detected.  All too many times in other games.. if you shoot and miss - the entire base is alerted. not in this game. if you shoot and miss, as long as you kill the target before he can take cover and call for backup - you are golden. nobody else knows you are there.

Jungle Warfare : I can't believe I hadn't done much research on this particular style of warfare, but it is realistic in this game.  Short wave radios, and sounds/sirens.  When you trip an alarm, the sound of the alarm carries to the nearby bases.  this explains why only a little amount of opposition comes your way and not an entire base.  QRF. Look it up!

Outfit Customization : This is probably one of my favorites.  As a person that enjoys immersing myself into a game - customizing my cammies is probably one of my favorite things to do. Desert Environment? Let's try some digital desert or chocolate-chip camo.  Jungle? Let's rock some long grass / leaves ghillie suites.  Winter?  Yep. there's a camo for that.

Vehicles : One complaint i "do" have about this game is the vehicles.  The selection is good, as you have vehicles ranging from a motorcycle, buggy, car, all the way up to a twin-engine plane.  That being said, however, the driving and flying with Mouse/Keyboard is HORRIFIC. I'd definitely recommend using your controller when flying or driving.  ANother point on vehicles is the scale is not accurate whatsoever, but that's ok. i'll let that one slide.

Story : As I was playing a mission - I started seeing that I was getting a little bit more tactical, a little bit more realistic and very close to the story line.  I started to know what our ghost team needed to do before we even made it to the next checkpoint.  Simply put; what your team is tasked to do doesn't seem very arbitrary. it's calculated and i think the writers of this game did a fantastic job.

Random Events : Now, i don't want to conflate this word "event" with what other people would consider some event, so let me just explain:  As I was footing it down the bolivian foothills, I happened upon a tiny encampment.  There were two enemies chilling and talking.  After I systematically neutralized my targets, i took a closer look.  There were medical supplies that you could tag, and some food parcels.  The makers of the game put these in there as a way to justify their presence there.  You wouldn't put two guys in this little camp without food or supplies.  It's the small things.

Multiplayer : I haven't played much multiplayer with "random" people, but I can tell you that I have the most fun in this game when I am playing with somebody that loves realism and tactics as much as me.  I have a buddy that I will sync shot, systematically take out stragglers, breach buildings with actual breach tactics, etc.  I can't sell this enough - such a FUN game when you have people that know what they are doing.  Like an "actual" ghost squad or a green beret.

Artificial Intelligence (NPCs) : To be fair, this is something that, in my opinion will never be mastered as humans are chaotic. No one move is the same. constantly changing.  One complaint i have on this game is the AI that you are given in Single Player.  Other than the sync shot, and reviving you when you are down - they are outright useless during stealth missions.  I recall assaulting a city.  I advanced, my squad followed.  I had crossed a street and took cover on a corner of a building and I get DETECTED. why?  My other squad members were crouching in the MIDDLE of the street.  Well done team. :|

All in all - this is a fantastic game and if you read this whole review - thanks for listening to my ramblings. Hopefully it helped you in a decision whether to or whether to not buy this game.

I enjoyed the time I did play the game. It wasn't anything special but was a somewhat fun waste of time and reminded me a lot of the old Ghost Recon games. I only played the game solo as I was testing it on on a free-play weekend.

A couple of quick impressions:

The AI for your squad is terrible - and even if I specifically directed my teammates to a location, they would often get lost so I'd run the mission "solo." I'm sure there's a sweet spot where I could micromanage their movement over very short distances, but the game isn't enjoyable enough on its own to put in that kind of effort. Nothing like having your team members complain about "unit cohesion" when they're wandering around aimlessly. Seriously - at one point two of my squad members got stuck trying to maneuver around the same post.

The AI on the enemy units isn't much better. You can roughly stand in plain sight facing three enemies, shoot two of them, and the third will be looking around, trying to figure out who shot them as you reload. I honestly did exactly this on more than one occasion. I also had a sniper attempt to repeatedly shoot me through a wall from a simulated distance of about three feet. Apparently the AI wasn't familiar with the concept of solid objects or switching away from your sniper rifle at close range.

The vehicle damage is just plain silly. It can best be described as driving around in a vehicle with a plywood frame. Drive too fast, hit a bump, and your vehicle is a pile of sticks - well, pretty beat up and churning out smoke.

Playing a member of an elite special ops team, I would assume that I could climb up a rock plateau that was approximately waist high. Apparently this wasn't covered in training. However, if I moved to a section that was a simulated six inches shorter, my character would figure out how to climb it.

I saw other reviews describe this as The Division without the bullet sponge feature (which was the entire reason I gave this game a try). It's not. I enjoy The Division (minus the bullet sponge stuff). This was pretty much the opposite. I don't believe I actually wounded an AI enemy the entire time I played - it was pretty much instant-death each time I shot them.

The graphics are very good. (The running water looks laughably bad but the rest of the game is well above average.) I actually paused a time or two in a rainstorm to watch the lightning.

However, the game crashed every time I went into the load out screen. This is kind of a big deal since one of the payoffs of the game is being able to customize your weapons and such. If it would have been a game that stood out from the pack I would have looked for a fix, but since it was barely average I uninstalled it. Wild ambitions vs. Ubisoft clichés: the game.

+The map is spectacularly large without lacking detail, content or variety. Truly one of the best open worlds around in terms of quantity-quality ratio.
+The gameplay manages to be mostly fun. Open gunfights aren't the best, but ideally you'll be playing stealthily most of the time. Enemy AI and overall mechanics strike a passable balance between realism and accessibility, making the game challenging but far from absurdly so.
+There's tons of stuff to do. Quantity-wise, this game has hours upon hours of content for the dedicated or completist player wishing to clear the map out, but even by rushing the main story as much as possible it lasts quite a while.
+The details are all there, graphically speaking the standard is pretty high and sounds are nice. There are some problems, though, as pointed below.
+While this is meant to be a co-op game, the AI teammates are overpowered enough to be of some use and make single player a possibility, at least.
+You kill a ton of named characters so obviously not all of them can stick in your mind, but the game does make an effort towards giving them some personality through collectibles and sometimes cutscenes. The main antagonist also has a decent personality, though it's not a shakespearian plot by any means.

-This co-op game somehow wasted time on a PvP... thing. Some might appreciate, I do not.
-Quantity is there, but while quality isn't always terribly low (though the open world leaves little room for scripted "spectacular" missions) variety is definitely so, the secondary missions in particular being terribly repetitive, if only for their sheer amount.
-The game kind of forces you to play without radar most of the time unless you want to stop leveling up for rewards (you hit the level cap of 30 for skills way too early). Kind of gratuitously dickish, if you ask me.
-For a supposedly realistic games, bullets sure drop way too hard on snipers, while bullet penetration is ridiculously low and sometimes you'll hit an invisible hitbox which will screw up your perfectly lined shot. And that's discounting all the usual slew of bugs you can expect (try exiting from a helicopter too fast when landing and you'll most likely fall through the map).
-While it's not exactly the focus of the game, one has to wonder why facial animation is so primitive. It kind of detracts from the cutscenes. The fact that some voice actors (female protagonist, I'm talking to you) seem to be phoning it in to absurd degrees. Two very unusual problems for a Ubi game.
-As mentioned before, points for trying and give your targets a name and history, but the story still is mostly forgettable. The plot is basic, the twists minimal, and the ending feels shallow. Nuff said.
-The DLCs are hardly worth their money, and aside from actual quality their progression is inexplicably disconnected from the main game (no Tier going up while playing those). One pumps up the difficulty at the expense of believability and internal coherence (and fun, incidentally), the other is just plain awful (of course, this being Narco Road).

So while i didn't exactly hate this game and I played it quite a while I still wouldn't recommend it to just anyone, you have to actually like the gameplay a lot for it to be worth your money.

How can I start this review? Well, I can say that few games compelled me to do everything. Ghost Recon: Wildlands was one of them.

I did all missions and got all kinds of collectables. It took me 76 hours that I barely felt. The different landscapes of Bolivia provide an excellent atmosphere to the game. Exploring the map never feels boring.

You have A LOT of freedom to complete missions and to customise your character, what gives even more possibilities. You can either go "Rambo style" or with stealth against your enemies, though I strongly advise the latter. Upgrade your drone first, and let the weapons skills for later. 

Aside from your drone, upgrade your stamina. It might seem useless at first glance, but in many situations you will need to literally run away. The last stamina upgrade gives you infinite stamina. And, of course, upgrade the skill that increases the number of AI mates that you can use to mark and execute enemies. About weapons skills, the most useful one are those that inflict more damage to vehicles and helicopters.

You can choose the order of provinces to beat. I encourage you to do the hardest ones first. Don't get scared: they are not much harder, the main difference is a heavier presence of Unidad helicopters and patrols. However, the best weapons are in such provinces, and getting them early in the game will help you a lot.

Game mechanics are great. You can mark enemies and your AI mates will finish them. The only problem is that you have to wait some seconds to do it again. You also don't need to go to a safehouse to change weapons. All your weapons are always available to choose.

You can go after the main boss after dealing with two of his four underbosses. Doing the campaign this way is shorter, but you won't regret beating all of them. Moreover, there is a different ending if you do everything.

Thinking about all that, I have no doubt: I will miss this game.

To start with, I'm going to open this review by saying it has been a LOOOOONG time since I played a game that got me marathoning it for a week straight.  From dragging myself out of bed, to dragging myself TO bed.  In the two to two and a half weeks I've owned it, I've put in about 130 hours.

But before I go from there, let me put in some caveats for those on the fence.  This game requires an online connection to operate through Ubisoft's Uplay network.  I find this feature annoying, but it's tied to the partial loot box system the game has built into it.  You are not required to utilize the loot crates to play the game, but you CAN spend real money to artificially speed up game progression.  

I find that mechanic eye-roll worthy.  All the main equipment in the game can be acquired through pickups placed in the world.  There are a few weapons that can only be acquired through the crates, but by the time you're fully kitted, they're little more than what I would consider reskins.  Yes, different stats, but there's nothing I can't do with a BFG-50 that I pretty much can't do with an HTI.  

That being said, let's move on to what the game shines in...

The absolutely colossal open world.

Starting with the game map, it's massive.  Coming from the BF1942 generation, the complete and open world game map that GR:W has makes stuff from the 2000s feel like a postage stamp.  But it's not just the size, but the unprecedented detail in the maps.  Jump into this game, and you are placed into a 400 square kilometer box in which the development team has seemingly managed to squeeze the entire array of earth biomes...  Except maybe sprawling grasslands.  But it has jungle, swamps, forests, mountains, deserts, canyons, and salt flats.  No regional load screens (just when you first load up, fast travel, or die/fail a mission and it resets you).

This massive world size allows the player to take the weapons, and use them at realistic ranges available to them.  If you like playing Sniper, then being able to pop enemies up to 600 meters away with a rifle in this game will make you giddy.  There is a caveat that enemies will despawn outside the 600 meter distance range, and the game only in-depth renders the area out to a km, but honestly, beyond that, long range marksmanship becomes a chore anyway.

Moving forward, this level of detail shows in other places that surprise.  From the various prone positions you can roll around in, to the correct kind of 'landing' animation your character goes through after jumping off a ledge, to enemies in mortar positions in the distance that can actually be SEEN going through a mortar-loading animation when they fire it.  These don't necessarily improve the fun of the gameplay itself, but it shows real polish for the title.  

Other elements of polish that I like are the enemy AI's behavior in a fight.  While the player's ghost squad AI might have others moaning about their poor decision skills, I honestly don't expect even the BEST AI to match the tactical movement of a player-operated character.  But the enemy AI honestly makes me smile.  Some of the AI flagging is cheesy, such as them instantly knowing what direction you took a shot from and instantly moving to flush you out, but again, the little details you don't expect pop out when you notice them for the first time.  Like the fact that the enemy does not merely take cover when fighting you, but that you can actually SUPPRESS the enemy by opening up on them even if you can't really score a hit.  In my years playing, I have never seen a combat game where suppressive fire actually makes enemies duck and hunker down in the middle of a fire fight.  Whether playing with your AI squad, or other players, this opens up new and interesting ways to drive a fight.

Moving back to the map, another unexpected but nice feature is climbing.  Most combat games give you the imfamous bunny-hop to get around vertical obstacles.  But here in GR:W, you don't get to mario jump or bunny hop.  Instead, the dev team has taken the time to go through the pain-staking process of mapping the character to a variety of stepping, scrambling, climbing, and vaulting motions to handle getting up and over all kinds of natural and man-made obstacles.  They then put the time and effort into making sure you can use these abilities just about everywhere on the map.  Simply put, if you can reach a ledge with your arms up, you can climb it.  This opens up all kinds of path ways in every environment on the already colossal map.  Enemy base on a cliff over looking the water?  Most other games would funnel you through a choke point and make the cliff one of those impassable boxes.  The ability to climb HERE allows you to scale that cliff and assault the base from the back.  

Details continue to impress, like the implementation of bullet drop, penetration factor against various surfaces, and even how much noise a weapon has with, and without its suppressor.  Or perhaps the various handling dynamics between different vehicles and their ability to drive on, and OFF the roads.  (Personally, on the ground, I like me a good dirt bike.  Handles well in turns, and offroads crazy well, going so far as to allow you some WICKED SICK jumps when you ramp right.)

There's so much more to praise the dev team at Ubisoft on this title for, that I could fill a small book.  Yeah, there are some drawbacks here and there, but nothing I would say should drive you to post hate about the game.  The AI ghost team could stand to be a LITTLE more intelligent...  Nothing quite like ordering them to 'open fire', only to watch them not only cover you by shooting enemies near you, but then to rush the choke point and get mowed down by a mounted weapon (derp!).  It would also be nice to see the 'render area' extend past 600 meters to something more like a 2 km range (to REALLY get those long range sniper rifles put to good use).  The reinforcement system for the enemies could also use some tweaking.  It makes sense to try and force the player to watch their back and stay undetected, but it puts pressure on them WAY too quickly.

Overall, this is a game to get, provided you're okay with handling UPlay.  130 hours of game marathoning, and I STILL haven't finished the missions or even fully explored every little outpost?  It's worth the money spent, never mind the nitpicks.  The positives and the attention to so much detail overwhelms a loot-crate system you can ignore anyway.

And finally, a special shout out to support for a fast response.  If you can be patient about a problem you encounter, and report it with clarity and detail, you can get even times when the devs missed something fixed.  Personal case?  I found one of the 'terrain holes' that hide on the map.  400 square kms of map and a colission box glitch the size of a single person standing is bound to pop up here and there.  I found one, reported its location using the GPS grid the game comes with, and it got passed to the dev team within three days.

Pros:

- Like most of other Ubisoft's games this looks outstanding graphically. Seriously, at some moments you just stop and  look at the that beautiful landscape - it's breathtaking, great foliage, clouds, building's textures, character and NPCs details are amazing.
- Day/night and weather cycle is one of the best I've seen in a PC game. And NPCs adapting to it too. During night enemies usually sleeping at their camps, excluding some patrolling guards, your squad is more difficult to spot.
- Sound is good, nice voice acting, great weapons sounds.
- Lots of different weapons to try out, plenty of attachments and throwable items. Assault rifles, SMGs, LMGs, sniper rifles, shotguns, grenades, C4, mines, flashbangs etc.
- Co-op is amazing, very fun to play with friends. I had great time attacking enemy bases and completing missions in co-op.
- Gameplay is okay but it could be better. Using strategy and planning your assault is really good in Wildlands. Using drone to spot enemies and sniping them from distance is my favourite part of this game.
- AI is okay, you can't run into enemy like some Rambo guy, you will instantly get shot and knocked out.  When enemies spot you, they will try to get to you from different angles, they'll use environment to cover, throw grenades to flush you out.
- Skill tree is okay, although it takes long time to max out every skill.

Cons: 

- Physics are pretty bad in this game. For instance, when helicopters gets shot in the air by RPG or any other rocket, most of the times it won't explode when hitting the ground, instead it'll fall down as some random piece of metal and only explode after awhile (even though it's full of fuel), it's very unrealistic. Also, you can't even jump, I lost the count how many type I got stuck under or between rocks when approaching enemy camp and I had to restart from last checkpoint because I couldn't jump out of it, simply because there's no option to jump, only to climb up on obstacles when game promts you command for that.
- Driving is hell in Wildlands. No matter where you drive - asphalt or off-road, it feels like you're driving on some plastic surface. Most vehicles seems very unstable and jumpy on any type of road, it's very easy to crash even at lower speed, that's very annoying.
- Friendly AI is garbage. When your character gets down, it takes forever until your AI teammates gets you up, even out of combat, they're moving trajectory is super dumb when sneaking into enemy camps, they constantly get spotted, and sync shot is very badly and unrealistically designed. No matter whether they can see enemies or not, they can snipe them through walls with sync shot, but apparently in close combat they can't even kill enemies that are 10 feet away from them.
- Bullet spongy enemies. When you stealth killing enemies, there no problem at all, most of the time you can one shot them with simple pistol in torso. But after they spot you, it takes 3-5 shots, sometimes 8-10 shots if enemy got armor, even with assault rifle. On the other hand, enemies (on higher difficulty) can put you down with 1-2 shots easy. That ruins realism for me. 
- Grind, grind and even more grind. You got 30 levels, lots of skill points and resources to gather. Skill points are easy to get, just get intel, travel to camp and get it or just level up. But after you get to level 30 you will be able to unlock tier system, you will be able to grind from tier 50 to tier 1, you will also get prestige credits to be able to buy prestige crates and unlock some random (mostly useless) stuff in-game. It's okay until around tier 33. After that, this game becomes cancer. I like challenging games, but in Wildlands "hard" won't be concept anymore, it will become your only reality in this game. As soon as enemies will spot you, enemies start flying and driving in from random locations, they will literally just spawn one squad after another, until you get out of that enemy base or camp. You will also need to get resources because with every tier enemies will become stronger so you have to upgrade your weapon's damage and you're gonna have to grind a lot, doing same thing over and over again. And this is already became a trend in gaming, especially in Ubisoft's games. And this is total bullsh**t if you ask me. 
- Microtransactions. Like in most new games you can become god in the very beginning of the game. Just buy resources, skill points, weapons, weapon's attachments, vehicles etc with real world money and you're good to go :)
Ubisoft's doing great job again - milking hell out of this game with MTX.
- Some glitches and bugs like I mentioned before - stuck between/under rocks, some random death when falling undermap because of glitch, not being able to attach suppressors on weapons etc.

I'm doing my second playthrough solo right now and still enjoying it most of the time. I just think Ubisoft should make all in-game stuff available for all, just by playing game, without this stupid microtransactions nonsense. All weapons, all vehicles, everything should unlockable by playing or be given as rewards. But no, it's to difficult for Ubisoft. They have to lock most of in game items under paywall - some items can only be acquired by buying spec ops or ghost war crates. Of course you can grind for hours for some items but is it worth it? Once, I had to grind for 8 hours straight just to get 2 items, yeah that was really fun...

Right now I'm just trying to not pay too much attention to it, I'm playing with Tier system disabled. Still, this product is one of few newer games that actually gave me lots of fun and entertaining moments, and actually made me play it more than once, so I think I have to give this game thumbs up. Just bear in mind that this is not typical old school Ghost Recon game, this product only got GR tag on it, but it's nothing like classical GR 1.

Esse game é muito legal quando jogado em Stealth, e só. Quando tentado em modo Loud, fica tudo uma bosta e explicarei o porquê: A inteligência artificial desse jogo é uma porquisse sem fim, então ela não corresponde de forma realista ao modo Loud. 

  Exemplo: Quando eu estava no meio de um matagal na montanha, com as roupas camufladas com as cores do ambiente, e eu matei um cara que estava muito longe de mim sem supressor, o colega dele viu o corpo morto e me detectou - veja que ele não me detectou pelo estampido do tiro  mas por ver o parceiro morto - e após ele perceber o cadáver, fiquei com o nível de detecção: ''caçados'', que quer dizer que os nossos inimigos sabem que estamos por ali e estão vindo em nossa direção, mas não nos viram, tudo normal até aí, daí fui matando todos eles até que os reforços chegaram, e aí que a put4ria aconteceu: o carro de reforços chegou pela rua e simplesmente começou a me detectar instantaneamente e começou a me metralhar através de uma grossa camada de matagal que estava entre eu e o veículo, algo que é impossível, uma vez que eles acabaram de chegar na zona de combate e só poderiam ter uma noção de onde estávamos por meio de comunicação entre os combatentes que já estavam na área, mas saber exatamente o local em que eu estava deitado.... isso já é mais conhecido como AIMBOT, fora os caras segurando duas MAC-10's e atirando de 100 metros sem errar 1 tiro, sendo que ele atira em hipfire e nem faz a mira... ou o combatente que anda com uma PKM e atira com ela pelo hipfire também e acerta tudo de uma distância imensa.

  Outro exemplo aconteceu ontem: Estava eu destruindo submarinos do cartel, os quais eram usados para levar drogas para outros países, e o cenário dessa parte da história é em uma floresta densa e pantanosa, com muitos matos envolta dos rios como Taboas, que são plantas que nascem em uma grande densidade, e lama, tornando tudo muito fácil de se esconder. Entretanto, quando fui destruir um desses submarinos comecei a trocar tiro com os combatentes do cartel, até aí está normal, mas foi em um momento em que eu saí de todo o cover e fiquei enfiado no meio de um monte de Taboa e continuei tomando tiros com precisão de alguém que eu mesmo não conseguia enxergar por causa da densidade do mato que estava entre eu e ele! Os meus parceiros AIMBOTS tiveram que matar ele, pois qualquer ser humano não conseguiria ver por meio daquele mato.

   Basta tentar jogar online e verá que é quase impossível acertar um alvo enquanto seu colega dirige o carro em curvas fechadas e desviando de obstáculos, mas para a inteligência artificial isso não é problema, eles atiram um laser de chumbo até você, mesmo que o veículo dele esteja fazendo a curva mais fechada do mundo. O mesmo vale para helicópteros.

  Podemos concluir, portanto, que tentar jogar esse jogo como um jogo tático em modo Loud é impossível, você terá que apelar para usar os seus colegas com a AI zoada para ficar te salvando, pois eles são tão cheaters quanto os inimigos, entretanto eu zerei o jogo pela primeira vez no STEALTH e achei divertidíssimo, pois o STEALTH não ativa o modo combate dos inimigos, e é exatamente esse modo combate que deixa eles cheatados.

[h1]BUYER'S GUIDE to Ghost Recon Wildlands.[/h1]
-- ONLY BUY THIS GAME [b]ON SALE[/b] --

Solo and Co-Op is where this game shines. When it's on sale for only about $20 that's what I feel is the only fair price for this game. The AI is complete trash and so long as you're using silencers and calling shots intelligently... The AI really isn't that challenging even on the hardest difficulty. The Gun Customization, RPG-lite Skill Tree Mechanics, and the Open World itself are the highlights of this game. I genuinely enjoyed traversing the map they created here; it has pretty much every biome imaginable and the day/night cycle can really make you feel like Special Ops. I just wish the AI was better. Your squadmates will do things like crawl two-feet from an enemy and it just... breaks the immersion. The world itself is gorgeous but the NPCs that inhabit it are pretty devoid and lifeless. 

What this game does do extremely well is the combat itself. Guns are quick and snappy. Bullets drop over distance. The automatic cover system is surprisingly smooth and intelligent. The best part (and the reason I enjoy this game far more than The Division)... ENEMIES ARE [b]NOT[/b] BULLET SPONGES!

As for the Expansions ---
Year One is complete trash. The two DLC "Campaigns" are super short and forgettable; not even close to as lengthy as the Main Campaign (although they expect you to shell out a Main Game's worth of $$$ for it).

Year Two so far is a little bit more interesting... Ghost Mode is pretty cool but I just don't think it's worth $30. To be fair, I only bought Year Two for the Splinter Cell Campaign but it's really not even worth it for that.

In my opinion... You do not need the Expansions. A lot of it is just wasted on the Multiplayer PVP that's not even the highlight of this game. Seriously, if you want a PVP Experience then I'd highly recommend playing Rainbow Six Siege instead.

Another reason this game is only worth $20 is the miles of DLC. Save your money upfront and that way you can spend the other $30 on skins, cosmetics, and guns assuming that is your prerogative. This is not a bad game by any means, which is why I'm recommending it, but it is simply not worth more than $20 - $30.

In Ghost Recon: Wildlands, you take over the leader of a team of ghosts as they travel to an unstable Bolivia during the summer of 2019. The South American country has become a narco state, producing more cocaine than any other nation in the world. The U.S. aren't terribly interested in any of it until one of its embassies in La Paz, a region within Bolivia, is bombed, and one of their embedded agents, Ricky Sanderval, is found dead. In comes the world's deadliest unit no one but us gamers have ever heard of: the ghosts - Paragraph Taken From IGN

The only times you really get a glimpse of the story is through videos uploaded to you from your operation boss, Karen Bowman. These videos are visually appealing, but are lacking in compelling storytelling. In spots you will be reminded of why you're in Bolivia and why the cartel must be stopped, but the main story failed to deliver in keeping me hooked in caring for it or anyone in the game but one, which I will address shortly. 

Most of the story is better told through the innumerable amounts of collectibles found throughout the map. Whether it's Santa Muerte shrines, historic locations in the mountainsides or random documents scattered around cartel edifices, reading through these definitely gave me more valuable and interesting information than any of the videos of cartel members did.

Outside of these cartel members, there is one person you will learn more about as you carry on with the game: Sanderval, the agent killed in action. His side of the story should be compelling, and without spoiling anything, the information you get from collectibles that detail the beginning and end of the late CIA operative are actually brilliant and add a twist to the procedurals.

Now, that last word is probably the most damning criticism I have of this game; procedural. The amount of content in this game isn't bad at all, there's quite a lot to do. The issue is many of this content is rehashed across the map. The collectibles are understandable, but the repeated side quests are incomprehensible.

These side quests consist of quick 5-10 minute operations that either help you upgrade you and your squadmates or the rebel support you can call in. The issue with the former is that there are literally only two types of cache-involved sidequests: helicopter deliveries or plane deliveries. Both are fun the first few times, raiding a makeshift helipad or airstrip and flying said aircraft to the rebels, but quickly become repetitive. Worst are the latter of the quests. The upgrade branches can be maxed out, but even after you do so, the quests continue to pop up with no real use. They're repetitive to the point where I could only do one region a day or else I would have nearly died from boredom.

Luckily, my interest was held together by the game's vast environments of snow-capped mountains, vegetation-stuffed forests and rolling hills. It's a beautiful game.

The gameplay is great, with the vast array of weapons all feeling weighted and full of oomph. I enjoyed trying out all the dozens of guns. The customization we all liked in Future Soldier makes a great return, with hundreds of possible customization patterns available just to one gun. So if you're a gun nut, this game might trip your trigger.

I got GR:WL on sale for $20 and can confidently say this is a complete title worth the price point. The world is enormous, open, beautiful, and rich. Combat is fun and satisfying. The narrative is surprisingly good. It's clear that Ubisoft took their time getting this one right and doing justice to a loved, long-standing franchise. 

Customization is extensive. You control a ton of aspects of your weapons and character. Some of it comes across as loot box store-bought ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but you can unlock most of the content just by exploring the world, and that you're not actually supposed to pay anything unless you want a shortcut. There's a store, but this game is not pay2win. 

Playing alone is fun, precise, punishing, and rewarding. There is a certain open-world freedom that Wildlands completely nails, where every mission can be completed any way I want. Whether I'm stalking through foliage trying to find the perfect angle for a simultaneous triple-takedown on a group of enemies, or kicking the front door down guns-blazing, every play style feels like I'm playing the game "correctly." They really designed it so you can do whatever you want. As you level up you unlock new abilities that allow you to solve problems differently. 

Multiplayer with random people has almost always deteriorated to chaos, zipping around in high-level helos from mission to mission in a sort of speedrun-esque fashion, but the multiplayer experience is a great one; playing with other players is entertaining and everyone online has been fun, supportive, and positive even after I tell them I'm new and clueless. I recently botched a mission we'd all spent 10 minutes setting up, and even though everyone knew I was the one who screwed it up, nobody cared. They simply educated me what to do next time and we moved on. It reminded me of how chill people were in Borderlands 1. I imagine more structured multiplayer at the highest difficulty would be a different experience entirely.

Negatives from my play time so far have been few. A couple of unexplained crashes. The "im specops, stay frosty" cringey voice lines that come out of the characters from time to time. Sometimes driving cars and flying feels a bit janky and J-RPG-y.

- Smart shooting. Bullet drop, stealth and firing modes. Think First Blood not Rambo 3. 
- Large selection of vehicles (land, air and sea) and gear (UAVs, mortars, C4), that add real options.
- Hunt and kill your way up the Cartel hierarchy. Taking down bosses is satisfying.
- Big lush south american map, with lots to do.
- Great weapon progression and customization.
- Seamless coop integration. Squad of AI if playing solo, much like old games.

Cons:
- Limited enemy variety.
- Tedious resource grind (optional).
- Complex pay system -- one spreadsheet is not enough.
- Microtransactions. The best clothes and guns cannot be attained without them (even if you have season pass).
- Some really annoying bugs.
- Uplay

Verdict:
A great free-roaming tactical shooter, if you are able to stomach the Ubisoft parasite. If you're tired of the grind of loot&shooters, and like the idea of a bullet being deadly -- I whole heatedly recommend this title.
