Unplayable broken garbage.  The game was released unfinished, over half of it is locked behind micro transactions and forgotten about by ubisoft.  As a long time fan of ghost recon, the franchise is as dead to me as ubisoft.

Despite the fact that this game epitomises all the problems with Ubisoft's open world formula that it seems to apply to just about every game it makes, I’ve had an absolute blast playing Ghost Recon in co-op with some buddies.  

Part of that comes from the fact that, when you pop the difficulty up on high, it can be challenging, and even though it is repetitive ad nauseum, there’s just something really enjoyable and repayable about scoping out an enemy base, forming a wee strategy and pulling it off, especially when enemies will mow you down pretty quickly if you’re seen.  Its even more fun when said strategy goes balls up and you’re stranded in the middle of a base, surrounded by enemy fire, desperately trying to get to that chopper to escape, leaving your friend behind to die as he takes out the anti-air missiles. 

There’s also a ridiculous amount of fun to be had in just how bad the game can be, whether that’s the awful driving controls, weird glitches, getting run over by civilians in the middle of a fire fight, or just doing silly stuff like driving around on tractors or parachuting out of a helicopter when your mate hasn't the parachute unlocked yet. At the same time,. taking on a unidad base in a tougher province can be a legit test of skill and strategy, and hella fun to boot. It doesn’t hurt that the game overall is very pretty, shooting mechanics are solid, and the weather and lighting effects are very atmospheric.  

This game is literally 15 times bigger than it needs to be, and I doubt I’ll even come close to finishing it, but when played in moderation with friends, its so much fun.  It also helps that you can drop in for a mission and then drop out after 20 to 30 mins.

As for playing single player, meh its boring; the story is bland and forgettable and your AI buddies are crap.  I wouldn’t even think about it unless you have someone to play with. 

It's a shame, though, that the devs didn't scale back on the sheer bloat of this game and spend more time adding mission variety or writing a complex and engaging narrative. However, playing with a friend or two is just pure unadulterated fun, but remember that you're going to have to make a lot of that fun for yourself.

I don't feel like writing a very long review and there are many things that could be said about this game. All in all it is very fun, that is hard to deny and it does many things right, including allowing very good customization of HUD so I will recommend it as it is a very fun game. I just feel it is a shame at the same time that Ubisoft seems to pump out games in such a rapid succession that their games while being very impressive in scope never really reaches that master piece level like games from Rockstar etc. That last polish that would be needed to make it feel like these games are really made with a passion behind it, instead of this kind of souless factory style vibe you get from many of their games these days. Quantity over quality is one word that often feels kind of appropriate, since there is an insane amounts of repeating style of  "tasks" to do as in many of Ubisofts games. 

Besides the very many bugs there are so many parts that feels so incredible stupid and overlocked that further give this impression of a "factory made" game. Some examples are how the game have the same repeated dialogue over and over again when entering a new territory. This is extremely annoying and feels cheap and stupid, especially when you have just played a game like Red Dead Redemption 2 where the developers actually try to make the world and characters feel like real people and not robots that repeat the same style of dialogue over and over again. 

Also the writing and characters are horrible and gives vibes of the developers trying to be edgy and hip, but just ends up being embarrassing. I get vibes of looking at an E3 show when playing this game and watching how the hosts thinks they are cool on stage while in actuality being at maximum cringe level. To have writing and performance more in the style of the Sicario movies would maybe be to much to ask, but a fraction of that kind of quality would make things so much better. It is possible to make shady spaced out characters though if done right, the Hitman games is a good example. 

Also the game seems to have a bit of an identity crisis at times, wedging between realism and arcade. I play on the extreme setting and it can be brutal and you often get killed without even seeing the enemy first. But at the same time there is no way to move bodies and bodies just seem to disappear after they are killed like in some arcade shooter. The game also does a good job of always reminding you that it is a game by having your guys spawn in your helicopter after you leave them behind or when you call for a transport it is just spawned out of thin air (even though it is just spawned though the game does a horrible job at actually spawning it in a good place for you, often you have to run a long way and sometimes it even spawnes the ride inside an enemy base)

The game is very pretty though and the weapons feel great with bullet drop and it is very fun to play. It is just a shame that there are so many things that are just overlooked.

Edit: After numerous more crashes that freeze up the whole computer, numerous bugs and incredible stupid design choices I just can't give this the thumbs up anymore. I get the same feeling from this game like if you got a really nice car that was very pretty, but the manufacturer decided to place a stinking turd in the back seat and not bother removing it because of a calculated business decision that it would cost to much and their revenue would be higher by just releasing the car with the turd intact. This is like a really fine car that is very enjoyable to drive for the most part as long as you don't get that turd in your face which will happen from time to time.

Summary: It’s quite hard to tell what’s larger here – the map that Ubisoft made, or the in-game store they plonked on top of it? 

I'll start positively. Ubisoft can make a sandbox, and Wildlands is probably the best constructed sandbox I’ve played (albeit the cities and the cartel bases do start to feel very, very cut and paste half way through the game. Likewise, the ability to customise your team is also a welcome experience. It’d get mighty tedious playing with the same look of operative the entire way through what is a massive world of game play.

Unfortunately, that’s also where I must leave happy land. Some of the basic complaints:

AI in the game is dumb, but have we ever met a good smart AI?

Driving (only something game devs have worked on since the beginning of gaming) is hopeless.

Half way through the game you get the feeling that the writers got bored of the game or just ran out of ideas for a narco state – it’s clear that there are some characters and regions that have been developed more than others, and those less thought through have a story line akin to 4 people arrive on a budget airline for a stopover for a day or two in a place adjacent to something interesting to blow up some drug minions dreams and then kill them before actually jetting off to Hawaii for their actual holiday. I know no one else is probably asking for this, but I’d like to have seen some sort of post murder bit in each region where our four trained killers put on their USAID bibs and rebuild a local post-narco economy. That’ll probably be another 100 DLC. It’s also come to my attention that every sandbox rebel group (farcry is also subject to this complaint) is a complete stereotype of what we think locals would be carrying around a couple of AK47s. Seriously, rebel development needs an up-tick. Likewise, for a game that market’s itself on realism, the cartel could be slightly more realistic. There’s some interesting themes and stories in the cartel, but their lost amongst some of the stupidity of the narco state.

Why I don’t recommend this game however is because of the massive cash extraction operation Ubisoft attempted to set up in the game. I bought this game for 75 dollars a year after release when it came out at AAA full price. What you quickly discover is that the game is a “service game,” and the really unnecessary multiplayer acting as an excuse to pedal constant in game purchases to make your character better. This is in addition to the loot boxes, and the absolutely insane amount of money it costs to purchase things in game. It would be ok if five real world dollars bought you a million hats in game, but a hat can cost you 30 Australian dollars! Additionally, the game also plugs a series of expansion packs (which are acceptable of a game) but also yearly passes, which might make sense for a game like Rainbow Six, but are ridiculous here. Also here are loot creates, and I know what you're thinking by now - it must be a game about special forces because they are using a special amount of force to get you to shill more and more cash into the game. It’s sad because the game has these great missions where you see other characters from the Ubisoft universe, but they feel really tacky and even a bit sleezy when you can then purchase them. It’s quite hard to tell what’s larger here – the map that Ubisoft made, or the store they plonked on top of it? You can say if you don’t like it don’t buy things in the game and just play vanilla, but the ad on purchase options actively soil the experience. 

Buy it on sale, at quite a discount. They’ll most likely get their money anyway.

I haven't played previous Ghost Recons, so I started this game with no expectations from previous games. DEA Agent was murdered, so Ghosts went to Bolivia to avenge him and bring down a cocaine cartel, with help of local resistance. It's done by slowly eliminating key figures in four key areas of cartel operations: Production, Security, Influence and Smuggling. Each branch has a few "Buchons" (no idea what plural is), an underboss which can be taken down as soon as only two Buchons remain, and branch boss which can be eliminated once everyone else is dealt with. Upon eliminating enough bosses, an option to eliminate cartel leader is unlocked. 
Each Buchon has their own province - area with a few points of interest, and various collectibles scattered around - from weapons and weapon mods, through medals giving few skill points (player character and squad can be improved via skills system - they require some skill points and supplies) and enchanting previously unlocked skills, to "Kingslayer Files" - lore pieces containing information about cartel and Bolivia. 
Story missions often revolve around "abduct", "intercept", "eliminate", "destroy", "find info" - but personally, i haven't gotten bored yet. Choosing approach to mission is mostly left to player, save for necessity of killing some buchons, and capturing others alive. Asking yourself questions like: "Should I land further away and try to quietly abduct enemy, and risk longer walk under fire, or land close and shoot my way in and out" can be fun.
Something about bad design decisions. Enemy soldiers can surrender. Yet you can't arrest them, and they won't leave the cartel when you tell them to, so only logical decision is neutralisation. Still, if you kill enough surrendering enemies in quick succession, you will have to start again from nearest safe area. Entire idea seems kinda pointless. Also, identity of some buchons is unknown upon entering the province, and is discovered when doing story missions. However, you can learn their identity earlier from Kingslayer files - however, he will still be regarded as unknown when talking with your handler. 
Also, not really a design problem, but map is big - travelling without a heli is pain. Moreover, when recovering supply planes and helicopters, I sometimes had to fly through 2 provinces to reach nearest rebel-held airfield - and SAMs are watching.
I spent 72 hours in game so far, prioritising collecting items from provinces before completing missions there, and stopped doing Rebel Ops as soon as I reached max level of the Rebel skill they were improving (eg. diversions, mortar fire or vehicle delivery) - they got boring rather quickly. And for reasons stated earlier, i rarely recover supply aircrafts.
I havent played previous Ghost Recons - but i played this one and it's fun

The first game in the past 15 years that I actually look forward to playing instead of just something to kill time.
Keep learning new things that make it clear just how close to perfect this type of game is, a few examples that really impressed me.

[list]
[*]  Seamless Co-op, where people (friends or public, depending on your choice) can join/leave without breaking the flow - if people join they replace your AI team and when they leave the AI comes back.
[*] People who join your co-op match your level, so no people are too OP than the others
[*] Most weapons are roughly the same, there are no OP weapons that break gameplay but you can get addons and level them (in Teir mode), but overall the weapons you start with could easily see you through the entire game - changing weapons is more just about what suits your gameplay/experience best (eg. sniper rifle that can shoot with rifle rate vs sniper rifle that can one-shot vehicles).
[*] Add/remove silencers from weapons without having to go into menus, can easily switch from stealth to full assault as the gameplay requires without breaking the flow.
[*] Difficult changes doesn't just make the enemies bullet sponges, it does things like removing your mini-map, not highlighting enemies, etc.
[*] Weather system... once you experience a lighting storm, with rain at, night while roaming through the jungle approaching an enemy outpost. I challange anyone not to have a bit of a nerdgasm.
[*] Familiar yet different, many people compare this to Far Cry and similiar open world games, and yes, there are similiarities however that just meant I could easily jump into the parallel world Bosnia without having to learn a brand new set of mechanics but it was different enough that it didnt just seem like a re-skin - primarily, this is heavily focused on stealth.
[*] Outposts/enemies respawn after revisting - at first, this annoyed me... a lot. I felt a lot of my work was just pointless, taking over an entire base to only realise that going back to it and all the enemies are back. This is my favourite part now, the fact I can revist my favourite areas numerous times means seemingly endless re-play value.
[*] Stealth orientated gameplay, but not too punishing if you want to just go in guns blazing.
[*] Micro-transactions, cannot get anything that you can't get within the game itself (or at least of equal value), ie. you can can cosmetic things and different skins for vehicles - I'm a big hater of micro-transactions, but this game shows that it can work, you don't need to get them but if you are a fan of the game you probably will, but you get quite a lot for what you pay and seems like a good way for appreciative fans to 'give a tip' to the devs, which if anything should be all additional micro-transactions should be, P2W or needing to pay to stay competitve (or even complete!) a game is where it is shady.
[*] Predator level, enough said!
[*] Llama bike, something everyone needs in their life.
[*] 'Cheat-level' gameplay, at first I was unsure of this as some things did seem to be a gameplay killer but turned out to be a great way to remove the annoyances of open world games without having to use them but the option to use them: spawn a vehicle anywhere (inc. chopper), call in rebal reinforcements, call in mortar strikes, drone to spot enemies, remotely explosive drone, rebel spotting that spots all enemies in an area you choose, AI with 'magic shots' that never miss and never draw attention (if they do, you did something wrong...), if you die, the AI will clear enemies around you and then revive you (even if completely surrounded), change difficulting level on-the-fly.

I played the original Ghost Recon excessivly but didn't follow the series after the LAN-days were over, but GR will be on my insta-buy list for all future games in the series now.

Overall this has been the most unexpectedly impressive game in recent years, I'm not a fan of war-type games or even shooters in general, I've played too many over the years that they all seem the same and forget them after I complete them but Wildlands is a masterpiece.

one of the most underrated games I have ever encountered. To be clear, this game is a visual and mechanical masterpiece. It functions perfectly at every level by offering an absolutely gorgeous and varied open world for you to execute combat strategy as you see fit. This game rewards slow, surgical approaches to planning and tactic, but will not punish you if this isn't your style. Instead, game world itself responds to aggressive gameplay in kind by sending reinforcements. 

The gunplay is tactile, visceral, and challenging.  You can lie in wait - half a kilometer into the desert - for the perfect shot to line up. At higher difficulties the AI is cunning and relentless. You will be sent crawling into ravines as death squads hunt you down. 

Do yourself a favor and forego the multiplayer components. Play this in single player, on ghost mode, with simulation difficulty. Immerse yourself in the lore and the mists of the jungle. Let the lethality and danger of every firefight drive this game to the intensity it should be played at.

Ghost Recon Wildlands offers some of the best cooperative Player-vs-Environment gameplay I've ever experienced. It has a diversity of mission types such as material asset defense, intelligence operations, convoy attacks, rescue operations, interrogations (very basic), resource "aquisition" (read: stealing vehicles full of stuff), etc. 

The players have the freedom to choose how to approach a given mission. Stealth and more high octane options are available. There's an ample supply of vehicles such as the UH-6/AH-6(AKA Little Bird Helicopter), an LAV(rare), and other armored and unarmored military, and civilian vehicles. The player is encouraged to approach a given situation in any way they like given their available resources. For example, my buddy and I completed a difficult asset defense operation using close air support from a Little Bird when we had trouble fighting off attackers on the ground.

The game also features a wide variety of hand-held assets: firearms, grenades, mines, C4, and a drone for advance scouting of enemy positions. It also allows customization of the player avatar. There is a micro transaction system which allows players to purchase cosmetic changes for their avatar.

The story can be completely ignored with no consequences to the gameplay.

Wildlands has its issues but I think the good outweighs the bad. Graphically it’s one of the best-looking games on the market at the moment, almost photorealistic at times. The draw distance is amazing, flying in a helicopter and seeing trees, roads, and towns kilometers away is great and it makes the game world feel massive in scope which it already is but it’s nice to actually be able to see how big it is physically without things popping in from the distance. The game has the Ubisoft formula where the map is cluttered with all kinds of things to extend the length of the game and it’s to a massive extent in this game because the map is so huge. There is an abundance of side missions, upgrades, and collectibles in each area/region of the map-making this a really long game. A lot of the game is collecting weapons and weapon mods, skill points, and doing side missions which make the game feel like its on autopilot mode at times but because I played in the coop it lessened that feel quite a bit because we often found our own way to keep the game fun. I think this is a really good coop game because there is a lot of ways to cooperate and play the game together like the way you approach missions together or the way you navigate around the world together. The game also has that unpredictability and randomness feeling that open-world games often do which leads to a lot of fun, weird and unscripted moments. 

I think the gameplay is pretty good overall, the shooting feels great, headshotting feels great, especially with a sniper, and syncing shots together with your coop mates is awesome. The game feels really satisfying when you complete a mission in stealth but it’s also fun to just go loud at times and I love the amount of equipment and customization that’s available. The vehicles feel and handle pretty good, the animations are good but the transitions between first and third person and changing between the two when aiming can take a while to get used to, and even when you are used to it it’s not exactly a smooth tradition because you have to aim down the sights first before you can change perspective and then once you do you have to check if you have to change the shoulder position of your character, doing this while in a gunfight can feel pretty clunky.

I like how challenging the game is overall and how relentless the enemy ai is but there are times where the bulls*it meter goes up like an enemy having perfect accuracy from a hundred meters away while dual-wielding uzi’s. We started saying ‘I got lasered at times when we got downed because sometimes the enemy feels like it's shooting lasers at you that can’t miss, it can get pretty annoying. Overall if you’re looking for a coop game to play with the boys this is one worth playing through and one that you can spend a lot of hours in. 
7/10

Overall, this was a very expansive game with 100+ story missions, and plenty of open world and side missions.  The sheer expanse was more than I expected, and I've been playing AAA open world games for a very long time.  Yes, there was about as much repetition as any other open world map.. the necessary game parts to get you grinding and upgrading, but beyond that there was a very long story line, many characters, and unique locales.  The only part I really didn't like was that very few weapons were an actual improvement without purchasing something, but I generally was able to keep a couple favorites that did the job.  Not perfect, but not bad at all if you get it under the twenty dollar mark.

EDIT: I use to give this a game a thumbs down due to the RTX graphics card inventory issue, but that was fixed so as promised I did change my review... Due to the fix I do definitely recommend getting this game on sale if possible and definitely do find a group to play with.

The Bad:

- Gore? It doesn't exist. You can pop a cartel members head open with a sniper up on a hill and what's the remains? A "blood spot" that looks like someone accidentally spilt food coloring on the kitchen counter... It's really underwhelming.
- Microtransactions that exist for weapons skins that are unobtainable through normal gameplay.
-Repetitiveness exists. If you do nothing out of the ordinary I can see how this would get boring quickly.
-In singleplayer Teammates basically exist for either reviving you and sync-shot.
- Besides dirtbikes, I'm going to give the driving mechanics a "LOL" rating.
- Having to go through Uplay.

The Good:

+ Dirtbikes = re-envisioned Skyrim horse
+ Co-Op can be incredibly fun
+ Overall gameplay is fluid, and relatively easy to use.
+ Holy $%^& is the game BEAUTIFUL. I play at 1440p on Ultra settings and the scenary is absolutely stunning.
+ Stealth gameplay and sneaking around makes me feel like a kid in a candy shop.
+ Customization. Holy crap Batman is the customization awesome. You can customize your character anyway you wish to make you look and feel like a total badass. You can also customize your weapons down to the paint on each part thanks to the cool gunsmith.
+ Did I mention the game is pretty?
+ The map is HUGE. Absolutely massive with diverse scenery across the map. You are NOT allowed to complain about load times in this game (I'm running this on a separate 1TB 7200RPM HDD from the OS and realistically it's not that bad).


Conclusion:

Overall, the game can be fun. Playing by yourself can be underwhelming and sometimes boring, but if you squad up the game can be pretty dang fun. So far I've loved sneaking around, scouting out an enemy base, and slowly picking off enemies to interrogate the target, or flying in a heli at night and parachuting into a hot zone with friends and calling in a mortar from rebel allies. I would pick up the game at a discounted price like I did (I paid roughly $17-$18 from 2018 Winter Sale), and would not pay full price. If you and your friends are looking for a fun new game to play this is the one to play and I do recommend it if you're into tactical third person shooters.

1. You Don't Own the Game (Section 1.1)

    The Language: "THIS PRODUCT IS LICENSED TO YOU, NOT SOLD."

    The Issue: This is the foundation for "digital vanishing." Since you only have a license, Ubisoft claims the right to revoke your access at any time. If they shut down the servers or lose a music license, they can legally take the game away from your library, even if you paid full price.

2. The Mandatory Arbitration & Class Action Waiver (Section 10.4.2)

    The Language: "...you waive any right to participate as a member of a class in a class action... claims must be brought in the parties' individual capacity."

    The Issue: This is the "lawsuit killer." If Ubisoft does something that harms 1,000,000 players (like a data breach or selling a broken product), those players cannot band together to sue. Every single person must go through private arbitration individually. Because arbitration costs for a $70 game are higher than the refund itself, most people simply give up.

So: Ghost Recon Wildlands, aka War on Terror Simulator 2017. This game is, as far as I know, the ONLY real option when it comes to mutliplayer tactical 3rd person combat. It's kinda like MGSV except with the ability to hang with your bros, and a little bit more tonally consistent.

Synopsis: You roll around in a squad of 1-to-4 people and commit genocide against columbians for the crime of wearing wife-beaters in public. Great for scratching that 'Most Dangerous Game' itch that battle royales do so well, except without all the drawbacks of playing a battle royale. Great for roleplay as a spec-ops trooper, complete with the ability to customize your guy/gal to look like basically anyone, with any gear imaginable.

Overall, my experience with this game has been amazingly positive. The various difficulties are well-balanced to appeal to someone of basically any FPS experience, the world looks great, and between the ridiculous, saints-row-esque driving mechanics and the tendancy of enemies to spawn every 25 feet, along with the massively varied terrain, this is an open world game that doesn't struggle nearly as hard with "dead time" as most others I've played. The map is utilized to its fullest extent, as well - the few open areas of nothing still serve a purpose in some way, shape or form, even if that's just making a potential shortcut completely ridiculous to try and attempt.

That said, the game DOES need to be played with friends, and it DOES need to be played tactically to be enjoyed. Playing solo, the game sticks you with an annoying-ass AI team you can't turn off. Playing with randoms, you're probably either going to die every few minutes, or run over everything in the goofiest way possible. The game shines best when taking a slow, methodical, more roleplay-ish approach - identifying enemies, strategizing approaches, and working in tandem with your buds to cut down bad guys as quietly and methodically as possible.

My only real qualms with the game lie in limitations of the formula more than anything else. After a few dozen hours, you start to realize that there are only a few guns really worth using - the only real variety in your firepower is in the magazine size and effective range, and outside of the few best-ofs, "weapon variety" generally means "mediocre in slightly different ways."

Additionally, although the game provides a wonderfully refreshing, unrestricted freedom in how you approach basically any scenario, with very few (if any) mandated approaches to any encounter, the game could do for some more creative gadgetry to help you exploit that freedom to its fullest extent. Using the current selection of grenades, mines and other misc. doodads typically feels suboptimal for most scenarios.

Finally, like all Ubisoft open worlds, the game does tend to drag on a bit towards the end. Although the varied environments help keep things interesting, there is a point around halfway (25-30 hours) where you start to realize you've seen it all. In hindsight, I do wish that the developers had chosen to cut about the last 4th of the game away and instead use those resources to concentrate the remainder.

That all said, this is hands-down one of the best tactical shooters of the past 5-10 years, and the best tactical co-op experience I can remember. Would recommend to anyone looking for a good time with a pal.

there are plenty of positive things to say about this game. And those things can be found in other positive reviews. Most of those things are true. And they are true enough reasons to play the game. But it is the other miriad of small annoying things that compound together that in the end made me just straight up say "ya. i am not gonna play this after the main campaign"

So if you are fine with all the following, I guess you could enjoy this game

~Meaningless weapon customisation
save for magazine size, suppressor and scope, all other attachments just affect the stats of the weapons. More damage, longer range, more handling. All of them with tiny increments that if you really think about, it doesnt change the way you use the gun. The only real gamechanger is the grenade launcher.
~Meaningless weapon upgrade
In Tier Mode, you can upgrade your weapons but only the damage. But that honestly exists because the enemies have increased health. There are no other upgrade options. So why have that option at all? Why not keep the enemy health the same?
~Inconsistent environment effects
Some guns can shoot through brick walls. Some cant. Thats fine. But sometimes even the ones that can shoot through brick walls cannot shoot through sheet metal. Or a certain tree branch. Or a different brick wall. Or this plastic barrel. Or this bush. Sometimes you cant shoot through chainlink fences and sometimes you can. Ive read that this is somehow linked to having suppressors on. Really? It doesnt really matter because ive had instances where that doesnt affect it either way. And I found things that look like chainlink fence that just act as a solid wall and will NEVER let anything through. Bushes are worse because sometimes you cant shoot throught them AND you cant see what you are shooting at. Also they seem to not obscure enemy sight.
~Basejumping
To basejump, you need to need to sprint off the edge while holding down the climb button. while you are in freefall, if you press forward you dive stright down. So what happens when you sprint off the edge is that you dive straight down to your death because you were holding down the forward key and didnt let go of it immediately when you jumped off. 
~Vehicle damage
Vehicles take damage from everything. They take double damage from being shot in the tires. They take half damage from shooting the windows. Either case, they can be triggered to explode if you have depleted the vehicle health enough.  Helicopter I am riding in can be brought down if  a drone runs into the propeller. APCs can explode just from being shot with assault rifles. 
~Vehicle weapons
Generally awful. Helicopter has trouble aiming, especially the missile. The minigun hits but seem to do as much damage as a normal gun. The APC autocannon has trouble aiming lower which isnt helped by the fact that the turret is placed high. All the mounted minigun has the player's camera zoomed in way too much. There is no peripherla vision. All of these weapons are outmatched by simply using the passenger's own weapons. 
~Artificial Difficulty
In higher difficulties, the enemies simply take longer to kill, they do more damage and they find you faster. there is nothing else. nothing changes. no new enemies. enemy ai doesnt get smarter. just the same enemies youve been fighting the whole game. but now that dual uzi narco can kill you from 100m away. 
~No defensive options
No rolling from cover to cover. Not any sort of fast movement options while staying low. No ability to quickly go to prone. No ability to quickly get up from prone. No armor. No shield. Flashbang doesnt work sometimes. 
~Slow awkward animations
The player character is not nimble. Everything takes forever to play out the animations. You just get gunned down while playing out the animation to get out of the car or get in the car. Can jump out of the car but goes to a rolling animation that is about as slow. Prone related animations are also very slow. You can never duck or go to prone fast enough to dodge incoming fire. Also needs to play out the animation after being revived. Vaulting over low walls also painfully slow.
~Awful mission designs
Sporadic checkpoint system meaning that you are going to listen to that same NPC dialogue numerous times if you fail the mission. No option to skip the dialgoue. Gameplay sequences where long stealth sequence is punctuated by an action sequence but the checkpoint is at the beginning of the stealth sequence. Some missions where you HAVE to play as the designers have dictated. No freedom, no creativity. And other times, it's a gameplay sequence where you kill waves and waves of enemies, a thing that is thematically nonsense and also is completely boring.

I've played Ghost Recon Wildlands for near 150 hours at the time of writing this review, and I can say that it is definitely a must buy for those who like a more casual spin on combat sims. Ghost Recon Wildlands underpins its intriguing story about a Bolivian Cartel led by a nihilist with a god complex through superb customisation, both cosmetically and practically, along with an in-depth breathtaking environment which never fails to impress. Like some of my other reviews, I like to outline pros and cons then summarise them nicely at the end on why they justify a recommendation. So lets get into it!

Pros - This part lists the positives of the game and parts which I felt highlighted this game's ability to shine.
- Graphics are very well done.
- Environment boasts diversity and looks stunning!
- Codex and journal entries about Bolivian folklore, legends and history. (I found lots of it very fascinating)
- Process of dismantling a cartel seems well thought out and logical. 
- Customisation (Weapons) Weapons can be customised in such a way to suit a variety of playstyles. 
- Customisation (Cosmetics) You can customise what you wear throughout the game, some of which offers benefits such as the Optical Camouflage backpack, or the Predator Biomask offering infrared vision which is arguably better than thermal. 
- Adding side missions. Mainly nods to other Ubisoft titles, but I loved the Predator. 
- Kidnap people and put them in the boot of your car...

Cons - This is where we look at where the game falls short and feels somewhat like a missed opportunity in my own opinion. 
- Lack of air and sea vehicles, somewhat too much emphasis on land. Detracted from the environment diversity in some ways. 
- Loot boxes, no matter what these will always be a negative, this really took something away from the progression in the game and I felt that maybe cosmetics and weapons unlocked in these could have definitely contributed to the end game. 
- With a game like this where some missions require stealth or to be done in a certain way, multiplayer with randoms is not a good idea, best just to do them with AI teammates then go to multiplayer when you're not doing anything. 
- Terrible end game, get all the perks, complete the tier system, finish the campaign and you're done. I felt there really wasn't much to work towards. There definitely lacked some incentives to playing the tier system. (The tier system is a level up process which begins after you have finished the normal levels).
- DLC wasn't all that good either, just re-used content, with different enemies and more people to kill. 
- Changes to the environment based on your progress through dismantling the cartel and taking on the Unidad paramilitary were pretty much nonexistent. 

Summary - Overall I felt this deserved a recommendation as I felt the environment it drops you into with the turmoil, fear mongering and even civilian attitudes towards CIA operatives made it feel very alive and makes for great role playing! If anybody remembers the Crackdown games, which much like Half-Life, we will never see a third, reminds me of this. It is definitely worth picking up if you enjoy the idea of being one of the four most dangerous people alive, three of which are on your team.

Cons:

- Driving is baddddddd, very slow, and feels like an after thought. It quickly becomes replaced with flying. 
- Lack of controller customizations (when playing on PC)
- Not optimized (only uses about 60%-70% of my CPU, 90% on one GFX card and 50-60% on the other) and I only get around an average of 60FPS on low settings. WHY IS THIS A THING!? You're telling me that 2 years since the game launch with dual (overclocked) 1080ti's in SLI that they can't handle your game at 1440p on LOW? Please.
- Way too repetitive too soon (while fun for a few hours, it wears thin pretty quickly).
- Large map (see below)
- Mission bugs
- "Do not be detected" missions. Super boring, super annoying, and super linear gameplay that forces you to play a certain way. I don't know why some sandbox games love adding in these lack-luster missions, as if it somehow adds more difficultly. They don't. They're dull and should be canned immediately (this caused me to uninstall the game because I had to do one and immediately do another right after). 

Other thoughts: 
This game is a smash of Assassian's Creed, Just Cause, and a hint of Ghost Recon in one. Unfortunately, it doesn't work very well in the larger gameplay scheme. AC and JC are known for being grindy and repetitive, but then you combine the two, and it becomes super grindy (not in the fun way).

As of writing this review, there are still bugs that affect missions (side and main). For example, it'll partially unload the mission if you're a bit too far from the immediate area. Wildlands is a phenomenal game with a decent story, outstanding gameplay, and a very well thought out late-game progression system. If you want a good "tactical" shooter that can be played with friends and has some of the best graphics on the market right now then Wildlands is for you. 
If you are looking for a game with more than surface level content, look elsewhere. The PVP is stale and dry with combat being repetitive and overall lacking in design. The "bosses" have no real challenge as they fall just as easily as any other enemy lacking any real flair or challenge. I killed once boss by grabbing a .50cal and sniping him from outside the entire base, waited until the enemies died down, then completed the mission without breaking a sweat. Turns out it was supposed to be a high-octance fight, sometimes railroads can be helpful. 

Overall, this game gets a solid 7.5/10 for me. It has everythign I want out of a game but a good PvP system, which is honestly a very minor complaint.

Microtransactions and anti-consumer practices coupled with a Dev team that has no passion for the realism or authenticity make this a relatively hard title to recommend.

The core gameplay is competent but lacks any amount of serious tactical depth. It's missing core components that add to a realistic tac-shooter - minimal squad commands, cosmetic only customization, non-dynamic campaign or enemy AI.

It's "Freedom" is meaningless...your actions have NO weight in the game world - the trailers fabricated it. All mission outcomes and objectives are Scripted...you just choose whether you shoot your way in or sneak in. If you've played any of the Far Cry games, you've played Wildlands.

I've sunk 300+ hours into the game - mostly because I roleplay (as much as the game allows) and spend a ♥♥♥♥ ton of time playing Barbie with the customization available (Which is admittedly cool). But do not let it be an indicator of how much I like the game...I've often spent hours on a title which isn't much fun, but I tinker around in it...so it's a personal idiosyncracy.

Do not purchase this game. I'd recommend you wait for a serious price drop next year....and even then, the obnoxious monetization practices in the game do not deserve your time or money.

This game is kinda like if rainbow six / splinter cell (blacklist not chaos theory) had a baby with grand theft auto. 
Really neat open world with two main different enemy factions, and you can run and gun or stealth every scenario that you find yourself in. The open world adds a whole different layer of tactical fun, as you have the ability to approach any area you're about to infiltrate from any side, and if things get too hot you have lots of bolivian forests, buildings, vehicles, etc. to run off to and hide in. 

The weapons system isn't perfect in the way that it isn't true to life, but the customization is fun and unlocking items in the different areas of the massive map of bolivia really adds a fun element and a reason to play. 

There's an ability tree with lots of unlocks that add extra skills and items for your character to use, and none of it is pay to win which is a massive plus and almost a surprise in 2018. 

They teamed up with 5.11, so if you're into tacti-cool stuff IRL they might have some of your real gear to deck your character out in. 

The in game purchases are for the most part aesthetic and are in no way necessary, which is a very welcome bonus after playing stuff like siege where they force you into it. I'm very welcoming of this kind of purchase model, but even more welcome is the fact that there are less purchaseable items than items you have already or get by playing, and on top of that a lot of the purchaseable items are really dumb looking IMO which really provides no incentive to buy them. 

If it's on sale and you're into tom clancy games, buy it. You won't be disappointed.

[u][b]Pros:[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Good open-world design and size. Immersive environment from the start.
[*] Possibility of configure the desired gameplay style (from Hardcore with practically no HUD to something more Arcade).
[*] Varied character, inventory, and weapon part customization.
[*] With friends and good communication, it greatly enhances the immersion, and you can lose yourself in the game for hours.
[*] Configurable allied AI if one day you decide to continue the single-player campaign.
[*] For Side-Mission Hunters, the content guarantees many hours of gameplay, with nice surprises from other franchises.
[*] I highly praise the intention of bringing an arcade tactical style to an open world with an easy learning curve. The influence of ArmA is noticeable in certain aspects, and the idea of ​​bringing it to a less tense and complex setting, like a MilSim, is welcomed. If there's one feature to remember Wildlands by, it's this one.
[/list]

[u][b]Cons:[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Within a few hours, the repetitive pattern of the missions becomes apparent.
[*] Ubisoft. Not only because of what this company and its reputation represents with micro transactions and bloated menus in its games, but it also forces you to launch the Uplay launcher every time you run it from Steam.
[*] Sometimes, the immersion can be broken by the cheap lore of the missions; at times, the antagonists are bizarre stereotypes, and I wonder why it's named after Tom Clancy. Definitely don't play it for the story.
[*] The enemy AI is somewhat broken in one respect: when your presence or someone in your squad is detected, the entire settlement/facility immediately telepathically knows the location. It breaks the logic, but I recommend using it as an extra difficulty level to emphasize stealth.
[/list]

[h1]Decision:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Overall, recommended. It's worth the purchase, and if you get it on sale, it's a great value for money/hours of entertainment.
[/list]

I am big fan of Ghost Recon since the series started. And in all fairness Wildlands is a bit different than the previous games. First of all Wildlands is played in 3rd person, but as soon as you zoom in it switches to 1st person. Second, the game offers a huge open playing field without any loading screens. The setting looks amazing and for me the game runs so smooth (despite having an older pc). The single player story is really good and keep you playing for a lot of hours. You can also do side quests to unlock weapons and attachments. You can play full guns blazing or stealthy. It's all up to you. Really good is that you can play the campaign also with friends or other players at any time. 

In Wildlands you can also play Ghost War, a 4 vs 4 multiplayer game. You pick your specialized soldier and battle against other players on nice maps. I play a lot of Rainbow Six Siege and Ghost War is a very nice addition to that. You can see where they got their inspiration when they created Ghost War.

The only negative thing about this game are the season passes. They offer way too less for the price that you have to pay for it. So just buy the normal game and enjoy! 

See you on the battlefield!

Ghost Recon: Wildlands  is one extensive open world game. If you thought Grand Theft Auto 5 was the mother of all open world games, then this is even bigger, if not the biggest currently. The game developer, Ubisoft, has managed to get the environment spot on whether it’s the mountains, jungles, swamplands, desert, small rundown towns, salt flats or lakeside resorts. The graphics are so realistic that you feel that Ubisoft has managed to recreate a Bolivia of their own.

PvP mode is called Ghost War  It plays out as a third-person, 4v4 tactical team deathmatch, where you only get one life per match (unless a teammate is able to revive you) in best-of-three games.

Team deathmatch sounds like a really simple mode, but each game in Ghost War feels tactical and plays differently than the match before it. Matches often play out slowly, and you might find yourself going prone in tall grass on several occasions to listen for enemy footsteps. The maps are pretty open with varied terrain, so you might have some close-quarter combat inside buildings or long range fights across desert or jungle biomes.

It's a must-have game if you're a Ghost Recon fan or a shooter.

The thick, detailed foliage is a treat, and the lighting, shadows and occasional weather effects look gorgeous, and most importantly: very realistic.
A GTX 1080 is pushed to its knees even in 1080p with everything dialed up. I kinda look forward to spinning up this game again in a couple of years, when I get a faster graphics card, to look at it in its actual, full splendor.

Gameplay is enjoyable too, of course. Nice opportunities for sniping and entertaining stealth mechanics. 8/10, would recommend.
The game is regularly on sale for 20€, and is easily worth the price of admission.

Edit: Steam Awards 2019 has come around, and yep; this game is still good.

There's a way to play this game incorrectly. By rushing into every enemy outpost guns blazing you're limiting the experience that you can get. The absolute best way to play this game is by taking your time. Tag your enemies, take them out sneaky beaky like. The main storyline is very forgettable but you'll have a good time with the open world.

Story: Weak. You'll be hunting down and killing cartel members so you can hunt down this one bald guy. Not that the story matters in this kind of game anyway!

Vehicles: Oh boy. The driving physics are hilarious! Cars feel like they're constantly floating and sometimes you'll crash with your bike and fly 50 meters forward. Helicopters are pretty great though.

Sounds: The voice acting is hilariously bad. Your character will scream "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥!" on the brink of death. Very emotional. Also the weapon sounds aren't very impactful but the silencers make each gun sound pretty cool.

Graphics: Actually a very nice looking game if you play on the highest graphics! The open world is very detailed which you can truly appreciate.

Repetition: I, for one, don't find this game that repetitive. If you rush through every mission with the same weapons and with no strategy whatsoever, then yes, you'll find yourself irritated fast. Change your loadout, customize your character, USE THE DRONE. Utilize all the different things the game offers to you, please!

Overall: Wildlands is a game that stealth fans will like. The game isn't really meant for aggressive rushing. There are no unique mechanics that'll make this game special but when you take out an enemy outpost without anyone realizing, you'll feel like you've really accomplished what the game aims for in the first place.

Different title, same old Ubisoft. My review is completely on solo play only because I cannot find anyone to play with online. Maybe its my region so I cannot comment much on the co-op part.

Wildlands puts into a remote country where it is governed or ruled by some really bad guy. This particular bad buy has lots of ally/lieutenant and also happen to have bought off the police, leaving a "handful" of locals trying rebel against the bad guys and you are there to help. Sounds exiting? Lets continue shall we. 

The world/map is huge and they are divided into sub areas. Each of these areas are pretty similar and your mission is to lure the supposed person-in-charge out and dispose of them. In order to do so, you need to complete a number of mission. These missions are relatively the same. Sneak or go gun banging in and do/kill/grab something/someone. Then in each area are also some some side quests, well the same side quests like defend an area, flip some switchs, kill someone or steal some vehicle. These are always the same in each area. 

Your character has tonnes of arsenal in your dispose and you are always accompanied by 3 other A.I. They are quite useful in a way as they cannot be detected by the enemies and you can even upgrade them to be more lethal or mark enemies for them to take out simultaneously. Of course, best of all, they never seem to be able to fall in battle, run out of ammo and revive you when you fell.

While steering or piloting a vehicle, your companies are the only attack options as you cannot shoot while driving with the attack copter as an exception. Its the only vehicle you can pilot and attack at the same time. There is a plethora of guns around this time. Each gun is customizable except for the unique variant which comes equipt already with certain parts. Weapons and attachment parts can be unlocked by progressing through the game, completing certain quests, finding collectibles or buying cases through in-game store. Yes, microtransaction exists and you can also purchase certain boosts to add some edge to your game.

Weapons works pretty great in Wildlands. You can feel the difference when handling each weapon and they don't feel so plasticky. Ultimately, you will feel like trying different weapons and find those that you prefer most. Wildlands also has bullet drop so those long range combat is a little more fun.

Enemy A.I. also seem to get an upgrade. At close or far range, they can be quite a threat be cause they take cover pretty well now but most of the time its because their quantity can be overwhelming. 

The open world, at first glance is quite beautiful. Lush vegetation, mountains of jungle and islands. You have villages, enemy bases and towns all around. You also have fixed enemy spawns in certain locations and fortified enemy areas. But, these areas are bare minimal. There is nothing much to do and the buildings are all similar including the collectibles locations. You can find 2 exact same building in 2 similar locations and surroundings. Civilians randomly spawns to make places feel populated and livelier but mostly, they just seem to be zombified A.I. and don't do or react much. There are no animals except for some birds flying around so forget hunting. Not sure if that is a good or bad thing in a Ubisoft game.

The game currency is depicted to be food, salvageable parts, medical supplies and oil rather than actually currency. You can find these things lying around in game. Collecting them allows you to purchase upgrades in addition skill points earned. You will find escorted trucks that you can rob from the enemies. The spawn is random but the location and route is always fixed. They can prove to be a challenge at first but once you find out the way, then it is always the tactic.

That covers Wildlands mostly. Go to a an area, kill a bunch of enemies the way you prefer it. Do some quest and collect some stuff and proceed to the next area and repeat the same thing all over. In order to unlock the locations of collectibles in the map and also missions, you need to interrogate an enemy leader or pick up some intel. You always need to do this 5 times to completely unlock all locations and missions. Best part is, these person/intel are always in the same place. I picked up an intel, quits the game and logon again and the item is right at the same location again.

Wildlands can be fun even when playing solo. Gun fights can be tough. Sneaking and clearing enemy bases can be satisfying but unfortunately, doing the same things over and over without much rewards and just for the sake of progressing the story can be tiring when the story itself is plain, barren and simply. You don't even get introduced to your companions yet alone knowing their story. So much for bonding. 

Vehicles handling is one of the biggest part the game can improve. To be honest, they handle like vehicles in GTA: Vice City. Because you cannot shoot while driving, ultimately, the first thing you do when logging in is finding an attack copter.

Wildlands feels a lot like a white washed Ubisoft game. Wrap with a different paper, tweak it a little and you get this but after you unwrap the paper, it becomes a disappointment quickly.

I disagree with this game being originally advertised as a very multiplayer focused game. Yes, it is enjoyable with multiplayer, but I played the story solo with just me and the three AI you get in your squad and I thoroughly enjoyed it.

The squad AI: The squad AI is actually very good. Occasionally, yes, they can do dumb things when in hectic situations, but overall they are tactical and easily controlled with the in-game orders you can give them.

Enemy AI: The enemy AI is very believable. If you miss a shot from a surpressed weapon, they hear it go past them, and if you aren't quick enough they will shout out and alert everyone else, instead of like in some games where they investigate on their own like idiots.

Enemy Characters: The characters within the cartel are believable, whether they are deluded by the Cartel's religion or in it for the money. If you kidnap someone to interrogate, there isn't any of the ♥♥♥♥ in action films where a simple mercenary will be tortured beyond belief before giving intel. You put a gun to their head and they take it seriously. Death is taken seriously and I definitely appreciate that. Gives it a more realistic feel.

The story: I personally loved the story. It's a very realistic situation with realistic characters done in a fun and tactical way. It is very satisfying working your way through the cartel, ruining their smuggling, security, influence and production wings and seeing it fall apart piece by piece. 

The Stealth: Very fun and very easy to ♥♥♥♥ up, which I liked. It meant you had to think more of what you were doing so that you wouldn't be seen or heard.

All around, a very very good game that i had a tonne of fun with, though it is a little pricey due to it being under the Tom Clancy franchise. If on sale, 100% buy it.

REVIEW >>>>> I've really enjoyed this game: it's the best looking game I've played. Bolivia is stunning. The varied provinces, and dynamic weather and day cycle create unique visuals, and the feeling that you're actually there. 

The gameplay is what you expect from a ghost game: you approach a mission area, scout out enemy defenses, and choose how you wish to engage, whether it's stealh, ambush, or full on assault, and you're given a fair amount of tools to do this. The varied geography, enemy bases, encampments, and mission objectives make for interesting play. Also, the open world is great for CO-OP. It's the kind of shooter I used to fantasize about playing when I was a younger.

Also, you're given a lot of options for customizing your avatar, which is a fun little bonus I didn't expect. Makes your avatar really feel like yours.
 
There are problems, but overall it is a good experience; similar, yet different, to MGSV. I hope they make a sequel to this game set in a different location.

COMPLAINT >>>> The micro transactions are really obnoxious: for example, I completed a sidequest to unlock a bigger clip size for my assault rifle, only to find out that it doesn't actually unlock until I spend $15 on the "assault rifle clip package." You're given a clip size of 20 to start, and in order to get "medium" (30 bullets), and "large" (50), you have to spend a significant amount of real money on such a little thing. And that's just for assault rifle clips. You also have to buy the clip packages for other types of weapons if you want them. While this isn't game breaking, it is REALLY petty, and gives an advantage to players at higher difficulties. I hope gamers will refuse to indulge this kind of money grubbing by not spending in the store.

I enjoyed this game. I can see why a lot of people didn't. It's repetitive, simplistic, the AI is terrible, the game can be buggy/glitchy, and the world overall seems a little dead and scripted. Despite all that I enjoyed playing the game for an hour or so between doing other things, racking up almost 70 hours when I completed all the missions. I liked the huge range of customisable weapons. I liked choosing different loadouts for my different play styles. I enjoyed the Predator mission which thereafter gave me the creeps whenever I walked into a jungle. I liked trying to be stealthy then have something go wrong, and have to shoot my way out. 

Ultimately, if they put out future games like this I would keep buying them.

That being said I did buy it on sale for $23 so that's ~33 cents per hour of gameplay - this probably skews my overall view. Had I have paid full price I might have been disappointed by the fundamental weaknesses such as the weak AI and repetitive missions.


Improvements wishlist 

Stronger AI: rebels would be standing around with cartel members and soldiers and not be shooting one another even though we are in the middle of a shootout. AI-Squad members constantly getting hit by trains. Rebels won't free other rebels who are locked up in cages in enemy bases while we're storming said bases - they rely on me to do it.

Enemy mechanics: enemies seem to spot you from far away and have pinpoint accuracy, even with heavy machine guns. 

World seems dead: I'm not saying it has to be GTA V, but it's hard not to compare it to GTA V, a game which you can drive around and just explore the world and watch events unfold between NPCs. Wildlands has nothing like that - it's a beautiful world that you just rush through, either trying to get to a place, or trying to complete a mission.

Missions: more variety. The side/rebel missions being the same convoy tag etc are great and I wouldn't necessarily change these as they're fun and they provide quick side quests when you don't have much time to do an actual mission (though they could add some variety such as convoy destroy, rather than tag). The main missions do need more variety, and not just in what the objectives are (kill/destroy/take/follow etc), but the actual content of the mission and layout. There is certainly some variety but it feels a little cookie-cutter by the end of it. It was fun going through underground facilities or through mansions but there just wasn't enough of these different missions. I think of games like Hitman, where you're following a target through a crowd of civilians and, sure, you can kill the target and his henchmen in front of everyone and risk killing civilians, or you can choose to follow him to a secluded spot, or engage in some kind of distraction. Wildlands doesn't need to be that technical, but there are all kinds of other games the designers could have drawn inspiration from and they didn't. 

Vehicle variety: vehicle models were limited (and people NPCs too for that matter). There was only one type of supercar, a handful of trucks and vans, sedans, 3 differnt helicopters (albeit with different weapons loadouts), a couple of different bikes. Would have been nice to have more variety. Also, this mighting be asking a bit much, but I would have liked to customise my own car and helicopter - they could have added more grind-missions for the player to accumulate points to then spend on vehicle upgrades. (in all honesty though with Bolivia the way it was depicted with long winding roads and an overall crappy driving experience offroad - I stuck to helicopters to get around whenever I could and never drove cars - planes were horrible, bikes were an okay to dash over mountains to get to missions).

Again, despite all this I did thoroughly enjoy the game and recommend it.

Its fun at first, an open world, lots of missions, some simple progression and unlocks. Best part? Its multiplayer, so naturally you get your friends together and have some fun. Unfortunately this game comes with the training wheels bolted on, the target demographic in terms of difficulty for this is most likely kids in the regions of 8 to 15 in age. The content is closer to that of 16 at least. Issue?

So here are the default training wheels:
Enemy clouds - basically you always know the approximate area an enemy is in.
Grenade, missile warnings, enemy markers - everything that poses a slight remote threat to you is highlighted with audio, flashes and clearly marked on the map or your hud.

All of the above can be changed with some tweaking to the options, also these settings are not server enforced. So its entirely possible to have a friend or random join your squad with all of these enabled and effectively be Rambo while the rest of you look like the bob the builder.

Here are the bolted on training wheels:
Ammo abundance - Literally, why does some peasent have enough ammo stashed away in their bedroom that could sort out US ammo needs for the next 10 years?

Health regeneration - Take a shot and within 3 seconds youre back at full hp.

Zero weapon scaling - you may as well run around with the first gun you get. Actually just use the assault rifle and a sniper. Once you have the under barrel grenade launcher you can cover ever conceivable situation this game will ever throw at you. You get this attachment within the first hour of playing the game. So effectively it takes you one hour to get all useful unlocks, not bad.

Infinite bleedtime - You take a lot of damage, fall on the ground and wait till your friends come revive you. You can stay in this bleeding out state forever. So if you need to go have supper, watch a movie, finish your degree there is no stress, your character will faithfully bleed out for as long as he needs to.

Infinite revives - So you hit the ground, bleed out for an hour, get revived, hit the ground, bleed out hour, revive, ground....

Personal Gripes I have with it:
One of the selling points of this game is the massive landmass. Unfortunately this doesnt mean much when almost every third peasent village in this game owns their own helicopter capable of traversing the area within 5 minutes. You can also unlock the ability to spawn a helicopter eventually. Or you can just teleport to where you need to go.

The AI is really stupid for 2018 standards, this would have maybe impressed me when I played CS 1 or Doom 1 back in the 90's. They also have perfect night vision, so lighting means pretty much nothing. 

Hardest difficulty is really just a theme, kind of like changing the background on your Desktop. I mean its really still the same, things just look different.

So here is how I managed to make this game remotely challenging in single player and somewhat live up to the standards of 00's ghost recons.
Turn off all training wheels in the hud as far as possible.
Turn off all enemy audio (they like to tell you when they are coming to stab you, kind of like a general disclaimer)
Turn off all bots (they are gods for some reason)
Highest difficulty.
No under barrel grenade launcher.
No drone.
Selectively choose from talents in the tree (to ensure you dont become a god).

OK so do I recommend this?
For some people, yes: 
If you are highly stressed or just want something to kill 30 mins every other day, great purchase. Its always easy and is very non-commital.
If you are bad at Dota (or games in general) and want to feel like you are winning for a change then yes (totally not the reason i still play this).
Want something simple to play with your kids that is probably not age appropriate? Yea totally, I think...

Otherwise no.

He loved his job. Driving a train had been his dream ever since he was a child. He loved to make the train go as fast as possible. Unfortunately, one day he was a little too reckless and caused a crash. He made it out, but a single person died. Well, needless to say, he went to court over this incident. He was found guilty, and was sentenced to death by electrocution. When the day of the execution came, he requested a single banana as his last meal. After eating the banana, he was strapped into the electric chair. The switch was flown, sparks flew, and smoke filled the air - but nothing happened. The man was perfectly fine.


Well, at the time, there was an old Bulgarian law that said a failed execution was a sign of divine intervention, so the man was allowed to go free. Somehow, he managed to get his old job back driving the train. Having not learned his lesson at all, he went right back to driving the train with reckless abandon. Once again, he caused a train to crash, this time killing two people. The trial went much the same as the first, resulting in a sentence of execution. For his final meal, the man requested two bananas. After eating the bananas, he was strapped into the electric chair. The switch was thrown, sparks flew, smoke filled the room - and the man was once again unharmed.


Well, this of course meant that he was free to go. And once again, he somehow managed to get his old job back. To what should have been the surprise of no one, he crashed yet another train and killed three people. And so he once again found himself being sentenced to death. On the day of his execution, he requested his final meal: three bananas.


"You know what? No," said the executioner. "I've had it with you and your stupid bananas and walking out of here unharmed. I'm not giving you a thing to eat; we're strapping you in and doing this now." Well, it was against protocol, but the man was strapped in to the electric chair without a last meal. The switch was pulled, sparks flew, smoke filled the room - and the man was still unharmed. The executioner was speechless.


The man looked at the executioner and said, "Oh, the bananas had nothing to do with it. I'm just a bad conductor."

So, after 241 hours of gameplay, I can say that I really enjoy this game. 8/10

PROS
- Extraordinary beautiful landscape. It's a pleasure to play all the time.
- Really large and diverse map. Everything from jungle to snowy mountains. Awesome!
- Lots to do. Even if some missions are a little samey it's a lot of fun in this game
- The sneaking is even more fun and exciting than it is in the Hitman-series :) 
- The gunplay is fun and easy and intuitive (but not as good as for example Arma, when it comes to long distance sniping)
- Lots of vehicles to use (which have to be there on a large map like this)
- The synced shots with your fellow ghosts are really satisfying.
- I think that 241 hours is like my 4:th most played game ever and that must mean something.
- I like that there are several very different difficulties, because that gives you a lot of options how to play the game.

CONS
- Extremely repetitive dialogue (both the bad guys, the secarios and the santa blanca, and the ghosts). At first the dialogue is fine, but when you are scouting your seventy-fifth base and hear the AI using the same phrases and bits of dialogue you are pretty fed up.
-Missions starting without you wanting them to start (worst of them all is that Sam Fisher-mission, which also have a really annoying dialogue when you hear it for the tenth time).
- The weapons are mostly potatoshooters. Ballistics and bullet drop are rediculous. A sniper rifle has bullet drop after 150-200 meters in this game. In reality you can fire an AK at twice the distance with no or very little drop. It would be really fun in this game if you could pull off long shots, but the AI is not even visible (or spawns) at long distances. Also canvas and camo netting is often bullet proof in this game.
- If or when you are detected everyone in the whole world and their grandma knows where you are. And I mean exactly where you are. And they will spare no costs in finding you. :)

I'm gonna give it to you easy: this is a game you should get on sale. While not worth full-price, it's still worth playing. Despite the kinds of negative reviews I've read, don't let them bother you.
For starters, yes, there is a weird issue where this game can crash unexpectedly. Luckily, this game has a frequent autosave feature, along with checkpoints in the missions to help alleviate this problem. And for note, if you're looking for a game that's beautiful and runs well, play this game on low or medium graphics. (Somehow, this game runs better on my gaming laptop while on medium settings than Mirror's Edge on the lowest graphics).
But the gameplay is another story. It has a lot of things going for it. The cover system feels natural, and the overall gameplay feels like it had been set up to support whatever playstyle you preffer. Keep in mind, though, the game itself has an overall gameplay feeling of "go here, kill some guys, beat the boss, move on and repeat." The story is present throughout the game, and is revealed through files collected and videos given to you by Sueno and Bowman. Overall, though, the story just felt like The Division's; minimal character development, a mostly absent antagonist and the only way to progress is to trek across the map and do a bunch of seemingly tedious tasks before reaching the boss of the area and moving on. And there are two ways to play this: do the simple method and just chase down the final boss and only get collectibles that are in your path. Or, you can do the hard way and collect everything then take on the buchon.
The characters are mostly unmemorable, aside from Sueno and a few of the Buchons. The rest don't really have a personality, aside from just "antagonist."
All in all, this game is pretty good. Getting it on sale is likely the best option, considering how it doesn't have much appeal to it. The bright side is that you can go at your own pace and accomplish things in your own way, in any order you want. That said, I'm willing to give it a 7/10. Maybe 7.5.

I really wanted to like this game. I truly did. 

To be fair to it, I want to point out what I think is great about the game, and understand, I do only have a few hours on the game. That said- I have enough gripe with it to be almost certain I wont play it much ever again.

The Good: The game is gritty, very tactical, has good stealth AI and when it comes to strategy based shooters that are live and not turn based, it does this fairly well.

The Bad: The game has serious programming issues. I have experienced crashes, stuttering, freezes that last 10 seconds (in a gunfight), and other issues. One would think, upgrade hardware, update drivers, check for computer issues... but in hundreds of games, this is literally the only one giving me issues of this degree. Upon research, it isn't hardware related. In other words, I have a great graphics card, sufficient RAM, and processing... it doesn't care.

The combat is clunky. It plays only in third person (I dislike this immensely in shooters), and while it isn't my preference, games like Mass Effect and Gears did this really well. There is no cover button. You frequently take cover facing the wrong direction, and although there is a button to face the other way, you will turn around randomly while aiming and see wall. Lazy.

Control: Fail.

Sound design is really good. 

The world map is huge. Cool. 

The graphics are great.

The story is.... well... acceptable. 

Overall the game didn't feel like it took itself seriously. At all. The leveling system is lazy and not inspiring. 

It feels like this game wanted to shoot like gears, but failed to match it even 50%. It wanted to be a completionist open world like Assassin's Creed, but doesn't satisfy or make you feel like there is much point. 

It wants to be a stealth game, but fails to appease as its control scheme and lack of flush, clear controls makes me only focused on that most of the time. 

I really wanted to enjoy this game with my friend, as he recommended it, but frankly? Save yourself the trouble and frustration. There are 100 better shooters, 100 better stealth games, 100 better open world games, 100 better games for immersion, and a game as clunky as Dark Souls better impress me with its direction and immersion. It didn't at all.

This game doesn't deserve much of the negativity in the reviews. The whining about the loot boxes is particularly surprising since they're a feature of practically every major title nowadays. In Wildlands they're mostly there to incentivise progressing in the relatively new permadeath mode called Ghost Mode. Yes you can straight up buy items in loot boxes using real money but if you just play the game then there's no need.

As for the complaints about it being repetitive, well I'm honestly not sure what those people expected? Every single game nowadays is repetitive, that's what genres are all about. What did you expect to find here anyway, a cocaine farming simulator? A management sim? Come on. Wildlands is a tactical shooter and there is bundles of that to be had here. If having a huge arsenal of weapons and vehicles available to you to tackle any mission anywhere on the map at any time using your own strategy is repetitive to you then you are not the target audience here.

If you want the items available in the new loot boxes then it's quite simple - just play through on Ghost Mode and activate Tier 1 mode when it becomes available. You'll get so many credits that you'll soon unlock most of the better equipment anyway all for free.

Hmm... where do i even start. Beautiful graphics, environment, atmosphere, they're almost perfect. Though nothing is perfect.  The story was meh and i didn't really follow into it that much, but we'll get to this stage later. There were some bugs and glitches, like how i couldn't deploy my drone, but that happens only when i'm playing co-op with my friends. The world is huge, one of the biggest maps ive eever played in, in a game. Sometimes, the map's so huge that it gets me tired driving, or flying from one point to another. moving on to the awesome parts of the game. The game really delivered the feeling of being a field operative on a mission to take down a cartel. Making the right choices of which enemy to kill first, makes you think really hard. the bullet drop, oooh, something i haven't experienced ever since i played the Battlefield series. As you progress through the world, leveling up, moving to different provinces, enemies get tougher, and so will the difficulty.
