Ghost Recon... I've been waiting for a long time when Ubisoft will once again remember this series of tactical shooters and I was very happy when on E3 2015 they finally announced the Wildlands. However, the joy was short-lived and that's why.

Firstly, we see the completely redesigned concept of the game. Instead of traditional levels, we are sent to the big open world of virtual Bolivia. On the one hand, this is a plus, with the other negative. Advantage of the open world - we get freedom in the passage of missions, but not every developer can take advantage of this advantage.

In the Wildlands, the minus dominates the plus, as the developers could not think of anything better than filling the game world with the ctrl-c -> ctrl-v principle. This is easy to explain: we have 29 bosses, and to get to 21 of them (the rest will then appear themselves), we need to perform a bunch of monotonous objectives: kill, capture, clean the sector, intercept, destroy and sometimes overhear. I will not deny that in most modern games everything is the same, but these things are not repeated in one game several times.

The secondary objectives are presented with the same monotonous routine: defend the agitation installation, hijack a plane/helicopter with supplies, deactivate relations, intimidate the mercenary leader and all the time. As a bonus, players are invited to collect various documents that make up the history of the Ghost Recon Wildlands, skill upgrade points and weapons with gadgets. The last two things look really stupid, because it seems that Bolivia was not abandoned by special forces, but by regular infantry.

Tactical gameplay, which was the basis of the series ruined. The artificial intelligence of local dudes is even dumber than in Future Soldier, which makes it easy to eliminate them on the stealth, and no one will notice a puddle of blood or a shortage of personnel. The high difficulty only increases the accuracy and damage, as a result of which you will be killed even by firing from Uzi from the sky-high distances. And this is relevant both for the cartel soldiers, and for La Unidad soldiers (local police and army). The latter will be dangerous only at high wanted levels, because we will be regularly chased by helicopters and heavy armored cars.

As for the plot, it's secondary, as if the developers spent on creating live action trailers. I expected the story at least as in Denis Villeneuve's Sicario, but as a result, there was some crumpled narrative with a typical ending. I have long noticed the trend that the theme of Latin American cartels is one of the weakest in video games...

Of course, it's hard to evaluate Ghost Recon Wildlands. In my opinion, the series went in the wrong direction, and the ideal option is the Future Soldier concept, but not the open world. Perhaps, I wouldn't rank it as a flaw, but the game turned into a continuous routine, not to mention the ruined tactical gameplay. It's ridiculous to say, but even in Metal Gear Solid V virtual opponents had more tactical features than here. In Ghost Recon Wildlands, opponents can surprise you only with their stupidity and high accuracy, no more, and the plot is very mediocre. I put thumbs up, because there is no neutral evaluation. The game has potential, but implementation leaves much to be desired.

Hi,

My first review so be gentle.

After playing many Tom Clancy games in the past (including the first...yes I am that OLD!) I was not actually expecting much from this offering since I felt the game series had gone down a slippery slope of "arcade" style.  After watching "The Mighty Jingles" play this on his Casual Saturdays I thought I would give it a shot.

The graphics (if you have a decent spec, I have a Nvidia 1080, quick SSD & i7) are brilliant and I really enjoyed flying/driving/running-like-hell around Bolivia, obviously a beautiful country I have yet to see IRL.  Some bugs do exist but I can appreciate that making an open world, mountainous country without the game occassionally having a bug is pretty hard given the amount of variables.  Some of them can be "mission" breaking but never game breaking in my experience, a quick reset and new approach can sometimes be frustrating and on other occassions be more rewarding.

The sounds can be a tad repetative and the radio is annoying after a few hours of the same messages.  I played with a headset (married with kids so....yeah) with virtual surround active which was fine.  Some variations are noticeable with the weapons but most of the generic "bang/splut/pop" which is unfortunate.  Again, not game breaking but attention to detail would have been great.

The story is a typical "America World Police" but there are some lovely twists dependant on the choices you make.....my femme fatale associate was "right" to do what she did at the end and took the fall in my first play through.

The missions are varied at the start until you realise that they are all pretty much repeated, IMHO the most fun you can have is varying your approach to each.  Go stealth, go snipe, go loud and go balls-deep.....all viable but some work better than others and sometimes you just get lucky!

AI can be stupid beyond reason at some points and absolute Special Forces monsters at others.  It depends what the game feels like it wants to do.  No mission I played ended up with the same outcome....some Unidad patrol overkill and some sneaked, shot, sneaked & complete.  The stealthy ones are the most satisfying but getting a long range silenced sniper kill without alerting anybody is probably the most fun!

The weapons....hmmmm.  You have to "find" the weapons/upgrades that make this game a lot more fun.  Most powerful sniper rifle..head to another zone and pick it up.  Nothing wrong with that but if you read online guides then you will get the most powerful stuff really quickly which takes away some replayability but on my second run through thats exactly what I did.  Still enjoyed the suppressed variation which is accurate IRL (loudest guns are still loud-ish if you have one fitted) and the fact that you can decide what upgrades you use.  Oh, and the worst aspect is the option of buying weapons in the "store"......what a money grabbing act of complete fail.

Co-Op is a lot more fun than I imagined.  3 of us sneaking from different directions, calling out targets, sniping, lobbing grenades, saving each other when we failed massively to sneak around.....huge plus for me and if you have friends who play this then I recommend grouping up and taking the cartel down together. 

Multiplayer....I don't do it due to old age, failing reflexes, poor old man eyesight and just being crap at it.....so I can't comment on it; sorry!

I have played Far Cry etc but being a military man IRL I felt this is so much more fun and allows me to decide what/where/when.  Loved the game despite its obvious flaws!

Hope you have fun.

Kind regards,

This is one of my favorite games I have in my Steam Library. 

[h1] Visuals/Graphics [/h1]
This game is the best looking open world game ever and is one of the best looking games in general. The lighting, the terrain, the weather and the distant landscapes are all superb quality. Seriously a visual overload. And your graphics card will suffer. Cranking every setting up to the max stresses your GPU like no other game can. This is the new "Can it run crysis?". There's a price to pay for visual fidelity and it sure is worth it.

[h1] Sounds [/h1]
The sounds in this game are awesome. The gravel under your feet, swimming through one of the many lakes and hiking up a mountain covered in snow all sound spectacular. The environmental sounds are spot on. 

The weapon sounds are great for the most part. The majority of the weapons sound beefy when they're fired (especially the sniper rifles) and the suppressor sounds are good as well. The SMG's can sometimes sound like pea shooters and the pistol sounds can leave a little to be desired but overall the weapon sounds are awesome. The hitmarker sounds are a little too much (COD like?) in my opinion. 

Helicopter and plane sounds are great but car and truck sounds are lacking. Obviously they aren't the main focus of the game but they just sound okay.

The voice acting is good but nothing to write home about.

[h1] Gameplay [/h1]
Is the game repetitive? Yes but I enjoy that. I'm one of those nerds who likes figuring out the best vantage point and turns their HUD off. The game world is huge. Massive. Gargantuan. And extremely detailed. Probably the biggest map in any game ever. The gun play is solid but there is a ton of bullet drop after a certain point; almost exponential. And the vehicle controls are crappy at best. I liked the story and it was fun to play but there wasn't anything new with it. They've fixed the AI so they don't know your position without ever seeing you but them searching your general area still happens.

[h1] Verdict [/h1]
If they ever make a second Wildlands, I hope it's more hardcore and less "mainstream". I feel like that would get rid of a lot of the problems that exist in the game currently due to it being caterted to the more casual gamer. I wouldn't go totally hardcore like Arma but tuning the gunplay and AI would make it near perfect. 

Even with all of it's flaws, this is still one of my favorite games. I've spent hours walking from one waypoint to the next clearing outposts and gazing at the incredible visuals this game offers. It's not perfect but it sure is a ton of fun.

The game is better than I thought it was gonna be. I've never played a Tom Clancy game so I went into this with no real idea of what to expect. From the hours I've played, it feels to me like a mix of Just Cause and Metal Gear. There's a lot of action and some good quality gunplay, but my preferred way to play is using stealth, marking out enemy locations and picking the best way to sneak in undetected. In my opinion its a stronger aspect of the game than the combat itself, but both are good.

The story is decent too, though I haven't progressed very far. It gives you good reasons to travel to each area and there are a lot of videos and documents that go into more depth if you desire it. 

My initial main draw to the game was from the open world itself and I have to say it didn't disappoint. The different regions of Bolivia represented here are very diverse and exploring each new area has always brought surprises. As for how  you can traverse the world, you have your standard ground vehicles like cars and bikes, along with boats, planes and helicopters. The land vehicles seem a bit too floaty for my liking, especially in faster ones like sports cars. The helicopters are definitely my preferred method of travel. They control well and most of them are helpful in combat.

Finally, I want to talk about the AI. If you plan on playing this game solo like myself, you'll have 3 AI teammates who follow you around and provide assistance. But don't worry if you'd rather go it alone; you can always tell them to hold back if you don't want the help. Not that the help they provide is always top-tier anyway. [h1]TL;DR[/h1]

Wildlands can't really decide whether it's an action game, stealth game, tactical simulator or a skill based exploration MMO. In the end, it excels at none of those, becomes a fancy shooting gallery instead and falls short in the endgame. One thing it's definitely not, is a Ghost Recon experience.

[h1]Too long part[/h1]

The limited amount of unlockables and gear doesn't really allow for sensible team-oriented builds. You eventuyally unlock all skills and have all of them at your disposal at all times. You're always better off being a one man army which by itself stomps teamwork and public matchmaking into the ground. Not like matchmaking with people who run off hunting llamas is fun anyway.

The extremely vast environment, while nice to look at, provides surprisnigly low variety. Same goes for missions and enemy types. You fight the same dudes for the whole game, you just become a bit more efficient at it by the 30th level.

The combat system obviousy encourages you to be stealthy as you are very easy to kill with a few rounds, very hard to detect by oblivious enemies (who are shooting with great accuracy once they DO detect you), headshots with pretty much anything are a 1-shot kill and the recon tools at your disposal are outright Godlike overpowered. 

You know where everyone is at all times which actually sucks. A fair challenge would be turning on the highest difficulty and disabling all HUD elements, but then it's you against tens of Bolivian clones of John Wick. That's not really fun either!

If only Wildlands got the same after-release care that the Division got, same amount of fine tweaks and additional content, it would have been an amazing game. Unfortunately, it seems abandoned and unfinished in comparison. Fair to say, it's fun for a while, you can mess around with various difficulty settings, unlock new gear and skills, but the will to go on pretty much ends once you reach level 30.

I would recommend getting it on sale if you're just looking for some temporary mindless action-packed fun.

A lot of people mention how repetitive this game is. Well, they're correct. It definitely is. But, I don't mind. I'm a really laid back gamer and I'll take my time on a game until I either finish it or walk away completely. This is one of those games.

The AI can be a bit stupid at times, as in, hold your position clearly means not stay out of sight and shoot the enemy while the player tries to go all ninja and wipe out a base without getting busted, but instead dies repeatedly because of the mentally challenged A-Team you just gave orders to. Oh, and I should mention how members of said team like to belt out how they can see an enemy through mountainous terrain/rocks/trees and buildings five miles away before you even get to where you're going or have a clear vantage point. If I can't see through things, how can they?! Whatever the superpower is called, it's actually pretty helpful, if not unrealistic.

The game looks beautiful. I have a GTX 1080, so I can't say what it'd look like with a lower-end GPU, so this may come off as...bias? Everything is crisp and clear. No complaints in this department. Day and night seems to cycle at a decent rate, unlike other games where day lasts a minute and night goes on until you graduate college.

I've played for about 16 hours or so, now, and within that time they've already done an update and screwed up the way the camera operates. It now pans slower than a sloth on a skateboard, well, if you're using a controller, that is. Keyboard and mouse still function as normal, I assume. They've also changed on-screen button icons that didn't need to be, but I suppose that's not something to whine about, though. Worth a mention, I guess. Someone obviously hasn't heard the phrase "if it ain't broke, don't fix it".

All in all, it's a decent time-killer. I haven't played multiplayer as of yet, but I'm sure it's fun. Most games are in this mode, especially when playing with people who have loud music going in the background or constantly scream obscenities because they lack Jesus. I don't know. I'll eventually get around to it. As of this review/rambling, the game is on sale, so it's worth it at the $20 price point. Stay away if at full price and just be patient for the next sale.

Well, that about wraps things up. I think I'll go drive down a mountain at full speed and keep going because of the realistic way the vehicles have super-strength or, fly a helicopter until it explodes in air, wait to hit the ground and walk away like nothing happened. Yeah, Wildlands for sure.

I won't say this is a bad game, it does have a lot of problems though.  Random crashes, the occasional invisible enemy, stuff like that.

It is not very well optimized, like at all, so if you are using anything under the power of a RX 570 or 1060 then you'll need to play on medium settings or be prepared to run under 30 fps in a lot of areas.

The Story is just the typical generic "America is here to save the day" ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with all sorts of military talk cheese that games like these all seem to have. None of the characters are relatable (I could not ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stand Bowman at all). There is little to no character development.

Gameplay-wise it can be pretty fun, especially with friends. The map is pretty large and has a ♥♥♥♥ load of main and side missions. It plays like a stripped down MGS5, but still has plenty of fun moments and decent stealth. A good amount of weapons to unlock and plenty of attachments to go with them.

Overall I'd say wait until its at least on sale for $25 or lower.

Adding a quick note: I am not saying I hate the game or that you, by definition, should or should not get it. The customization is fun, and the gunplay is pretty tight, but for a game series that's been all about stealth and tactics, it's far away from where the series used to be, and not everything works as advertised.

If you want an open-world, third-person shooter to mess around in with your friends, or if you like customizing your character with tactical gear, and like customizing guns, You can get this game. Preferably, wait for a big sale. At least 50% off or so. Aside from that, I'm not sure if the game is worth it.

As an open-world game, it does everything bad open world games do wrong. The map is clearly designed around diffirent 'arenas', with everything else coloured in between. You do not get rewarded for exploring, there's nothing there. These arenas are oftenly surrounded by impenetrable walls, including inexplicably undestroyable chainlink fences, or unclimbable cliffs. Apparently elite special forces operators didn't get the mountaineering training all special forces get. Which I think is a missed opportunity. It also has horrible pop-out and pop-in, which makes some missions unplayable. For instance, if you want to take out sam-sites in advance for a mission to steal a helicopter, just driving too far away from them will either respawn the sam-sites, ur despawn the C4 you put on it. Sometimes enemies will pop-in around you if you drive into a village too fast.

People who were expecting a Tactical Shooter with heavy stealth elements like Ghost Recon is known for, they'll be disappointed. For a good singleplayer experience, get MGSV instead. It's clearly defined as a multiplayer game, to the point where some missions are almost impossible to do. Such as stealing a driving car without destroying it. If the only thing you can do as the driver of your own vehicle is ramming it, this is almost impossible, and the game feels more like a 3rd-person shooter than a tactical shooter with stealth elements. Again, no planting bombs ahead of time, and the enemy AI is rudimentary. When you are detected by one enemy, all others seem to immediately know where you are. There's no way to silently take out enemies from behind cover aside from shoot them, which can have repercussions such as the bullet alerting someone else, and it's impossible to avoid random helicopters. This is remedied by being able to pause the game and switching weapons to adjust tactics when you're forced to. The problem with this is that the game seems to WANT to be a stealth game, as enthousiasts that play on the hardest difficulty emphasize you're not winning extended gunfights. So when you choose a stealth approach, and you don't have all the tools to deal with, for instance, helicopters, which feels somewhat unfair.

Add to that that it's become the rather typical ubisoft tick-off-all-the-icons-on-your-map kind of game with over 80 times the same kind of mission, like we already got tired of halfway the first assassin's creed, it's become a boring, very basic third-person shooter.

There were also promises of being able to affect factions: These are false. You can do missions that level the assistance rebels can give you. That's it. Nobody gives a ♥♥♥♥ if you accidentally run over a rebel or a civilian, and Unidad and the Cartel will always hate you. Spoiler alert: [spoiler]The rebels betray you in the final mission and become enemies.[/spoiler] That's it.

Lastly, there's a weird dissonance, which is ultimately a miniscule issue: Why have elite special ops guys never had mountaineering training? Why have they never heard of bolt cutters and are stopped by chainlink fences? Why do two guns that shoot the same caliber have extremely diffirent stats? Why does all intelligence come from magical story-convenient hacking or awkwardly convenient papers? Why is gathering intelligence other than enemy positions not part of the fun?

Edit 25-03-2018: adjusted spelling as pointed out by Kattegat. I was not aware of the spoiler tag, I have implemented this (but really, if you are bothered by a spoiler in this game, you have a very low storytelling standard, imho).

When in a firefight, you have to take into account the distance between you and the enemy and adjust your aim accordingly. For the enemy AI, they have none of that. Once they spot you, they shoot, you instantly take damage, and you're dead. They're shots have no bullet travel. This means that even if you shoot at the same time, you'd still be the first one to go down since you're bullet will still be travelling as you shot, while theirs are already implanted in your character's body. [h1]In short[/h1]
Remember the part in Far Cry 4 where you’re taking on a whole base with alarms and all? Well in this game, you’re mostly doing the same thing, with friends, and more guns/vehicles.

[b]Is the game any good ? Pros vs Cons:[/b]
[h1]Pros[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Nice amount of weapons.[/b]
[*] [b]Nice skill tree[/b]. Your character has a nice progression.
[*] [b]A good challenge[/b]. I feel accomplished after clearing out a base.
[*] [b]Good balance (weapon/vehicle)[/b]: There's no best vehicle. Sure that huge helicopter has way more firepower than that other helicopter but it's sooooo much slower. Same for weapons.
[*] [b]Good tactics[/b]: There's the alarm you have to take out to prevent reinforcements. Take out the lights to take advantage or your night / heat vision. That base has 2 exits: make sure to block any escape for the guy you have to capture. And to accomplish all that you have a lot of equipment: High-tech drone to spot enemies, grenade launcher, C4, flashbangs, grenade launcher, diversions lure, mines, grenade launcher. Yes, I have an unhealthy obsession with the grenade launcher. Oh? You think you're going to escape in that car? Oh, my dear friend, here, have a grenade.
[*] [b]Multiplayer [/b]. You get the guy on the left, I got the guy on the right. Ready ? 3… 2… 1… DOUBLE HEADSHOT!
[*] [b]Realism[/b]: You're sniping a guy a mile away ? Sure. But you better aim high above him because of that realistic that bullet drop. Also, bullets are not instant. They have a speed. Sounds like a pain but it’s not. I’m telling you: there's nothing more satisfying than aiming at the sky, pulling the trigger, nothing happens for a few seconds and then you see a bad guy drop dead a mile away from your position. The Perfect Shot. Myyyyy god!! Was that as good for you as it was for me?
[*] [b]It's fun[/b]. The next section will seem like a lot of whining, but overall, it's fun.
[*] [b]Grenade launcher.[/b]
[/list]

[h1]Cons[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]The grenade launcher is too strong[/b] and only attaches to a hand full of weapons. In my opinion, that makes 90% of guns useless. Incompatible with launchy? Get out.
[*] [b]The skill tree is not that big[/b]. After 40 hours, you have all skills maxed out.
[*] [b] No real sense of world progression[/b] (only character progression). That camp you cleared? It's going to be reset. That Anti-Air missile launcher that is preventing you from moving around in an helicopter? Destroy it as many times as you want. It will still be there the next time you’ll want to go through that zone.
[*] [b]Casino loading times[/b]. Fast travel somewhere: Loading takes 25 seconds. 2 minutes later, fast travel again to the same place: 97 seconds. Fast travel a third time to the same g** d*** place : 41 seconds. Then 12 seconds, then 127. Really?
[*] [b]Uplay.[/b] (see below for what I mean)
[*] [b]Difficulty?[/b]: Easy means you have a lot of HP, and Hard means you have less HP. But you know that mission where you have to protect some dude ? Super easy or super hard has no influence because the dude has the same HP. And that guy you need to capture that will flee at the first sign of troubles ? Well, he will flee just as quick regardless of difficulty.
[*] [b]Action animations[/b]. Don’t use melee in this game, ever. The melee attack animation is sooo long that the guy will have died of old age long before the animation is over.
[*] [b]"Repetitive"[/b] (see below for what I mean)  
[*] [b]The corrupt Unidad Army.[/b]  (see below for what I mean) 
[*] [b]Minor annoyances.[/b] (see below for what I mean)
[*] [b]Lootboxes.[/b]They’re not mandatory but they have NO place in a 70$ game.
[/list]

[b]Repetitive[/b]

Here is how you will spend your time in the game:
[olist]
[*] Look at your map for the next objective: A base camp.
[*] Approach the camp.
[*] Scan for enemies.
[*] Stealth kill 76% of enemies.
[*] Miss a shot because the dude you were trying to snipe is now participating in So You Think You Can Dance, break dance edition, at the very moment you fired you shot.
[*] Observe all remaining alerted enemies closing in on your approximate location.
[*] Kill the all remaining guys in loud mode, except for one dude because even though he doesn’t know exactly where you are, he can still dodge your bullets while facing away from you because of his spider-sense, obviously.
[*] Brute force that last ♥♥♥♥♥♥ with everything you have
[*] Pick up power-ups in the, now empty, base.
[*] Fill up on ammo with a single click on any ammo box.
[*] Do the objective.
[*] Rinse and repeat.
[/olist]

That’s about 80% of the game. Sure, every base camp is slightly different than the last one. And no it's not a mindless button mashing game so it's no THAT repetitive. But if you don’t like clearing base after base, don’t buy this game.


[b]Uplay[/b]

That software is an insult. I bought the game on steam. Bought the DLCs on Uplay. DLCs won't work. People are screaming in the forums. Ubisoft doesn't care. The game even tells me: Hey, here are some DLC that are available for you to play since I know that you bought them ! Just click here to activate the DLC. An error occured, get lost. 
Oh, one more thing ! My friend couldn't play for a whole night because Uplay wouldn't connect. Uplay? More like FU you can't Play. Ok I'm done about Uplay.
WAIT!! One last thing I swear: Every 20 hours I can't deploy a drone. I hit the hotkey and nothing is happening. Restarting the game doesn't fix it. I have to restart Uplay. I'm not kidding. Restarting the game doesn’t fix the hotkey issue. I have to restart Uplay, constantly, to fix a hotkey not working. How is that a thing? That’s like having to restart Netflix because the characters on Friends don’t have anything to say to each other and stop talking. That doesn’t make sense!! Hmmm Ok. I'm done about Uplay. For now.

[b]The Unidad Army[/b]

Even though you are the good guys, the army in place is corrupt and will attack you. So you're infiltrating a base and then you get spotted by a passing Unidad car. You turn around and destroy it. But too late... it's on. OH IT’S ON. Another car arrives. Grenade and it's destroyed with all its occupants. Then 2 cars. You destroy them. 3 cars, 4 cars, helicopters, and before you know it, every soldier in the country is shooting at you. And changing the difficulty won’t change that. Sigh...

This concept is realistic: any good dictator should send more and more soldiers until their pest problem is solved. I get that. But it's not fun. C’mon… it’s a game. It's supposed to be fun and make me forget about worries in the real world. Like long commutes, and work and having to deal with Uplay. Myyyyy god Uplay sucks !

[b]Minor annoyances[/b]

Hmmm my next objective will take 3 minutes to get there in car. I’ll ask the rebels for an helicopter.
- I would like an helicopter please!
- Here you go sir, I just spawned an helicopter waiting for you on the other side of that impassable canyon, past that huge lake, on top of that impregnable mountain, way beyond the clouds. You can get there in 35-40 minutes, top… if you have an helicopter to get there, of course.
- … I’m standing next to an empty helipad…
- Yes, you are sir!
- Can you spawn another?
- Yes sir! I just spawned an helicopter on top of your exact location aaaaaaaaaaand you've just been crushed by an helicopter. Enjoy the loading screen!
(This happened for real)

There’s a lot of minor annoyances like this, nothing game-breaking… but it’s annoying.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
The pros still outweigh the cons. The game is fun. It's pricey but the content, graphics and long gameplay justifies it. The game got my heart racing a few times. I felt pride, joy, shock, fun, the wrath of infinite vengeance and more.

(Fun * Time Spent - Annoyances) / Pricing  = 7.5 / 10
But then you factor in Uplay and you get negative 291. Out of 10.

Having played several of the earlier Ghost Recon games I'd personally say that Wildlands has next to nothing in common with them and if you'll allow me to be so bold I would say that's a good thing. If I were to hop on the popular trend of comparing it to other games I'd say it's an amalgam of The Division, the later Rainbow Six games, and Splinter Cell (I used all Tom Clancy games to be fair). It has the open world and a similar way of storytelling to The Division although obviously the open world in Wildlands doesn't work the same way... you can basically go wherever you want whenever you want and you'll be able to survive if you're a decent player. The combat is a mix of Splinter Cell and Rainbow Six... leading up to every major engagement you'll probably want to use stealth and scout the area out, marking targets and setting up traps, but once you tell your team to engage it's full on action. Really the only thing about this game that make it a Ghost Recon game are that it's squad based and you have a drone.

The squad is handled better and worse than in previous GR games. Better in that you won't lose just because you didn't give orders to your squadmates quickly enough or because their AI is stupid. Worse in that it has been severely dumbed down. You can't (as far as I know) tell individual squad members to go anywhere... they all have to move as a unit. You can't specifically tell who to attack who and you have no say in their weapon loadout. The latter point is kind of minimal as once they're actively engaging enemies they kill them pretty quickly and efficiently; the exception to this is in vehicle combat. For some reason when your AI squadmate mans a turret on a humvee he does basically no damage to enemy vehicles. Maybe this is to keep your AI squad from accidentally blowing up mission critical vehicles but they also have a hard time killing non-mission critical vehicles as well. Whereas if you hop on the turret you will mow down anything and everything in your path with little effort. Unfortunately without playing coop this means your vehicle will have to be stationary as your AI mates can't drive (which makes sense that would cause all sorts of pathing issues).

I bought Wildlands at the same times as Siege, Just Cause 3, and Dark Souls III and Wildlands is taking up a disproportionate amount of my time compared to the others. I can't get enough of it. I think they executed a lot of different systems better than a lot of other games have. It's not perfect, nothing is, but even the side content feels like you're advancing the story.

For some reason I’ve been ignoring Ubisoft over the last several years but they have won me back with their current triple threat lineup; The Division, Siege and Wildlands and may be one of the last AAA developers to bring quality to their named franchises while improving on every subsequent update and full release. Wildlands is one of the best (and largest) sandbox games I’ve ever played. Add in drop-in / drop-out co-op and you have the perfect receipt for games with this kind of mechanic. 

Want to play solo? No problem. Want to play with three other friends? No problem? Want to roam casually via GTA style wile matchmaking? No problem. 

Want a leveling system that isn’t just XP > Level up > Max out? No problem. Wildlands offers a way to continue amp up difficulty as you progress. As you reach level 30, the game allows you to turn on a 2nd tiering system while on Extreme Difficulty. IT also allows you to level up your guns damage so the difficulty scales with your weaponry. When there three other players in your party, the game scales back the difficulty automatically based on the average level of all players. 

There’s a few annoying things about the game. The driving mechanic needs a bit of work as some vehicles are difficult to steer. 

The re-spawn area may sometimes throw you outside of your party, or may spawn you in the middle of a firefight. Good luck figuring that one out. 

And probably the biggest thing that needs tweaking is the extreme difficulty as you approach Tier 1; The game prides itself on allowing players to complete missions in a verity of different ways. Go stealth, go in from the air, go in on ground assault, call in reinforcements, go in at night/day- however in the extreme Tier 1 difficulty, your only option is stealth. If you even try to go in Rambo style enemies will spot you quicker, kill you faster with no time to react. In that regard the game becomes a little stale doing the missions the exact same way every single time. 

It looks as though Ubisoft will be supporting these games for a while which is fine by me. I don’t need a sequel until there’s another country that needs to be reconed.

Ghost Recon is an open-world game that takes place in Bolivia. The game is about a special forces group from the USA that has a task to take down the Cartel and arrest the drug lord El Sueno. To take down the Cartel, you have to take down four different parts of the Cartel first. They are Security, Smuggling, Production, and Influence. Each part has around five or six bosses in them. The game has two different ways you can finish a mission: you can go in stealth and have someone far away sniping the people close to you, or you could go in loud and shoot them with the help of the rebels. The game has a fantastic variety of guns. You also have a drone, which you can use to find enemies. If it's dark, you can use night vision or thermal vision.

In the game, there are four factions. The first faction is the Ghosts, which is the group that you are in. The second faction is the Rebels, they help you in battle and are your allies. The third faction is the Cartel, they are the enemies and the people you can kill quite easily. The fourth and final faction is La Unidad, which is Bolivia's military. You should really be careful when you kill anyone from La Unidad because if one sees someone getting shot, he will call in that they are getting attacked, and you will get stars like in GTA V.

I think you should buy the DLCs. The first DLC is Narco Road. In Narco Road, you are working undercover as a narco. It also has a lot of interesting vehicles. The second DLC is Fallen Ghosts, which is when the Ghosts are tracked down by some private military forces who have camo vests and bulletproof vests. The last DLC isn't really a DLC, but it came after the game, so I will call it a DLC. I am talking about Ghost War. Ghost War reminded me a lot of Rainbow Six Siege. It's very much like Siege, but it uses the physics from Ghost Recon.

I would recommend this game to people who like open world, military, FPS shooters, tactical shooters, or are interested in how a drug cartel works.

Wildlands free weekend is long gone and i´m actually glad i was given the chance to test the game for free during a weekend. I managed to get enough hours in to form my opinion about the game. 

Here´s what i liked about the game:

+ Visually, Wildlands can be amazing to look at, and there are a ton of options to play with, unlike many games, it also shows you the exact changes in graphical quality, using a still picture, which was a nice feature.

+ They promoted the game as an open world Ghost recon game, and well, open it is, the game world is big. Something like 24km x 24 km, of course a big ammount of the map is just rural areas and forrests, but still, the map is gigantic. 

+ There´s more customization then i thought, you can customize the character and the weapons pretty freely.

+ Weapon mechanics remind me of MGS V, which were done well for the most part, the whole "sync shot" mechanic was pretty nice. You can line up and execute shots from three different people at the same time.

+ The support skills were okay, you can call in a mortar strike, support squad, recon, vehicle drops and that short of things.

And then, the the negative:

- First off, driving mechanics. I´v seen better car / motorcycle mechanics on PS2 games that are 15 years older. Especially the motorbike. It just feels like the vehicles arent responding to the terrain at all, and they constantly do weird stuff. Plane mechanics are absolutely fine, but theres some weird things there too, like how you are able to get hit by an anti air missile, having your plane explode into pieces and fall to the ground and survive.

- Cutscenes had constant FPS drops, while the normal gameplay didn´t have any.

- With customization and online features comes microtransactions, which gate off a large portion of customization options.

- Really, absolutely the biggest negative i have about the game is the mission design. What you have here is a massive world, that is of course filled with different missions and side missions, you also are "required" to do the side missions, if you want to upgrade different support skills you have so i was doing a lot of them. And well, beign a big completionist, i would have done them anyways.

But what came painfully obvious pretty fast is that there are about a handfull (around 8) different side mission types, its always either steal this truck/plane, interrogate that guy, defend or capture this location or get that intel. So after about 5 hours of playing you have seen them all, after that, each side mission is the same, with a different location and more / less enemies. 

This is a way of doing side mission that i just cant stand, whats the point of having a huge map with a ton of missions if you´re just reapeating few missions, with absolutely no context or story on them, other then "go steal a plane, we could use a plane" 

Many games fall into that sort of mission design, which just feels like having missions for the sake of having them, they dont add anything meaningfull to the story. It doesn´t help that the actual main quests often dont feel any different. Its just lazy.


If you have friends who play the game, and you can co-op it, i bet it would be pretty fun, but as a singleplayer experience, which is the way i experienced it, i really wouldn´t pay the standart 59,90 for the game, just so i could have a mediocre campaing and side missions with minimal effor put into them. It was fun to play around for a while, but the game got old really fast. Which is it´s downfall. It really reminded me of Just cause 1, that game also had a huge open world, with repeated side content and support skills much like Wildlands.

Recommended price and the price i would pay for the game is around 10 to 15€

Mixed feelings on this one.  The graphics are amazing, the guns feel fantastic, and there is a ton of content.  Unfortunately, vehicles are strictly for utility.  There's no fun to be had crashing around the hillsides on a dirt bike or sight-seeing in a chopper.  The missions are interesting and diverse, but too many suffer from insta-fail stealth checks.  It's bad game design and we've been telling Ubi to stop since the first Assassin's Creed.  

The microtransactions are excessive.  If you expect to be able to unlock all the weapons and such, expect to shell out considerable real-money funds.  As of Jan. 2018, the game also has loot crates for gambling with real money.  All purchases use a credit system which forces you to buy credits in increments impossible to spend.  $20 for 1,000 credits when everything costs 900 or 1,100 or whatever.  You don't actually *need* any of the stuff, but that fact is needlessly difficult to determine.  The actual DLC seems very substantial: new enemy types & AI, new maps, new missions, new weapon archetypes... it feels more like an expansion than a DLC.  Unfortunately, it is ultimately more of the same and it isn't really captivating.  It's also more difficult than the base game, which is a bad thing.  

Ubi seems to think that the game should become increasingly difficult with time played and as a result I no longer enjoy the game.  As players progress through the tier 1 system, they eventually become restricted to extreme difficulty with reduced visual cues and other aids.  Enemies become super-durable with Spiderman-like detection abilities while the player becomes ever more fragile.  The insta-fail mission mechanics were bad enough already, but the tier 1 stuff is just over-the-top.  The best parts of the game play like Far Cry 2, but tier 1 plays more like Metal Gear Solid (a bad thing).  To wit: I've yet to see a player that has actually reached the highest tier of tier 1 mode.  Even popular streamers seem to be struggling.   It's a neat concept, but it's just not well done.  Not at all.

Wildlands really is a good game and there is a lot of fun to be had, but once the veneer wears off it's painfully clear just how many missed opportunities there are.  Aside from performance and visual fidelity, the game falls short of excellence in almost every possible way.  6/10 - among the best games of 2017, but practically nobody will be able to stomach it long enough to see all the content.  A real shame.

Great tactical shooter. Giant and I mean huge, open world that allows you to tackle missions utilizing a variety of tactics. Run in hard and fast on an armored vehicle lighting up anything that moves, utilize support to call in distractions on one side of a base while you clear from the opposite side and their backs, send your team in while you snipe down threats, sneak into bases disabling generators and their ability to call in reinforcements, then stealthily clear the base at night one target at a time. The possibilities are virtually endless and completely up to you. There is no linear storyline, so tackle the main missions if you like, do side missions, find equipment throughout the map to upgrade your character first, it's completely up to you. 

Weapon customizations are virtually limitless, dozens of guns, with hundreds of various attachments, allow you to utilize the weapon you want, how you want to. Run and run playstyle? Close range red dot, with laser sights, shorter barrels, and buttstocks. Like to engage in medium range? 4x ACOG scopes, a good forgrip, standard to long barrel, and possibly a silencer. Long range fighter? Take a high caliber rifle, equip it with a long barrel, silencer, long range scope to take out targets at distance and not give away your awesome position. What rifle you use, and how you'll utilize it is up to you, and the weapons systems provide for a lot of freedom. 

Vehicles are in game, and definitely, help navigate the huge map. From various types of helicopters to pickup trucks, to armored APC's and humvee's with mounted weapons, to dirt bikes there is a good variety of vehicles in the game, and with rebel support, you can call in vehicles to your spot at pretty much anywhere. The physics however with the vehicles leaves a little to be desired as they can fly across any terrain while sustaining little damage or proper feel for that rocky path your on. 

You play in 4 man squads unless you're playing co-op with fewer players, but for this write up we're talking the AI. Controls are a bit lacking in my opinion. You can designate targets for each ghost to focus on, and synchronize your shots, it's very rewarding using this features as you countdown and drop 4 targets at a time. What would have been really awesome though is the ability to plan and sync assaults on compounds, laying out a path for each ghost to clear in steps, as it is you can sync shots, then give the ghosts general directions to proceed either hot or stealthily. 

Where the game shines the brightest is in co-op and online modes. With your friends and a good discord server you can really set up the assaults, and execute them perfectly, each team member knowing his objective and in which order to take them. The games are brilliant and perfect like this and I can't heap enough praise upon it. 4x4 online 'ghost war' mode is pretty cool as well, but it requires a good squad which it assigns pretty randomly. But when you get that good squad and everything hits just right, it's also an amazing experience. 

All in all I highly recomend this game, while it has a few short falls, such as the single player mode can start to get pretty repetitive towards the end game, it has a ton of redeming features, especially in co-op and online modes. I would rate this 4.5 out of 5, and definitily recomend this to any fans of FPS and tactical shooters.

This is as generic as generic gets. A massive and undeniably beautiful open world with only a handful of things to do over and over.

First and foremost, let me just say that this should NOT be played singleplayer. The characters and dialog are so unbelievably one dimensional that you will find yourself groaning as every single attempt at humour falls flat. Throw between one and three friends into the mix and there is a possibility to glean some entertainment out of this.

Taking on a fortified base in complete silence, synchronising shots with your sniper buddy. There is no denying how much of a badass you will feel when you nail that headshot or wipe out an entire squad of enemies in a single flurry of sniper fire. Even when things don't go as planned, the subsequent firefights are hectic and sometimes hilarious.

Unfortunately, you will find yourself doing the same thing every half hour. There are side missions you can tackle, but the variety is extremely lackluster. Trigger a radio antenna then race to another, defend a radio when it broadcasts rebel propaganda, steal a guarded chopper/plane or stop and tag a supply convoy. That's basically it. There are so many tactics that can be applied to complete these objectives, but you will quickly find the best method and this suddenly becomes routine and dull.

There is a nice level of customization with your character's gear and weapons, allowing you to spend literally hours tweaking your setup and making yourself look as professional or as goofy as possible. Sadly, the game is lacking in the "goofy" aspect, instead trying for force the serious tone of the game. There are weapon paints available such as bright red or pink, but surprise surprise, you have to pay extra for them.

At first glance Wildlands looks like the typical Ubisoft open world Action-Adventure game, but a few hours in you quickly realize that the team behind Wildlands not only wanted to create a huge beautiful open world - but that they also wanted to have meaniful content and realstic wildlife and NPCs present as well.

I'm a huge Assassin's Creed fan, but I'd be the first to point out that a vast majority of the side activities available in those games does nothing to push the story forward in a meaningful way. In Wildlands every side mission you complete is either bringing you closer to dismantling the cartel, or giving you intel or resources to unlock or improve support options.

These support options range from vehicle dropoffs such as armored weaponized vehicles and helicopters, or literally giving you a dozen rebels reinforcements to help you with different scenarios across the huge world.

All of the game's mechanics come together in such a polished and coherent way that you really do get immersed into this role of being a ghost solider. I cannot praise enough how open the game is in letting you tackle missions. There are countless times where I'd intentions to go in stealthy only to make one wrong move that in most games would be an insta-death, but in Wildlands you're given the freedom to recover and adapt to even rookie mistakes.

The story in Wildlands was actually pretty great and one of the main reasons I'd be hooked for multiple hours in a single session was because I wanted to see what was going to happen next. 

I have yet to play the DLCs but I hear they're great as well. I've only put about 10 hours into the PVP mode, but I can see that I am going to really enjoy it as well. Right now I could best describe it as Metal Gear Solid V meets Rainbow Six Siege.

TL;DR: If you're only interested in the singleplayer aspect, buy Metal Gear Solid V. Otherwise, wait for a deep sale (50% off or more) and convince your friends to buy Wildlands with you.

On the surface, this game seems awesome. Huge open world with a ton of environment diversity, fair amount of guns and attachments, and, of course, co-op mode. Unfortunately, this game, like many other Ubisoft titles, simply doesn't fully realize its potential.

There's hardly any depth in gameplay or mechanics when compared to a similar game like Metal Gear Solid V. The game is also WAY too forgiving: skills are unlocked relatively easily, dead bodies simply disappear after a short time so you really don't need to worry about enemies finding them - which is lucky because you can't drag corpses! In a stealth game! - and there's a pretty easily unlockable skill that basically allows your AI teammates to perform a one-shot stealth kill on any enemies at your command, etc.

This game is a tragedy. You can tell the developers wanted this game to be something much more, but simply couldn't reach their goals. On the other hand, Wildlands has one single redeeming factor that potentially makes up for all of its flaws...

It's an absolute blast with friends. I've never had so much fun pretending to be a badass covert operative. The admittedly generous customization options make role-playing easy and fun, and playing with two or three friends doubles that fun. When playing with friends, the bugs and flaws become hilarious instead of a hinderance. I've had tons of fun seeing how far I could launch myself after crashing a motorbike (hint: it's upwards of a mile).

In summary, the game is stale and shallow when played alone, but promises hours of fun with friends. If you're interested in this game but don't have friends, buy Metal Gear Solid V. If you can convince your friends to get this, wait for a deep sale. Evidently, despite the fun you can have with friends, I've decided to rate it with a thumbs down, as games shouldn't have to depend on multiplayer to be fun if they promise engaging singleplayer gameplay.

I wanted to like this game.  I really did.  But it's a mess.  I'm currently waiting on a refund.

Nine months after release it's still full of bugs.  The two that really stood out to me in the two hours I spent with the game were losing access to my drone and binoculars and vehicles clipping into the ground.  The first is apperently a bug that has been reported since the game was released, but has still not been fixed.  

The game seems to have a lot of promise if you like stealth infiltration.  I do and that's why I bought it, but it's not worth 8,000 yen in it's current state.

Beyond the bugs I found the game play lacking in a few areas.  The first was vehicle control.  None of the ones that I tried (Jeep, pickup truck, car, helicopter) felt like real vehicles.  I've played blender games that had better handling.  The developers should have spent a bit of time playing GTA 5.  That game did an amazing job with the feel of it's vehicles.

The second area that I was a bit put off by was the character progression.  You have a wide variety of skills you can learn as you level up and collect skill points (they can be found around the map like in Watch Dogs 2).  However, in this game to learn a skill you need more than skill points.  You need to find resources and deliver them to the rebels.  What the ♥♥♥♥?  What does supplying the rebels have to do with a steadier aim or learning to parachute?  For that matter, why am I spending skill points on these things?  I thought I was supposed to be an elite special forces soldier.  But I don't know how to parachute yet?

The third thing that bothered me was character mobility.  Assassin's Creed Origins has spoiled me.  In that game if it looks like you should be able to climb it, you can.  That's not the case here.  I was very frustrated not being able to use a window as a foothold to climb onto the roof of a single story building.  Origins spoiled me.  I want that in any open world game that I play going forward.

I may pick this game up again during a sale (but probably not, I'm much more likely to take a chance of Far Cry 5), but I don't think it's worth more than 2000 yen (about $20 US).  The base infiltration aspect of the game seemed to be sound (as long as you don't get hit by the drone bug).  I did look at the Uplay E-store for the game.  I thought that the content they had available there was insanely overpriced for this game.  Though I didn't feel that way about their offerings for Origins.  If I do pick it up later on sale I will be using Cheat Engine to bypass the resource requirements for learning skills.

Before I played this game I was very excited about Far Cry 5.  After playing this I am less so.  I loved Far Cry Primal and AC: O.  But Far Cry 4 left a bad taste in my mouth.  I didn't like the way any of the vehicles handled in that game either.  It looks like they will be a big part of 5, and the way they handled them in Wildlands does not inspire confidence.

Edit: Something else that really bothered me was constantly being pestered to join a coop game.  I live in Japan and most games put me in a server located in this region.  That usually means I end up playing with a bunch of people speaking Korean or Chinese.  I had Zero interest in the multiplayer aspects of this game when I bought it and was extremely annoyed that it was constantly pestering me about it.  Hold enter to join coop.  Get that ♥♥♥♥ off of my HUD.  I don't want to see it.  If I want to join a multiplayer game, I'll go into the menu and join one.

Edit 2:  Also your AI teamates suck.  I don't mean they're stupid.  I mean the way the were concieved is just moronic.  They don't seem to do much of anything except revive you if you get taken out.  Of course the enemy AI's ignore them while they are doing that.  As bad as the companions were in Fallout 4, they were better than this.  

The after taste this game has left continues to worsen.  I don't think I'll ever give this game another chance.  I also don't see myself playing Far Cry 5 after seeing what a mess this was.

Edit 3:  After writing this I went back and played some Watch Dogs 2 and gave Far Cry 4 another chance.  Since playing 4 the first time I picked up an Xbox controller for my PC, before I was using the keyboard to drive. The controler really improved the feel (I use keyboard and mouse when on foot and the controller for driving).   Driving in both of those games feels far better than in Ghost Recon.  I think I like the feel in Watch Dogs 2 a bit more than in GTA 5.  So it puzzles me greatly that vehicles handled so poorly in this title.   I'm feeling much better about Far Cry 5 as a result of playing both of those games again and will be picking it up on launch day.

In-game controls/feeling: 3.5/5
Graphics: 4.5/5
Unlockables(Quantity and quality): 5/5
Freedom to do what you want, when you want, how you want: 5/5

The Good:

- Much like the Far Cry series, the game is at its best when you're not focusing on missions and just jerking around. I've had more fun trying to take down a random checkpoint or convoy than any of the structured mission-related activities. 

- The combat is satisfying. And, seriously, whoever did the sound production for the guns in this game needs an award-- every gun in the game sounds unique, supressed and unsupressed. 

- There's a ton of stuff to collect-- and while you'll never use most of it (for instance, I never used any of the shotguns or LMGs I found since the Assault Rifle is, by a wide margin, the most versatile and effective primary weapon class) it's a lot of fun knocking down the outposts to get those weapons and parts. 

- The intel briefings videos for each target are very well done and serve to make your targets feel like more complete characters. There were a few times I even understood or sympathized with them. 

The Bad:

- From all indications, the game isn't terribly well-optimized for PC. I'm running a fairly beefy setup featuring a 1080ti GPU and i7 6700k CPU and I struggle to keep the game above 45 FPS on very-high settings. I settled for high settings with some graphical features disabled and managed a respectable 60 FPS average. 

- I encountered some persistent bugs. During some sessions the game would repeatedly display a message stating my keyboard had been disconnected/reconnected. Other times, my binoculars or drone wouldn't zoom in or allow me to use the Sync Shot ability. There are some puzzling terrain detection issues where I couldn't climb certain waist-high rocks or certain rocks weren't climbable except from a very particular angle. None of these were necessarily game-breaking, just annoying.  

- Story mission variety is lacking. You're going to see the extent of the mission variety in the first province and it's just more of the same from that point on. Kill this target, steal/hack this thing, capture/interrogate this NPC, free this NPC from capture. The game throws a few curveballs here and there like disabling your drone-- but other than that, it's fairly boilerplate stuff. 

- The three NPC members of your squad are totally forgettable and the game does absolutely nothing to flesh them out aside from some color commentary during certain missions. As a matter of fact, as most of their dialogue is delivered via headset chatter and their voices are so similar, I never took the time to differentiate which voice belonged to which guy. They're basically there to drive the Sync Shot and Revive mechanics.  

The Meh:   

- As I mentioned above, you'll never use a lot of the gear you get. There's not a lot of incentive to approach missions guns blazing as enemies will continuously call for reinforcements, especially in some of the more difficult provinces-- so shotguns and LMGs aren't ideal for all but a few side missions. I received the G36C from the Ubisoft Club at the start of the game (since I own The Division)-- and it was so absurdly OP that I never used another primary weapon. 

- Once you acquire the rebel spotting ability and max out your drone and Sync Shot, the game becomes an absolute cake walk. I had to self-impose restrictions on using the drone and Sync Shot because they make the game so laughably easily that it becomes laughable.    

- The lack of mid-mission checkpoints during certain missions is mind-boggling. Many missions begin with a lengthy infiltration phase which transitions into a secondary phase like a timed activity or NPC extraction. Failing any portion of the second phase immediately restarts the mission from the beginning-- meaning you have to repeat a very time-consuming infilration phase from the beginning.

Final Verdict: 

6.5/10 - Lukewarm recommendation. Try to pick it up on sale unless you're a huge fan of the genre. It's a passibly-enjoyable sandbox experience built on satisfying combat-- but, content-wise, there's nothing new here and the optimization issues are a bummer.

Personally, I'm not too fond of Uplay and them forcing the Uplay connection even when owning the game on Steam but that didn't stop me from getting Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands because I was looking for an open world tactical shooter that I could play and enjoy with a friend or two and I don't regret it at all.

Aside from the main missions, there are plenty side missions that you can approach and finish in order to gain more resources to upgrade your character's skills whenever you level up. The world is huge and beautiful which is something I definitely like about the game and it's fairly easy to get around as you can travel by land, sea, or sky. I have to admit that car handling isn't the smoothest but it still works and so far I haven't really encountered too many problems. While a lot of people don't like the car handling and prefer the bike handling, for me, it's the other way around even though, in general, I prefer to just fly a helicopter to get to where I want or need to go. The plane handling isn't too bad either but takes some getting used to.

Something I personally really enjoy is that there's no set way on how you approach anything in the game. Of course, the main idea is to be stealthy and there are penalties for killing civilians but as far as the progress goes, it's completely up to oneself where you go first and which missions you approach. Sure, to get to the end, you have to take a certain path in a way but you don't actually have to finish off all the people connected to the drug cartel and you're still able to finish the game even though, it may have an effect on the outcome.

What I also like is that you don't have a set difficulty once you've picked it but that you can change it whenever you want. So far, I haven't come across a mission that was too hard but I like that I can just make the game harder or easier whenever I feel like it without having to start all over again.

As for co-op, I haven't used the online mode yet to play with random people because I simply prefer to play with friends rather than strangers but I do like the on the fly matchmaking system though, which lets you easily join someone else's game without much waiting or lag or any of the sort.

Of course, the game can also be played alone in which the game grants you three AI characters but more often than not I wanted to strangle or shoot them just to get them out of the way because they've either given away my position or didn't follow my instructions at all. One of the reasons why I think this game is best played with friends.

Look at all those negative reviews!  What game are those people playing?  Frankly I don’t get the hate, and that is coming from a Ubisoft hater. 

So, lets talk turkey.  Is this a good game?

Frankly?  Yes! I am enjoying the heck out of it so far.  The game is JAM PACKED with things to explore, locations to raid and conquer, missions to complete, and a fairly compelling story of Drug lords, corruption, rebellion and American covert ops. 

This isn’t a perfect game by any means, but the gameplay, at least for me, has been addictive.  I am constantly playing longer than intended, always having a “just one more thing...” habit when I should be going to bed.   The gunplay, stealth, and action feel pretty good to me.  I prefer light real/sim tactical shooters to frag fest action shooters.  This is decidedly right smack dab in the middle, with a strong stealth element.  I run around like a Ninja in the night, sniping and assasinating bad guys methodically, getting deep into the enemy stronghold.  Here is where it usually goes south and I end up having to shoot my way out like Rambo (which makes it even more fun and white knuckle, especially on harder settings). 

The open world plays like a super watered down GTA, or like A slightly watered down Watchdogs.  Enemies do re spawn when you leave the area far enough, breaking immersion sometimes, but it’s very tolerable.

The difficulty settings scale up pretty well, with arcade being for kids and people who don’t like shooters.  With each harder difficulty making the enemies quicker and more aggressive.  They don’t become bullet sponges, instead they spot you better and start shooting before you can spot them.  The highest difficulty turns off all the radar elements unless you scan with your drone.  Meaning bad guys can sneak up on you now too!

One flaw I have to mention is that for whatever reason, they allow you to swap your loadouts at any point and time in the world.  In other words, they have all these ammo supply boxes in the game world, offering you the ability to swap loadouts.  So, most people, myself included, at first assume you can only select a loadout while at these boxes… So you spend some time meticulously planning your weapon selection to make sure you fit a concept (stealth sniper?  CQB specialist?).  Only to find that if you go into your loadout screen, you can swap your equipment at any time.  Replenishing ammo etc. 

This utterly robs the game of any sense of individual specialization in Co OP, or solo play (to a lesser degree in solo, because you have to make up for the limited AI controls, you can do well without an LMG for example, but sometimes you just have to have a sniper rifle. 

I wish the game had a setting (or if it does I wish I knew about it) to limit this somehow.  Especially in Co-op, where I feel it would go a long way.  

I also find being able to carry 2 long guns on your back at any time to be kind of silly.  In real life you don’t typically do that… This further dumbs down weapon selection, because you could easily pick a high power sniper, and a LMG and have no problems carrying both… Try that in RL, to say nothing of the ammo… 
 
Lastly, one flaw really irks me… But I managed to get over it just by swearing off buying any extras for this… It’s the Shady/greedy DLC and addon scheme, not quit battlefront 2 loot crate, but certainly not reasonable Free to play item store with reasonable pricing.  For example, the Predator pack of items and cosmetics costs around 30$.  For a handful of guns, a new melee animation and some cosmetics.  I suppose if you add it all up, it’s actually not THAT expensive… but only really IF this was a FREE TO PLAY GAME.  I mean, if I want to be honest, I’ve spent several times that in a Free to play game on cosmetics etc. But pay 60$ for a base game, another 30-40$ for season pass or all DLC, PLUS 15-30$ for extra packs like that?  Oh, hell no. 

Final verdict – Do I recommend it?  IF you like or don’t mind, the Ubisoft open world formula, and the lite tactical mil/sim style of Tom Clancy and ghost recon games… Hell yeah! If you got 2-3 friends willing to play with you… then make that a double hell yeah!

[h1]TL;DR: Somekind of a sweet experiment between The Division and Ghost Recon Future Soldier and add 'SOME' GTA elements for the free roam. It could also be interpreted as a FAR CRY third person shooter, minus the skinning the wildlife![/h1]

Wildlands, a game I actually beta tested before its launch. Back then, I totally couldn't enjoy the game as the helicopter controls were abysmally ATROCIOUS. Same goes for the driving of cars and jeeps. That was a deal breaker and I skipped purchase. And here comes the Black Friday Steam sales, I decided to take a leap of faith and give it a shot at reduced price. Oh damn the game got improved! Helicopter flying and cars driving got IMPROVED CONSIDERABLY!

[h1]What is Wildlands?[/h1]
[b]Team of 4 elite soldiers sent at Bolivia to take down the big Santa Blanca cartel that controls the country, even the Unidad military. The game follows you and three other A.I. partners (just like GR Future Soldier) and you go around the open world of Bolivia and free roam to your objectives. The country of Bolivia is divided by MANY ZONES called Provinces so if you want to explore all, you get your money's worth! You can only stick to the main missions but the exploration you do is rewarded with new weapons and weapon mods unlock, same goes with skill points and some notes scattered around everywhere to give you a deeper explaining of the backstory of Santa Blanca cartel.

So... yeah! I have enjoyed this game very much! I may have listed many cons down there and hopefully, Ubisoft could work on that for another GR game... IF it follows the same recipe of Wildlands that is![/b]


[h1]PROS:[/h1]
[b]+BEAUTIFUL VISUALLY! The world, characters, weather effects, 'some' wildlife... all looking amazing. Bolivia is divided into 20 Provinces who have each of their own ecosystem.
+Ultimate freedom in your free-roaming. You can decide to go ANYWHERE you want, even the most dangerous provinces right of the start. Not very recommended but can still be done with lots of patience and some planning!
+Gameplay is addictive AF! Stealthily or guns blazing, the gameplay is really fun.
+Decent music and voice acting.
+Drone usage is very handy for many different type of needs (EMP, Explosive, Medic, etc) and for spotting enemies.
+LOTS OF WEAPONS and attachments makes for endless customizations.
+PREDATOR MISSION DLC. The mission is VERY challenging. Predator sounds and orignal soundtrack. This is very well crafted by Ubisoft! I suggest you equip a good shotgun and assault rifle coupled with a grenade launcher. Took me around 10 tries to beat that ugly mothafu... The rewards aren't that great and the game requires you to pay money to unlock the real deal in the Predator pack.
+CO-OP (drop-in/out) mode adds more versality than those 3 poor AI partners you're stucked with! No restrictions if a friend comes to your game and that he haven't went to that zone or done a mission. All is saved from both solo and co-op!
+Unidad vehicles pack (from Ubisoft Store) helped me save a lot of time. The Unidad helicopter is very handy with its rockets and you can clear an enemy zone really fast.
+Perfect Ultrawide 21:9 support[/b]


[h1]CONS:[/h1]
[b]-A few gamebreaking bugs that required me to restart the game. Wildlands saves often so no big deal!
-I found the game world to be way too big. It could've been cut in half and been fine!
-VERY repetitive gameplay. If you dislike the first hour or two, refund asap!
-Poor mission variety. Always the same ones coming up!
-Constant swarms of enemies when an objective is triggered. And is actually worst in the Fallen Ghosts DLC.
-Weak Team A.I.. They don't help much and enemies always focus on you first, anyway. Only good at basic enemy spotting and the sync shot mechanism. Usage of rebels are for cannon fodder.
-Many good items are locked in the Ubisoft store paywall. Some can be unlocked in the normal gameplay but why not all? Not good UBI!
-Would be great that once you clear a zone (or Province) of enemies in Forts and Outposts, it STAYS CLEAR. Always tiresome to circle around and clear that damn SAM infested zone over and over again...
-Not as tactical as previous GR games where in this one, Wildlands is more of an improvision simulator!
-Average story with a clash of tones where pretty much all is predictable.
-Vehicles spawning mode when calling the rebels often spawn the car/copter very far and sometimes, clipping inside walls or grounds, making them unusable and making you wait until the cooldown is over to spawn again. This is nasty especially when you are in a battle and require help from something!
-CAN'T KILL CIVILIANS!!!! Sure this is not GTA but if you kill more than 3 civilians, you get a warning... the next dead fails your current mission. Annoying AF![/b]


[h1]OVERALL AND RECOMMENDATION:[/h1]
[b]ENTERTAINING MILITARY SHOOTER. Ghost Recon Wildlands is not the GR game you are accustomed to. It is a wild ride into a HUGE open-world setting with various zones that has each a different cartel boss to undermine (kill or capture). The gameplay is VERY addictive and carries you until you finish the game.

As an action game, I found it excellent to almost all of its facets. But as a Ghost Recon game, the so many differences of all this free roaming could annoy GR purists. All in all, great action game but average Ghost Recon title that may differ too much from known GR grounds.[/b]


[h1]GHOST WAR DLC:[/h1]
[b]Basically 4vs4 PVP! Not much a fan of PVP gameplay and especially with Third Person Shooters! This requires a separate purchase if you only have the vanila version.[/b]


[h1]NARCO ROADS DLC:[/h1]
[b]That DLC is like some poor experiment between GTA and Saints Row 3/4. It is mostly a joke of a new content and I strongly suggest you ignore it. Completely breaks the Ghost Recon setting![/b]


[h1]FALLEN GHOSTS:[/h1]
[b]The setting is semi-realistic as this DLC happens after Wildlands main campaign. Vision is VERY restricted 'cause of all that damn raining. Somehow, other mercs took over Bolivia and have cutting-edge tech to challenge you. Big gripe is the constant raining and constricted roaming (Only 3 provinces of Bolivia to roam) whereas in Wildlands, you have 20 provinces to roam; might be too huge but had various weather too. Main problem with this DLC is the constant spawn of enemies everywhere near you. Even when playing stealthily, enemies spawn everywhere in all sides! Since you can't rely too much on your team AI, you're pretty much screwed.

3 new Enemy types:
-"Fresh air" no helmet guy that can only be killed with headshots... and no typo here, multiple headshots are required for this spongy "Tom's Clancy THE DIVISION" type dude. He can eat rockets from that Unidad helicopter with no problems. Quite lame and gamebreaking.

-"Predator" type enemy that is mainly invisible to all visions except thermal. He uses somekind of a crossbow weapon that you unlock. Acts like a semi-sniper weapon and also can be used with an explosive arrow. Annoying enemy as the spotting and tagging won't work unless you go thermal vision.

-Last but not least, the guy with a jammer backpack. What happens? Once inside 100m of his range, your minimap shutdowns, can't use any vision modes and your drone can't function too. And all that was tagged earlier get's untagged.

Overall, I was getting to look forward to this DLC but the numerous annoyances breaks it to me. Having played and completed everything (except the leftover rebel side missions) in Wildlands, this Fallen Ghosts DLC just kept getting frustrating. Geting swarmed with countless enemies in all sides, snipers that can shoot through walls, helicopters and even armored vehicles, your A.I. partners seems even worst than the vanila game, areas are filled with SAMS, making using any flying copters worthless. 

I CAN'T RECOMMEND THIS DLC TO ALL but only for Ghost Recon purists that don't mind the cons mentionned here or gamers seeking a challenging gameplay.[/b]

The game certainly has it's detractors, mainly people saying 1. the story is lacking, 2. it's repetitive, or 3. the landscape is just meh. On the first point, I don't disagree; the story is almost a footnote. Just like they had to check the "Include Main Story Arc" box. It's really less of a story and more of a framework to provide some context and rationale to why you're where you are and why you're doing what you're doing. It gives the opportunity to run many "story" missions in parallel. There's so much other stuff to do tho, I'm not even bothered by it. On the second point, I mostly disagree. While you do end up doing some of the same stuff and/or the same types of missions (as you do in ALL open world games), the enviroment, location, time of day, weather, etc... all add to making the experience feel varied. The way you approach a loot raid, for example, will be different depending on whether it's day or night, whether it's a huge enemy base or a small squad outpost, or whether you want to be stealthy or go guns blazing like Rambo. On the thrid point, I absolutely disagree. I don't know how anyone can even say the landscape is 'meh' with a straight face. It's effin incredible. Massive jungles, sizable towns (and TONS of them) and the ability to travel around the map and see it all in numerous ways was great. Planes, helicopters, dirtbikes, SUVs, Ferraris, bulldozers, whatever! Flying a plane or helicopter is so enjoyable I find myself spending up to 30 min capturing one just to be able to fly over the [huge] map just because it's so beautiful. Oh and you can parachute right out of it when you get to your destination. That brings up anonter point. The map is HUGE. I can't think of a game I've played that has a larger one. And it's all so meticulously detailed.

[h1] I really wanted to like this game, but it's not making it easy.	[/h1]

Let me start by saying that, for me, with the specific problems that I am having, I [b] cannot recommend [/b] this product.

My main gripe is the performance. I am running a computer that can easily handle this game on the highest settings, yet it [b] frequently [/b] has painful graphical lag - either because it attempts to load in new chunks of map, textures, or autosaves (though, I think I've found the problem with autosaving.)

[u] Occasionally during my play [/u], especially when traveling quickly, the game will hang up in a semi-buffering state where limited camera controls exist and menu access is possible. This issue is mitigated slightly when traveling by foot, but with the size of the map, that's a rather cumbersome proposition.

[u] Frequent, to the point of surprise when it does work right, [/u] is the spawn system. I get it, it's a big game and if every npc or sprite were spawned and rendered all the time, it would bog down even the most competent system. The system employed in Wildlands, however, is unable to keep up with a regular player playing rather slowly. Oftentimes while playing in an area that should be crawling with baddies, I find that the area is unpopulated and things such as weapon drops and intel that are essential to character growth and story development are not yet rendered, even though their markers are displayed on the HUD. The only work-around I have found for this is to stop, enter the map, and give the game some time to load. The problem with this is that it eliminates most of the fun of infiltrating an area, whereas normally you'd have to either sneak through enemy lines and make decisions on what enemies to eliminate in order to progress stealthily, or burn through a ship's weight in lead to achieve the mission. In this situation, you might find yourself alone one minute, and then surrounded by enemies, and having your tactical decisions made for you.

I cannot comment on the storyline, as I haven't really been able to get very far in it. While it seems fairly compelling, the variety of missions and interactions seems limited and uninspired in scope. If you enjoy repeating the same scenarios over and over in slightly different ways, then you might enjoy this game - that is, if you can forgive the glaring and painful issues with performance.
